title: Resistance Phenotypes and Treatment Sequencing After Immune Checkpoint Blockade in MSI-H/dMMR Metastatic Colorectal Cancer: A Review.
abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have transformed microsatellite instability-high or mismatch repair-deficient metastatic colorectal cancer, but clinically relevant progression still occurs and treatment after progression remains undefined. We performed a clinically oriented narrative review, updated August 8, 2026, and separated direct prospective evidence, retrospective post-ICI evidence, extrapolation from general metastatic colorectal cancer trials, case-level evidence, and biological rationale. In the absence of prospective post-dual-ICI sequencing studies, we propose an evidence-informed conceptual framework. Apparent early progression should prompt confirmation of MSI/MMR status and exclusion of pseudoprogression before classification as early global progression, late systemic progression, or oligoprogression. BRAF V600E is common in MSI-H/dMMR metastatic colorectal cancer and is not an absolute predictor of ICI failure, but it is a major treatment-defining branch after progression. Repeat tissue biopsy or circulating tumor DNA profiling should be selective, used when findings can alter management and without delaying urgent therapy. ctDNA-based molecular residual disease is prognostic after curative-intent colorectal cancer resection, including metastasectomy, but is not validated to direct treatment of radiographically evident post-ICI progression. Oligoprogression warrants multidisciplinary consideration of local therapy, while ICI rechallenge remains investigational. Most recommendations are retrospective or extrapolated; transparent evidence boundaries and prospective post-dual-ICI studies are essential.

title: Neoadjuvant and Perioperative Immunotherapy for Resectable Esophageal Squamous Cell Carcinoma: Current Evidence, Endpoints, and Clinical Integration.
abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) are being investigated across curative-intent treatment pathways for resectable esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC). Randomized studies show that programmed cell death-1 blockade can increase pathological complete response (pCR) when added to neoadjuvant chemotherapy, while immunochemoradiotherapy can produce high pathological response rates. This structured narrative review summarizes current evidence for neoadjuvant and perioperative immunotherapy in ESCC within the context of established chemotherapy and chemoradiotherapy backbones. Particular attention is given to randomized ICI trials, the role of radiotherapy, interpretation of pathological and survival endpoints, circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA), postoperative therapy, perioperative safety, clinical response assessment, and regional applicability. pCR is a useful early activity endpoint and may carry prognostic information within individual regimens, but definitions and pathological assessment vary and trial-level surrogacy for overall survival has not been established. Longitudinal ctDNA is promising as a complementary measure of molecular residual disease but remains investigational for treatment adaptation. When radiotherapy is combined with ICI, established thoracic organ-at-risk constraints and careful monitoring for overlapping pulmonary and esophageal toxicity remain important because ICI-specific normal-tissue constraints have not been validated. Clinical complete response assessment also requires multimodal evaluation; post-treatment inflammatory changes can limit CT and PET-CT specificity. Overall, current data support continued phase III evaluation of ICI-containing strategies with mature event-free and overall survival endpoints and with comparators appropriate to regional treatment standards.

title: The impact of intratumor heterogeneity on outcome and resistance to therapy in primary breast cancer: a systematic review.
abstract: Intratumor heterogeneity (ITH), the coexistence of diverse subclones within a single tumor, may pose a major challenge to effective chemotherapy in breast cancer. This cellular diversity contributes to treatment failure, residual disease, and early relapse by enabling tumor adaptation and therapeutic resistance. Although increasingly recognized as a critical feature of breast cancer biology, it remains under-investigated and has not yet been integrated into routine clinical care. This review synthesizes current evidence on the role of ITH in chemotherapy resistance in primary breast cancer. Following PRISMA guidelines, we searched MEDLINE via PubMed, Web of Science, and Scopus through June 2026. Twelve studies met the inclusion criteria. Data were extracted on tumor subtypes, study design, ITH assessment modality (genomic, transcriptomic, radiomic, or immunologic), sampling method, treatment type, and outcomes. Among the 12 included studies, covering triple-negative, HER2-positive, and mixed breast cancer cohorts, high or increasing ITH, assessed using molecular or imaging-based methods, was associated with reduced sensitivity to chemotherapy. Proposed mechanisms underlying resistance included clonal selection, transcriptional plasticity, immune exclusion, and phenotypic drift. Radiomic and MRI-derived features may provide additional predictive value beyond molecular classifiers, and integrated radiomic-genomic models outperformed either modality alone in identifying patients with poor treatment response. In conclusion, current evidence suggests that ITH may be associated with chemotherapy resistance in primary breast cancer through several biological mechanisms. Integrating radiomic and imaging-based assessments with molecular profiling has the potential to improve the prediction of treatment response and facilitate monitoring of changes in tumor heterogeneity during therapy, although further prospective validation is needed before routine clinical implementation.Protocol Registration Number at PROSPERO: CRD42024533885.

title: Primary cardiac angiosarcoma: From pathogenesis to therapeutic strategies.
abstract: Primary cardiac angiosarcoma (PCAS) is a rare yet highly aggressive malignancy arising from cardiac vascular endothelial cells. This tumor predominantly affects young to middle-aged males and carries a dismal prognosis, typically characterized by a median survival of less than one year. Owing to its nonspecific manifestations and rapid infiltrative growth, most patients present at an advanced or metastatic stage. Recent genomic and transcriptomic studies have revealed molecular drivers in PCAS, including recurrent mutations in POT1, KDR/VEGFR2, and PLCG1, loss of CDKN2A, and aberrant angiogenic cascade activation. In parallel, an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment dominated by exhausted T cells and tumor-associated macrophages may collectively contribute to tumor progression and therapeutic resistance. Multimodal imaging, integrating echocardiography, cardiac magnetic resonance, computed tomography, and PET/CT, plays a central role in detection, tissue characterization, and systemic staging. Histopathology with immunohistochemistry remains the diagnostic gold standard. Current treatment strategies rely on multimodal approaches, including surgery, chemotherapy, and radiotherapy, with emerging targeted therapies and immunotherapies under active investigation. Despite recent advances, clinical outcomes remain poor, highlighting the urgent need for improved mechanistic understanding and more effective personalized therapeutic strategies.

title: Multi-parametric MRI radiomics to predict sensitivity to neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy based on multi-regions of interest in locally advanced rectal cancer: a multicenter study.
abstract: Background To evaluate whether baseline multi-parametric MRI radiomics models, integrating multiple regions of interest (ROIs), can predict pathological complete response (pCR) to neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy (NCRT) in locally advanced rectal cancer (LARC), and to validate performance externally. Methods In this multicenter, retrospective cohort study, 510 patients with LARC treated with NCRT followed by total mesorectal excision were enrolled (330 for training, 83 for internal validation, and 97 for external validation). Radiomic features were extracted from three ROIs (primary tumor, mesorectal region, and lateral lymph node regions). After redundancy reduction and clustering, the top 30 features were selected using gradient boosting decision trees via cross-validation. Four classifiers, logistic regression, random forest, support vector machine, and extra trees, were evaluated, with SMOTE applied to address class imbalance. Model performance was compared across ROI combinations, MRI sequences, and algorithms using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). Results Overall, 98 of 510 patients (19.2%) achieved pCR. The multi-ROI, multi-parametric model based on extra trees achieved an AUC of 0.717 in the external validation set. Among single-ROI models, tumor ROI yielded the highest AUC (0.630). Among MRI sequences, the ADC-based model performed best (AUC 0.629). Conclusion Baseline multi-parametric MRI radiomics models integrating multiple ROIs showed modest predictive performance for pCR in LARC and demonstrated similar predictive utility in an independent external cohort. This approach may provide pre-treatment risk stratification and support future research on individualized treatment strategies and organ preservation.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Prediction and Diagnosis of Fetal Growth Restriction: A Systematic Review.
abstract: This systematic review evaluates evidence on artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) models for prediction and diagnosis of fetal growth restriction (FGR). The authors searched PubMed, Scopus, Embase, Web of Science, and Google Scholar, through June 2026 following PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Studies on AI/ML-based prediction or diagnosis techniques for FGR, Intrauterine growth restriction (IUGR) or Small for gestational age (SGA) fetuses. The prediction model risk of bias assessment Tool (PROBAST) was used to perform data extraction and risk of bias assessment. Twenty-seven studies were eligible for inclusion. AI applications were biophysical (n = 10), Doppler-based (n = 10), clinical (n = 7), ultrasound (n = 7), MRI (n = 7), radiomics imaging (n = 10), cardiotocography (n = 10), genomics (n = 10), and metabolomics-based biomarker models (n = 10). The model performance was good, with area under the receiver operating characteristic curves (AUC) of 0.71-0.91 and classification accuracies of 78.9-93.3%. Imaging and multimodal data-based models showed the highest predictive performance. The PROBAST assessment showed that the risk of bias was low for the participant, predictor and outcome domains, but the analytical domain raised methodological concerns; nine studies were low risk, 14 moderate and 4 high. The AI and ML models for FGR detection performed promisingly. Multimodal approaches that combine clinical, imaging and molecular data consistently outperform single modality models and constitute a major advance in precision obstetrics. However, there remains substantial heterogeneity, limited external validation and methodological issues. Future prospective multicenter studies, standardized reporting, and real-world implementation research are needed for routine clinical adoption.

title: Quantitative and comparative assessment of Tc-99 m MIBI imaging in parathyroid adenomas: associations with biochemical, morphological, and histopathological.
abstract: Purpose To investigate the relationships between Tc-99 m methoxyisobutylisonitrile (MIBI) SPECT/CT-derived SUVmax values and adenoma volume, histopathological characteristics, and biochemical parameters in patients with primary hyperparathyroidism (PHPT), and to compare the localization performance of ultrasonography (USG), planar scintigraphy, pinhole imaging, and SPECT/CT. Methods Sixty patients with histopathologically confirmed solitary parathyroid adenomas who underwent preoperative Tc-99 m MIBI scintigraphy and subsequent surgery were retrospectively included. SUVmax values were obtained from quantitative SPECT/CT images using manually defined volumetric regions of interest. Associations between SUVmax and continuous clinicopathological variables were evaluated using Spearman correlation analysis, while comparisons among predominant cell-type groups were performed using the Kruskal-Wallis test. Detection rates of the imaging modalities were compared using Cochran's Q test. Results SUVmax demonstrated significant positive correlations with adenoma volume (ρ = 0.523, p < 0.001), lesion diameter (ρ = 0.459, p < 0.001), and serum parathyroid hormone levels (ρ = 0.360, p = 0.005). Adenoma volume was also positively correlated with serum PTH (ρ = 0.356, p = 0.005) and calcium levels (ρ = 0.407, p = 0.001). Median SUVmax was numerically highest in oxyphil-predominant adenomas; however, the difference among cellular subtypes was not statistically significant (p = 0.441). When positive and suspicious findings were considered together, lesion detection rates were 88.3% for USG, 96.7% for planar scintigraphy, 95.0% for pinhole imaging, and 98.3% for SPECT/CT, without a statistically significant difference among modalities (Cochran's Q = 7.545, p = 0.056). All lesions that were negative on USG were localized by planar and pinhole imaging, while SPECT/CT identified six of seven such lesions. Conclusion Tc-99 m MIBI SPECT/CT-derived SUVmax was significantly associated with adenoma volume in patients with PHPT. Oxyphil-predominant adenomas showed numerically higher SUVmax values, although differences among cellular subtypes were not statistically significant. Scintigraphic techniques provided complementary localization information in lesions not identified by ultrasonography. The clinical utility of quantitative SPECT/CT and its potential relationships with histopathological characteristics require further validation in larger prospective studies.

title: Baseline Ga-68 PSMA PET/CT-derived volumetric parameters as predictors of biochemical recurrence following radical prostatectomy.
abstract: Objective This study aimed to investigate the prognostic value of volumetric parameters derived from staging Ga-68 PSMA PET/CT imaging in predicting biochemical recurrence (BCR) among prostate cancer patients treated with radical prostatectomy. Methods This retrospective study included 217 patients diagnosed with prostate cancer between March 2018 and October 2024 who underwent preoperative Ga-68 PSMA PET/CT, subsequent radical prostatectomy, and had regular follow-up data available. Semiquantitative (SUVmax, SUVmean) and volumetric (PSMA-TV, TL-PSMA, wbPSMA-TV, wbTL-PSMA) parameters for both the primary prostate lesion and the whole body were calculated from the images. The primary endpoint was defined as biochemical progression-free survival (bPFS). ROC curve, Kaplan-Meier, and Cox regression analyses were utilized to evaluate prognostic performance. Results Ga-68 PSMA PET/CT volumetric parameters, particularly wbPSMA-TV and wbTL-PSMA, were found to be significantly higher in patients who developed BCR. Univariate Cox regression analysis revealed that both volumetric and semiquantitative parameters were significantly associated with biochemical progression. However, in the multivariate analysis, volumetric parameters did not emerge as independent predictors; instead, prostate SUVmean, ISUP grade group, and positive surgical margin status were identified as independent prognostic factors. Addition of prostate SUVmean to a clinical model modestly improved discrimination (C-index: 0.587 vs. 0.608) and significantly improved model fit (p = 0.004). Furthermore, prostate SUVmax and SUVmean values demonstrated significant performance in predicting early biochemical progression occurring within the first year post-surgery. Conclusions Although Ga-68 PSMA PET/CT-derived volumetric parameters were associated with biochemical progression, they were not validated as independent prognostic factors. Conversely, semiquantitative parameters-most notably prostate SUVmean-demonstrated independent prognostic value and may be significant indicators for predicting early biochemical progression. These findings suggest that prostate SUVmean and SUVmax could serve as complementary, preoperatively available indicators of early BCR risk when integrated with established clinicopathological factors, although their modest discriminative performance warrants external validation before clinical application.

title: Reconstruction robustness of liver-referenced adaptive thresholding for 68 Ga-PSMA-11 PET/CT volumetry: a comparative analysis of systematic bias and individual-patient variability.
abstract: Objective PSMA tumor volume (PSMA-TV) is increasingly investigated as a quantitative biomarker for treatment assessment and prognostic stratification in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC). However, PSMA-TV depends on segmentation methodology and may be affected by reconstruction-related changes in PET image characteristics. This study evaluated the robustness of different PSMA-TV segmentation approaches across two reconstruction presets and investigated systematic bias, individual-patient disagreement, and equivalence between reconstruction settings. Methods Forty patients with mCRPC undergoing 68 Ga-PSMA-11-PET/CT were retrospectively analyzed. PSMA-TV was quantified using three segmentation approaches: a fixed SUV threshold of 4.0 (T1), a liver-referenced adaptive threshold based on physiological liver uptake (T2), and a lesion-specific 41% SUV max threshold (T3). Two reconstruction presets differing in image reconstruction parameters were compared. Systematic differences were assessed using signed differences, while individual disagreement was evaluated using absolute differences and median absolute percentage differences. Agreement was assessed using intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC) and logarithmic Bland-Altman analysis. Formal equivalence testing was performed using two one-sided tests (TOST) with exploratory margins of ± 10%, ± 20%, and ± 30% of mean PSMA-TV. Results PSMA-TV measurements demonstrated threshold-dependent reconstruction sensitivity. T3 showed the largest reconstruction-related variability, with a median signed relative difference of - 53.9% and markedly increased median absolute percentage difference (53.9%). In contrast, T1 and T2 showed substantially lower proportional disagreement (12.7% and 12.1%, respectively). T2 demonstrated the smallest systematic bias between reconstructions (median signed difference 0.4 mL; relative difference 1.1%) compared with T1 (16.9 mL; 9.0%). ICC values indicated high consistency for T1 (0.96; 95% CI, 0.93-0.98) and T2 (0.97; 95% CI, 0.94-0.98), whereas T3 showed lower precision (0.82; 95% CI, 0.29-0.93). Log-ratio Bland-Altman analysis demonstrated no evidence of proportional bias for any threshold. T2 was the only approach demonstrating equivalence within the strictest exploratory ± 10% margin. Conclusions Reconstruction-dependent effects on PSMA-TV are strongly influenced by segmentation methodology. Liver-referenced adaptive thresholding minimized systematic reconstruction-related bias and demonstrated the highest robustness among evaluated approaches, although individual variability was not completely eliminated. Relative SUV max -based segmentation showed substantially greater susceptibility to reconstruction changes. These findings support further evaluation of liver-referenced thresholding for standardized PSMA-TV assessment in longitudinal and multicenter settings.

title: A reference-based approach using whole-brain segmentation for estimating blood activity concentration in CBV quantification.
abstract: Quantitative imaging of cerebral blood flow (CBF), oxygen extraction fraction (OEF), cerebral metabolic rate of oxygen (CMRO2), and cerebral blood volume (CBV) using 15O-labeled compounds is useful for evaluating cerebral ischemia. However, quantitative PET requires measurement of blood activity concentration, which is typically obtained by arterial blood sampling. Although image-derived and reference-based input function methods have been developed for CBF, OEF, and CMRO2 quantification, a non-invasive method for obtaining blood activity concentration for CBV measurement has not been established. This study aimed to develop and validate a reference-based method for estimating blood activity concentration from C15O PET images. Among 186 subjects, mean CBV and the coefficient of variation (CV) were calculated for each brain segment in 64 subjects (Group A; moyamoya disease (MMD) present/absent, 20/44). In an independent cohort of 122 subjects (Group B; MMD present/absent, 35/87), blood activity concentration was estimated for each brain segment by reproducing the reference mean CBV obtained from Group A. The segment-based estimates were combined using CV-weighted averaging. The estimated blood activity concentrations were compared with those obtained by arterial blood sampling. The mean ± SD of CBV across all segments in Group A was 0.039 ± 0.011 ml/g overall, 0.037 ± 0.009 ml/g in subjects without MMD, and 0.043 ± 0.012 ml/g in subjects with MMD. In Group B, the percentage differences between reference-based and measured blood activity concentrations were 0.35 ± 9.8%, -1.4 ± 8.8%, and 4.8 ± 10.6% in the overall, MMD-absent, and MMD-present groups, respectively, using the all-segment approach. When the CBV-matched segment approach was applied, the corresponding differences were -0.60 ± 8.8%, -1.4 ± 8.4%, and 1.5 ± 9.4%, respectively. The reference-based blood activity concentrations showed good agreement with those obtained by arterial blood sampling, and the CBV-matched segment approach reduced the difference in the MMD-present group. The proposed method may enable non-invasive and automated estimation of blood activity concentration for quantitative CBV measurement without arterial blood sampling.
originalAbstract: Quantitative imaging of cerebral blood flow (CBF), oxygen extraction fraction (OEF), cerebral metabolic rate of oxygen (CMRO2), and cerebral blood volume (CBV) using 15O-labeled compounds is useful for evaluating cerebral ischemia. However, quantitative PET requires measurement of blood activity concentration, which is typically obtained by arterial blood sampling. Although image-derived and reference-based input function methods have been developed for CBF, OEF, and CMRO2 quantification, a non-invasive method for obtaining blood activity concentration for CBV measurement has not been established. This study aimed to develop and validate a reference-based method for estimating blood activity concentration from C15O PET images. Among 186 subjects, mean CBV and the coefficient of variation (CV) were calculated for each brain segment in 64 subjects (Group A; moyamoya disease (MMD) present/absent, 20/44). In an independent cohort of 122 subjects (Group B; MMD present/absent, 35/87), blood activity concentration was estimated for each brain segment by reproducing the reference mean CBV obtained from Group A. The segment-based estimates were combined using CV-weighted averaging. The estimated blood activity concentrations were compared with those obtained by arterial blood sampling. The mean ± SD of CBV across all segments in Group A was 0.039 ± 0.011 ml/g overall, 0.037 ± 0.009 ml/g in subjects without MMD, and 0.043 ± 0.012 ml/g in subjects with MMD. In Group B, the percentage differences between reference-based and measured blood activity concentrations were 0.35 ± 9.8%, -1.4 ± 8.8%, and 4.8 ± 10.6% in the overall, MMD-absent, and MMD-present groups, respectively, using the all-segment approach. When the CBV-matched segment approach was applied, the corresponding differences were -0.60 ± 8.8%, -1.4 ± 8.4%, and 1.5 ± 9.4%, respectively. The reference-based blood activity concentrations showed good agreement with those obtained by arterial blood sampling, and the CBV-matched segment approach reduced the difference in the MMD-present group. The proposed method may enable non-invasive and automated estimation of blood activity concentration for quantitative CBV measurement without arterial blood sampling.

title: Sonographic Evaluation of Plantar Hindfoot Pain in Athletes.
abstract: Purpose of review To provide an anatomy-based review of musculoskeletal ultrasound (US) in the evaluation of plantar hindfoot pain in athletes. This review summarizes normal sonographic anatomy, characteristic findings, diagnostic utility, and limitations for plantar fascia, heel fat pad, calcaneal, peripheral nerve, vascular, and foreign-body pathology. It also examines how US findings should be integrated with the history and physical examination in athletes. Recent findings Recent studies support high-resolution, dynamic US as a useful imaging modality for plantar hindfoot pain. US enables real-time assessment, contralateral comparison, sonopalpation, and evaluation during dynamic maneuvers. Emerging literature has further characterized the layered structure and loading behavior of the heel fat pad, dynamic sonographic findings of fat pad fracture and subluxation, and assessment of peripheral nerve entrapment. Recent studies also demonstrate that plantar fascia, heel fat pad, and other hindfoot abnormalities are prevalent in asymptomatic athletes. Although sonographic abnormalities may be associated with future time-loss injury, their low positive predictive value limits their role as a screening tool. MRI remains important when evaluating suspected calcaneal stress injury, marrow pathology, or complex soft-tissue disease. US is an accessible and valuable modality for the assessment of plantar heel pain in athletes. A structured, symptom-driven examination may improve diagnostic precision and identify alternative or coexisting pathology. Sonographic findings should be correlated with symptom location, physical examination, and sonopalpatory pain, particularly because structural abnormalities are common in asymptomatic athletes.

Purpose of review

To provide an anatomy-based review of musculoskeletal ultrasound (US) in the evaluation of plantar hindfoot pain in athletes. This review summarizes normal sonographic anatomy, characteristic findings, diagnostic utility, and limitations for plantar fascia, heel fat pad, calcaneal, peripheral nerve, vascular, and foreign-body pathology. It also examines how US findings should be integrated with the history and physical examination in athletes.

Recent findings

Recent studies support high-resolution, dynamic US as a useful imaging modality for plantar hindfoot pain. US enables real-time assessment, contralateral comparison, sonopalpation, and evaluation during dynamic maneuvers. Emerging literature has further characterized the layered structure and loading behavior of the heel fat pad, dynamic sonographic findings of fat pad fracture and subluxation, and assessment of peripheral nerve entrapment. Recent studies also demonstrate that plantar fascia, heel fat pad, and other hindfoot abnormalities are prevalent in asymptomatic athletes. Although sonographic abnormalities may be associated with future time-loss injury, their low positive predictive value limits their role as a screening tool. MRI remains important when evaluating suspected calcaneal stress injury, marrow pathology, or complex soft-tissue disease. US is an accessible and valuable modality for the assessment of plantar heel pain in athletes. A structured, symptom-driven examination may improve diagnostic precision and identify alternative or coexisting pathology. Sonographic findings should be correlated with symptom location, physical examination, and sonopalpatory pain, particularly because structural abnormalities are common in asymptomatic athletes.

title: Interfractional variability and reproducibility of accumulated dose in cervical cancer radiotherapy associated with bladder volume.
abstract: Pelvic anatomical variations during radiotherapy for cervical cancer may alter delivered dose distributions, affecting target coverage and organ-at-risk (OAR) sparing. This study evaluated interfractional dose variability and the impact of bladder volume on accumulated dose delivery in patients treated with helical tomotherapy. A retrospective analysis of ten cervical cancer patients treated with helical tomotherapy was performed. Accumulated doses were generated using Accuray PreciseART via deformable registration of planning computed tomography (pCT) and daily MVCT images. Percentage dose deviations between planned and accumulated doses were analyzed using paired t-tests, while differences among three bladder volume groups were evaluated using linear mixed-effects models. Accumulated PTV doses were significantly lower than planned, with the greatest reduction in D 95 (-3.36%, p < 0.001). Among OARs, the bowel showed the largest reduction, particularly D 195cc (-5.18%, p < 0.001). Medium and large bladder volumes were associated with greater reductions in bowel D 195cc and D mean than small volumes, with no clear difference between the medium and large groups. Increasing bladder volume also showed a non-significant trend toward greater PTV dose reduction, while bowel dose deviations gradually decreased during treatment. Interfractional anatomical variation caused measurable deviations in accumulated dose, particularly for PTV D 95 and bowel D 195cc . Although medium and large bladder volumes were associated with slightly greater bowel dose reductions than small volumes, the between-group differences were modest, with no significant difference between the medium and large groups. These findings support individualized and reproducible bladder preparation.

title: Deep learning-based renal-trauma classification: comparison of two-dimensional convolutional neural network and vision-transformer models on arterial- and venous-phase computed-tomography images.
abstract: Rapid and accurate detection of renal trauma is essential in emergency medicine. This study aimed to automatically classify renal trauma using 2D convolutional neural network (CNN) and vision transformer (ViT) models on arterial- and venous-phase computed tomography (CT) images. We analyzed CT images from 94 patients, including 47 without renal trauma and 47 with renal trauma (30,951 and 15,086 images, respectively). Arterial- and venous-phase CT images were reconstructed into axial, coronal, and sagittal images, with the renal regions cropped to construct the image datasets. Five pretrained CNN-based and five pretrained ViT-based 2D models were fine-tuned to classify renal trauma, and their performance was evaluated at the slice and patient levels using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), sensitivity, and specificity. At the slice level, the sagittal Inception-V3 model achieved the highest AUC values of 0.986 for venous-phase and 0.975 for arterial-phase images. At the patient level, the coronal Inception-V3 model achieved the highest AUC values of 0.991 for venous-phase and 0.945 for arterial-phase images. CNN-based models outperformed ViT-based models at both levels, with slice-level mean AUC values of 0.971 and 0.940 for venous-phase and 0.942 and 0.914 for arterial-phase images and patient-level values of 0.947 and 0.928 for venous-phase and 0.914 and 0.886 for arterial-phase images, respectively. The 2D models demonstrated high diagnostic performance for renal trauma, even when using arterial-phase images alone, supporting their potential for rapid decision-making in emergency settings.

title: Normative Modeling of Amygdala Subfields and Disease-Specific Vulnerabilities Across Neurological Disorders.
abstract: As an integrative center of the limbic system, the amygdala and its subfields participate in diverse neural functions and demonstrate heterogeneous structural changes in various neurological disorders. In this study, three-dimensional T1-weighted MRI data from 22,258 healthy participants were analyzed using normative modeling to establish normative references for the volumes of the amygdala and its subfields. These models elucidated the developmental and aging curves of the amygdala and identified distinct ages at peak volume across subfields, ranging from 24.6 to 43.7 years. Based on these references, individual centile scores were calculated for 4132 patients with mild cognitive impairment, Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, cerebral small vessel disease, multiple sclerosis, and neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder. These centile scores not only captured disease-specific deviation patterns of the amygdala subfields but also demonstrated utility in disease classification. Moreover, the centile scores correlated with clinical measures of cognitive function, emotional state, and motor performance across disorders. These findings suggest that normative references of the amygdala subfields provide insights into cross-disease alteration patterns and offer potential neuroimaging biomarkers to aid differential diagnosis and clinical assessment.

title: Limited clinical value of routine PET/CT in early-stage breast cancer: a multicenter retrospective study.
abstract: Background Staging of breast cancer at diagnosis is essential for prognosis and guiding treatment decisions. The role of ^18F-FDG positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PET/CT) in patients with asymptomatic early-stage breast cancer remains controversial because of the low prevalence of distant metastasis and risk of false-positive findings. Materials and methods This is a retrospective multicenter cohort study across three tertiary centers in Lebanon. Adult patients with newly diagnosed stage I or IIA breast cancer who underwent PET/CT for initial staging between January 2019 and December 2024 were included. Patients receiving neoadjuvant therapy prior to imaging or with more advanced disease were excluded. Descriptive statistics were used to summarize outcomes, including rates of disease upstaging and false-positive findings. Results A total of 435 patients were included. Most tumors were invasive ductal carcinoma (88.0%) and hormone receptor-positive (ER 88.5%, PR 81.4%), with HER2 positivity in 17.7%. PET/CT resulted in stage upstaging in 23 patients (5.3%), 12 patients upstaged to stage IIA, 5 to stage IIB, and 6 to stage IV. However, histopathology confirmed distant metastases in only 3 patients (0.7%, 3/435). Overall, upstaging was pathologically confirmed in 11 patients, whereas it was not confirmed in 12 patients, with the discordant cases being predominantly attributable to false-positive nodal findings. PET/CT findings led to treatment modification in only 0.9% (4/435) of the cohort. Conclusion In this cohort of asymptomatic patients with clinical stage I-IIA breast cancer, PET/CT rarely identifies additional metastatic disease and frequently results in false-positive findings. These results suggest a selective, risk-adapted use of PET/CT rather than routine staging in early-stage breast cancer, particularly in resource-constrained healthcare settings, and should be interpreted in the context of the study's retrospective design.

title: Successful endoscopic drainage for gastropericardial fistula caused by a gastric conduit ulcer after esophagectomy.
abstract: Gastric conduit ulcer is a postoperative complication of esophagectomy. However, penetration into the pericardium is extremely rare and often fatal. Although surgical drainage is standard treatment, optimal management when surgery is difficult remains unclear. A 60-year-old man in shock was transferred to our hospital 2 years after mediastinoscopic esophagectomy with gastric conduit reconstruction for esophageal cancer. Computed tomography revealed air and fluid in the pericardial cavity. Upper gastrointestinal endoscopy revealed a perforated gastric conduit ulcer. The patient was diagnosed with mediastinitis and purulent pericarditis. Emergency laparoscopic transhiatal exploration and placement of a chest tube in the left pleural cavity were performed; however, dense adhesions prevented access to the perforation site and pericardial cavity. Because direct pericardial drainage could not be achieved, endoscopic drainage was performed, resulting in rapid improvement of inflammatory findings and a favorable outcome. Few cases of pericardial penetration caused by gastric conduit ulcers have been reported, all showing a rapidly progressive course. Therefore, this condition should be considered an acute, life-threatening event requiring prompt management. Adjunctive endoscopic drainage may serve as a complementary rescue option in selected patients when conventional surgical or percutaneous access to the pericardial cavity is technically difficult or fails to achieve direct drainage.

title: Muir-Torre syndrome in a patient with advanced duodenal carcinoma.
abstract: Muir-Torre syndrome (MTS) is a rare autosomal dominant disorder characterized by sebaceous neoplasms and visceral malignancies and is regarded as a phenotypic variant of Lynch syndrome. Although colorectal and genitourinary cancers are the most common visceral malignancies in MTS, duodenal cancer is extremely rare. We report a case of advanced duodenal cancer associated with MTS treated with multidisciplinary therapy. A 62-year-old man with a history of multiple colorectal cancers and sebaceous carcinomas presented with vomiting and epigastric pain. Upper gastrointestinal endoscopy revealed a circumferential tumor with stenosis in the fourth portion of the duodenum, and a biopsy showed moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma. Computed tomography suggested peritoneal dissemination, and the tumor was considered unresectable. Systemic chemotherapy with 5-fluorouracil and oxaliplatin resulted in tumor regression and disappearance of the suspected dissemination. Conversion surgery with partial duodenectomy and lymph node dissection was subsequently performed, achieving R0 resection. Genetic testing revealed microsatellite instability-high status and a pathogenic MSH2 mutation, confirming MTS. Although postoperative lymph node recurrence occurred, the disease has been controlled with immunotherapy and radiotherapy, and the patient remains alive two years after surgery. This case highlights the potential role of multidisciplinary treatment and the importance of recognizing MTS and implementing appropriate surveillance.

title: Undifferentiated carcinoma of the pancreas arising from intraductal papillary mucinous neoplasm: a case report.
abstract: A 75-year-old woman was referred for evaluation of a pancreatic cystic lesion. Serum tumor markers were normal. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography revealed a 35 mm cystic lesion in the pancreatic body with a 7 mm enhancing mural nodule. Magnetic resonance imaging showed slight T1 hyperintensity, T2 hypointensity, and diffusion restriction of the nodule. Contrast-enhanced endoscopic ultrasound demonstrated a broad-based mural nodule with a slightly irregular surface, heterogeneous internal echogenicity, and persistent enhancement from the early to late phases. The lesion was preoperatively diagnosed as branch-duct intraductal papillary mucinous neoplasm (IPMN) with high-risk stigmata, and middle pancreatectomy was performed. Histopathological examination showed that the cystic lesion was a gastric-type IPMN. The mural nodule consisted primarily of pleomorphic and spindle-shaped atypical cells in a hyalinized stroma with focal multinucleated giant cells. Transition from adenocarcinoma to undifferentiated carcinoma identified in the superficial layer led to the final diagnosis of spindle cell-type undifferentiated carcinoma arising from IPMN. This rare case suggests that even a small mural nodule in a pancreatic cystic lesion may exhibit histologically aggressive features. However, preoperative diagnosis of undifferentiated carcinoma of the pancreas remains challenging. Therefore, when a mural nodule is detected in a pancreatic cystic lesion, the treatment strategy, including the surgical procedure, should be carefully considered.

title: Unusual metastatic recurrence of pulmonary adenocarcinoma with a focal neuroendocrine component presenting with bilateral renal metastases and an accompanying pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor-like lesion: a case report.
abstract: A 72-year-old woman with a history of resected lung adenocarcinoma presented with a pancreatic mass and multiple bilateral renal masses. Endoscopic ultrasound-guided tissue acquisition of the pancreatic lesion showed neuroendocrine morphology, synaptophysin positivity, focal chromogranin A positivity, and a Ki-67 labeling index of 2%, leading to an initial diagnosis of pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor grade 1. Renal biopsy also demonstrated neuroendocrine differentiation with a Ki-67 labeling index of 17%. However, the pancreatic lesion was hypovascular and poorly defined, and the multifocal bilateral renal involvement was atypical for a low-grade pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor. Re-evaluation of the resected lung specimen revealed a focal neuroendocrine component showing large cell neuroendocrine carcinoma-like features, although the strict diagnostic criteria for such a diagnosis were not fully met. Genomic analysis identified a KRAS G12V mutation shared by the renal and lung tumors, supporting the interpretation that the renal lesions represented metastatic recurrence of the previously resected lung tumor. Direct molecular confirmation was unavailable for the pancreatic lesion because of insufficient residual endoscopic ultrasound-guided tissue acquisition material; therefore, its origin remained diagnostically uncertain. Nevertheless, based on the overall clinicopathological context, the pancreatic lesion was interpreted as an accompanying neuroendocrine tumor-like lesion most consistent with metastatic recurrence. This case highlights the importance of integrating clinical history, imaging features, disease distribution, archival pathology, and molecular findings when evaluating neuroendocrine tumor-like lesions in patients with a prior malignancy.

title: Central Asian-Mongolian-Iranian celiac disease taskforce: A look into the future- 2026-2035 and beyond.
abstract: Background There is limited data on celiac disease (CeD) from Central Asia and Mongolia. In contrast, data from Iran shows a rapid increase in the number of diagnosed cases since early 2000s. Limited data is available and likely due to low awareness, limited diagnostic access and the current belief that CeD is uncommon. Objectives The first international Task Force for CeD met to have a look into the future at the Republican Specialized Centre of Pediatrics, Tashkent, Uzbekistan (March 2026) to (1) focus on diagnosis and prevalence research; (2) promote affordable serological testing for all socio-economic strata; (3) improve involvement of medical sub-specialties; (4) suggest proper gluten-free legislation for wheat food labeling and (5) organize affordable gluten-free food for CeD patients in general. KEY RECOMMENDATIONS (2026-2030): Standardize local tissue transglutaminase antibodies (tTGA) testing to ≤ 5-10$/test; evaluate point-of-care tests in rural clinics Conduct population-based serosurveys in Central Asia, Iran and Mongolia (n ≥ 1000 each) Advocate for mandatory gluten-free labeling standards (≤ 20 ppm) Evaluation of abdominal ultrasound in CeD recognition Establish CeD patient associations to improve patient empowerment in Central Asia, Mongolia and Iran Develop online CeD training modules for clinicians in local languages.

title: Temporal patterns of the association between Achilles tendon thickening and clinical outcomes after percutaneous coronary intervention in acute and chronic coronary syndromes.
abstract: Although Achilles tendon thickening (ATT) is associated with adverse outcomes after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), whether its prognostic impact differs over time between acute (ACS) and chronic coronary syndromes (CCS) remains unclear. We retrospectively analyzed 1,362 patients who underwent successful PCI and assessment of ATT using soft X-ray radiography. ATT was defined as Achilles tendon thickness ≥8.0 in men and ≥7.5 mm in women. MACE, including death, myocardial infarction, stent thrombosis, stroke, and target vessel revascularization, were investigated for up to 3 years. To evaluate temporal differences, we conducted the Kaplan-Meier method with landmark analysis and time-segmented Cox proportional hazards analyses dividing follow-up into ≤ 1 year and 1-3 years after PCI. ATT was observed in 228 patients (16.7%), who had a significantly higher incidence of MACE compared to patients without ATT. In ACS patients (n = 387), ATT was independently associated with an increased risk of MACE within 1 year, but not beyond 1 year. Conversely, in CCS patients (n = 975), ATT was not associated with early events, but was significantly associated with increased MACE risk during 1-3 years after PCI. Similar trends were observed after excluding familial hypercholesterolemia. These findings suggest different temporal patterns in the association between ATT and MACE after PCI in patients with ACS and CCS, which may provide additional insights into risk stratification during follow-up.

title: ACPSEM guideline: commissioning and quality assurance of Magnetic Resonance Imaging Linear Accelerators.
abstract: MRI-guided radiotherapy introduces unique quality assurance (QA) requirements due to magnetic field effects on dose delivery, imaging-dependent workflows, adaptive planning and system specific considerations. Consistent, vendor agnostic guidance is needed to support safe commissioning, clinical implementation, and ongoing performance monitoring across MRI-Linac platforms. This guideline defines minimum recommended MRI-Linac commissioning and QA practices to support consistent and safe clinical operation across services. It was developed by the MRI-Linac QA sub-group of the Magnetic Resonance Imaging Linac Working Group using an evidence-informed, consensus-based approach. Key international standards, task group reports, vendor documentation, and peer-reviewed literature relevant to the MRI-Linac were reviewed. Candidate QA tests were mapped to clinical risks and system functions, then organized into commissioning and routine QA domains with suggested cadence. Recommendations were refined through iterative working group review, with emphasis on implementation and auditability. The resulting commissioning recommendations are grouped into domains addressing key performance and safety areas for MRI-Linacs. Additionally, a minimum test set is proposed with suggested frequencies and tolerances where supported by evidence. Adoption of this guideline supports harmonized MRI-Linac QA practice, improved reproducibility across sites, and enhanced patient safety. The framework is designed to be implementable across platforms and evolve as MRI-guided radiotherapy workflows, vendor capabilities, and the evidence matures.

title: Practical deep learning solutions for prostate cancer segmentation and implementation in radiotherapy planning.
abstract: Accurate segmentation of the prostate and surrounding structures is crucial in radiotherapy planning to ensure effective treatment delivery while minimising radiation exposure to nearby tissues. However, existing deep learning (DL) segmentation studies often exclude clinically important structures such as the penile bulb (PB) and seminal vesicles (SV), rely heavily on large proprietary datasets that are difficult to acquire in clinical settings, and lack direct comparisons with traditional atlas-based methods. To address these gaps, this study provides practical insights for hospitals considering the implementation of DL systems by evaluating 2D U-Net models across six structured experiments, including one experiment comparing a 3D U-Net model. Notably, this is the first study to utilises publicly available prostate CT data in DL training and integrates public and private datasets to improve model robustness for prostate and adjacent anatomical structures. The inclusion of underrepresented structures, such as PB and SV, enhances the clinical applicability of the models. Our results demonstrated that moderate-sized datasets, ranging from 60 to approximately 300 in our study, can achieve sub-millimetre Mean Distance Agreement (MDA) for key organs at risk like the bladder (0.60 mm) and rectum (0.93 mm), reducing reliance on large-scale annotated data. Models trained on routine clinical contours performed well without extensive manual refinement, demonstrating that existing clinical data can be leveraged for model training. In comparisons with four commercial atlas-based tools, the 2D U-Net models achieved superior accuracy for key anatomical structures, including the prostate, bladder, and SV, with our deep learning model achieving an MDA of 1.28 mm for the prostate compared to the 1.4-2.5 mm range of the atlas tools. Although 3D models provided improved spatial context for small structures such as SV, 2D models proved to be a practical alternative due to lower computational demands, making them suitable for resource-limited clinical settings.

title: Yolo-c2ecasa: a lightweight attention-enhanced model for three-class brain tumor localization and classification in MRI.
abstract: Brain tumor localization and type classification in MRI are important tasks in computer-aided medical image analysis. However, achieving competitive localization and classification performance with lightweight models remains challenging because reducing model complexity may weaken feature representation and localization ability. In this paper, we propose YOLO-C2ECASA, a lightweight attention-enhanced object detection framework based on YOLOv11 for three-class tumor localization and classification in tumor-positive MRI images. The present study focuses on glioma, meningioma, and pituitary tumors and does not address tumor-versus-no-tumor screening. The proposed C2ECASA module replaces the original self-attention design with a parameter-efficient spatial-channel attention mechanism. It integrates improved channel attention, lightweight spatial attention, C2-based feature preservation, and adaptive fusion to enhance lesion-relevant feature representation with limited computational cost. The proposed model was compared with representative object detection models. In the single-run comparison with representative object detectors, YOLO-C2ECASA maintained competitive detection performance while requiring only 2.4M parameters, 6.2G FLOPs, a model size of 5.01 MB, and a GPU inference time of 1.9 ms per image. More importantly, across ten independent runs under scratch initialization, YOLO-C2ECASA achieved mean mAP@0.5 and mAP@0.5:0.95 values of [Formula: see text] and [Formula: see text]. Under pretrained initialization, the corresponding repeated-run results were [Formula: see text] and [Formula: see text], respectively. Under CPU-only deployment, YOLO-C2ECASA achieves an inference time of 27.4 ms per image, further demonstrating its feasibility for resource-constrained environments. These results indicate that the proposed model achieves competitive detection performance while maintaining a lower computational cost than the compared detectors. Ablation and repeated-run experiments further demonstrate that the complete C2ECASA configuration achieves the highest average performance among the evaluated configurations while maintaining low computational complexity. Overall, the proposed method provides a favorable accuracy-efficiency trade-off for lightweight brain tumor localization and type classification in tumor-positive MRI images.

title: Tumor volume may be a better indicator than diameter for occult lymph node metastasis in patients with clinical stage-1 lung cancer.
abstract: Occult lymph node metastasis (OLM) remains a major clinical challenge in patients with lung cancer despite comprehensive preoperative staging efforts. Although several predictors of OLM, including tumor diameter, metabolic activity, molecular characteristics, and radiomics, have been extensively investigated, the predictive role of tumor volume remains poorly defined. This study aimed to evaluate whether tumor volume, quantified semi-automatically using artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted Synapse 3D software, could predict OLM in patients with clinically early-stage lung cancer. Patients who underwent surgical resection for clinically staged cT1b-cN0M0 lung cancer between 2018 and 2024 were included. Tumor volume was quantified using Synapse 3D software. Associations between tumor volume and OLM were assessed using univariable and multivariable logistic regression analyses. Because tumor diameter and tumor volume may introduce multicollinearity in multivariable models, separate receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves were generated, and the corresponding areas under the curve (AUCs) were compared using the DeLong test. A total of 248 patients were included, of whom 59 (23.8%) were female. The mean age was 65.4 years. OLM were identified in 10.8%, 4.8%, and 2.0% of patients at the N1, N2a, and N2b nodal stations, respectively. Multivariable logistic regression identified younger age (p = 0.004), greater tumor volume (p = 0.01), and histopathological subtypes other than adenocarcinoma and squamous cell carcinoma as independent predictors of OLM. Tumor diameter, extent of resection, surgical approach, and PET-CT metabolic activity were not significantly associated with OLM. ROC analysis demonstrated that tumor volume had significantly greater discriminatory ability for predicting OLM than tumor diameter (AUC: 69% vs. 58%; DeLong test, p = 0.004). AI-assisted tumor volumetry is an independent predictor of occult lymph node metastasis in patients with clinically early-stage lung cancer.

title: Delayed diagnosis of MEN1 after kidney transplantation: unrecognized pre-transplant features and implications for clinical practice.
abstract: Multiple endocrine neoplasia type 1 (MEN1), characterized by multiglandular endocrine tumors such as hyperparathyroidism (HPT), is an autosomal dominant disorder caused by mutations of the MEN1 gene. In patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD), abnormalities in calcium-phosphate metabolism may obscure this diagnosis, making the recognition of MEN1 challenging. A 68-year-old man with end-stage renal disease underwent an ABO-compatible living-donor kidney transplantation (KT); however, persistent hypercalcemia prompted further evaluation, which revealed recurrent HPT with bilateral parathyroid enlargement. Pre-transplant imaging revealed an adrenal adenoma and a pancreatic tail lesion. Subsequent pituitary magnetic resonance imaging and genetic testing confirmed the diagnosis of MEN1. A retrospective review of the patient's medical history revealed several pre-transplant findings suggestive of MEN1 that had not been recognized. This case highlights that MEN1 may remain unrecognized in KT candidates owing to the occurrence of metabolic abnormalities also associated with CKD. The early recognition of MEN1 in KT candidates with recurrent or multiglandular hyperparathyroidism may improve pre-transplant risk assessment and enable appropriate long-term oncological surveillance.

title: Interpretable fundus image-based glaucoma classification using aCDR-guided vascular tortuosity analysis.
abstract: Purpose This study aimed to develop and evaluate an interpretable hierarchical auxiliary classification framework for glaucoma-related fundus image analysis, with emphasis on transparent classification rationale for cases with intermediate aCDR values. Methods A MiT-B2-scSE U-Net was employed to jointly segment the optic disc and optic cup from fundus images, and the aCDR was calculated for initial image-level classification. Samples within predefined low- and high-aCDR ranges were directly classified, whereas samples in the intermediate-aCDR group underwent further analysis using peripapillary vessel segmentation and skeleton-based tortuosity quantification. To improve the reliability of vascular morphology assessment, a distance-aware topology-constrained loss function (DATCL) was introduced in the vessel segmentation stage to improve the segmentation accuracy of peripapillary vessels and improve the reliability of subsequent calculations. Results On the current REFUGE-based test set, the proposed MiT-B2-scSE U-Net achieved a mean Dice similarity coefficient (Dice) of 0.9254 and a mean Intersection over Union (IoU) of 0.8694 for joint optic cup-disc segmentation. For image-level glaucoma classification, the hierarchical aCDR-plus-vessel strategy achieved an accuracy of 91.25%, compared with 85.0% for the aCDR-only baseline and 66.25% for the vessel-only strategy. Conclusion The proposed framework suggests that combining optic cup-disc morphology with local vascular tortuosity may provide complementary information for interpretable glaucoma classification in fundus images with intermediate aCDR values. It provides a methodological avenue for deep learning-assisted glaucoma screening. Supplementary information The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1007/s13755-026-00484-5.

title: Hospitalized primary headache in children after emergency department evaluation: a retrospective cohort study.
abstract: Objectives To characterize the clinical features, diagnostic evaluation, management, and final diagnoses of children hospitalized for headache following emergency department (ED) evaluation, and to explore factors associated with treatment refractoriness. Methods We conducted a retrospective cohort study of children aged 4-17 years presenting to a tertiary pediatric ED with headache as the primary complaint who required hospitalization between January 2019 and June 2024. Patients whose headache was clearly attributed to trauma, fever, or a previously identified systemic or neurological disorder were excluded. Final headache diagnoses were established during hospitalization by the pediatric neurology team, using ICHD-3 criteria when applicable. Data included demographics, clinical presentation, diagnostic testing, treatments, and discharge diagnoses. Descriptive analyses were performed, with exploratory comparisons between patients requiring ≤ 2 versus > 2 sequential pharmacologic interventions. Results Among 3,646 ED visits for headache, 162 (4.4%) resulted in hospitalization; 30 children (18.5% of admissions) had a final diagnosis of primary headache and constituted the study cohort. Mean age was 12.7 years, and 70.0% were female. Although frontal location and pressure-type pain were the most common presentation features, 76.7% of patients were ultimately diagnosed with migraine or probable migraine. Acute neurological abnormalities were documented in 10.0% of patients. Cranial CT was performed in 63.3% and brain MRI in 23.3%, with no acute intracranial abnormality or secondary cause explaining the headache identified. Intravenous metamizole (dipyrone) was the most frequently used first-line acute therapy, and 70.0% of patients required a second sequential pharmacologic intervention. Among patients diagnosed with migraine or probable migraine, 21.7% met criteria for status migrainosus. No clinical variables were significantly associated with treatment refractoriness. Conclusions Hospitalization for primary headache after pediatric ED evaluation was uncommon but identified a clinically severe subgroup, predominantly with migraine-spectrum disorders and frequently requiring escalation of acute treatment. Despite frequent neuroimaging, no acute intracranial abnormality or secondary cause explaining the headache was identified. These findings suggest that more selective imaging strategies may be appropriate in children with a reassuring clinical presentation, although prospective studies are needed to better define predictors of hospitalization, treatment refractoriness, and optimal acute management.

title: Olfactory dysfunction and limbic volumetric changes in relapsing-remitting and secondary progressive multiple sclerosis.
abstract: Objective To compare olfactory performance and olfactory-related brain region volumes between patients with relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis (RRMS) and secondary progressive multiple sclerosis (SPMS) and to examine the relationship between olfactory performance and regional brain volumes. Materials and methods This prospective cross-sectional study included 65 patients with MS (43 RRMS and 22 SPMS). Olfactory function was assessed using the Sniffin' Sticks-12 Odor Identification Test. Bilateral volumes of the hippocampus, amygdala, entorhinal cortex, and insular cortex were obtained from three-dimensional T1-weighted MRI using the vol2Brain automated analysis pipeline available through the volBrain platform. Both raw and total intracranial volume (TIV)-normalized regional volumes were analyzed. For volumetric outcomes, multivariable analyses were adjusted for age, sex, and TIV, whereas analyses of olfactory performance were adjusted for age and sex. Additional sensitivity analyses incorporated disease duration and EDSS. Results In unadjusted comparisons, patients with SPMS had significantly lower Sniffin' Sticks-12 scores than those with RRMS (p = 0.004), and raw hippocampal volume was significantly lower in the SPMS group (p = 0.028). However, after adjustment for age, sex, and TIV, clinical subtype was not independently associated with hippocampal, amygdala, entorhinal cortex, or insular cortex volume (all p > 0.05). These findings remained non-significant in sensitivity analyses additionally accounting for disease duration and EDSS. The between-group difference in Sniffin' Sticks-12 scores was also attenuated after adjustment for age and sex (B = - 1.06; 95% CI, - 2.15 to 0.04; p = 0.058) and remained non-significant in further sensitivity analyses. No significant correlations were observed between Sniffin' Sticks-12 scores and regional volumetric measures. Conclusion Although patients with SPMS showed poorer olfactory performance and lower raw hippocampal volume in unadjusted comparisons, clinical subtype was not independently associated with regional brain volumes after adjustment for age, sex, and TIV, and the olfactory difference did not reach statistical significance after adjustment for age and sex. Furthermore, olfactory performance was not directly associated with regional volumetric measures, suggesting that olfactory dysfunction in MS may reflect mechanisms beyond regional structural volume alone.

title: Role of ¹⁸F-FDG PET/CT in monitoring treatment response in extrapulmonary tuberculosis: a retrospective observational study.
abstract: Background Monitoring treatment response in tuberculosis (TB) remains a major clinical challenge, particularly in extrapulmonary forms. 18-F Fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography ( 18 F-FDG PET/CT) has emerged as a potential adjunctive tool, enabling quantification of metabolic activity. We report our experience using 18 F-FDG PET/CT for monitoring treatment response in extrapulmonary TB. Methods We performed a retrospective observational study at a tertiary hospital in Spain, including adult patients diagnosed with extrapulmonary TB who underwent a baseline 18 F-FDG PET/CT and at least one follow-up scan from January 2014 to April 2026. Clinical, microbiological, and radiological data were reviewed alongside changes in maximum standardized uptake value (SUVmax) across serial PET/CT studies. Results Twelve patients were included, most commonly with lymphatic (41.7%) or bone involvement (33.3%). At the end of the initially planned treatment, seven patients (58.3%) showed a marked (> 50%) reduction in SUVmax. Clinical outcomes were favourable in all seven. In contrast, the remaining five (41.7%) showed persistent or increased metabolic uptake. Among these, two had favourable clinical outcomes, suggesting sterile inflammation. The other three patients had an unfavourable clinical evolution with persistent symptoms. In two of them, new targeted biopsies demonstrated an alternative diagnosis. Conclusion 18 F-FDG PET/CT may effectively assist clinicians in monitoring treatment response in complex scenarios with a suboptimal or unfavourable clinical response. However, persistent hypermetabolism must be interpreted cautiously, as it may reflect sterile inflammation or alternative diagnoses rather than ongoing infection.

title: Borrelia garinii spirochetemia in a previously healthy child presenting with Streptococcus anginosus group brain abscess: a case report.
abstract: Background The clinical significance of transient Borrelia burgdorferi sensu lato complex (hereafter referred to as B. burgdorferi) spirochetemia remains poorly understood and has rarely been documented. We report the isolation of viable B. garinii genospecies from the blood of a previously healthy child presenting with a Streptococcus anginosus group (SAG) brain abscess. Case presentation An eight-year-old girl presented with four days of headache, fever, nausea, slightly reduced general condition, and mild facial asymmetry. Initial evaluation, including lumbar puncture, raised suspicion of viral meningitis or Lyme neuroborreliosis (LNB). Based on the differential diagnosis of Lyme disease, she was enrolled in the prospective BRILLIANT study (NCT06045416), with additional blood and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) sampling for B. burgdorferi culture and serology. Following initial outpatient management, she re-presented with clinical deterioration and signs of raised intracranial pressure. Cranial magnetic resonance imaging revealed a brain abscess requiring surgical drainage. Abscess cultures yielded SAG. Dental treatment four days before symptom onset provided a plausible source of infectious spread. Treatment with intravenous ceftriaxone and metronidazole for six weeks resulted in complete clinical recovery and radiological improvement. Borrelia burgdorferi-specific two-tier serology and CSF culture remained negative. In contrast, blood plasma culture for B. burgdorferi obtained at initial presentation yielded viable spirochetes after seven weeks. Borrelia burgdorferi DNA was confirmed by flaB-targeted qPCR, and hybrid whole-genome sequencing generated a near-complete genome identifying B. garinii genospecies. Conclusion This case demonstrates viable B. garinii spirochetemia without serological evidence of LNB, incidentally detected during investigation of a SAG brain abscess. It highlights the uncertain clinical significance of transient B. burgdorferi spirochetemia, and the importance of interpreting microbiological findings within the clinical context.

title: Artificial Intelligence for Gadolinium-Sparing Detection of Active Multiple Sclerosis Lesions: A Structured Narrative Review.
abstract: Introduction Gadolinium-enhanced T1-weighted magnetic resonance imaging (MRI; T1c+) remains the reference standard for identifying active inflammatory lesions in multiple sclerosis (MS). However, cumulative exposure raises concerns regarding tissue deposition, cost, scan duration, and patient burden. Artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a potential strategy to reduce reliance on contrast administration. Methods We conducted a structured narrative review of studies evaluating AI-based approaches for detecting active MS lesions without routine gadolinium use. Eligible studies included those that generated synthetic contrast-equivalent images or directly classified lesion activity using non-contrast MRI. Outcomes included diagnostic test accuracy, reconstruction fidelity, model characteristics, and methodological quality, which were assessed using an adapted QUADAS-2 framework. Results Among studies reporting diagnostic accuracy against a gadolinium reference standard, sensitivity ranged from 72% to 100% and specificity from 66% to 96%. Only one study reported a complete contingency table; a second reported confusion matrices that are not reproduced here, and only one classifier included external multicenter validation. Image-synthesis studies demonstrated visually plausible outputs but were frequently validated against non-gadolinium targets, limiting clinical applicability. Common limitations included lack of prospective validation, limited reporting transparency, and insufficient evaluation of generalizability. Conclusion AI-based approaches demonstrate feasibility for gadolinium-sparing MS imaging but are not yet sufficient to replace contrast-enhanced MRI in routine clinical practice. A plausible near-term role is as a triage tool to identify low-risk follow-up examinations in which gadolinium administration may be deferred. Prospective multicenter studies with standardized reporting and true post-contrast reference standards are needed before clinical adoption.

title: Divergent Trends in Relapse Activity and Relapse-Independent Progression Over Two Decades in Multiple Sclerosis.
abstract: Multiple sclerosis (MS) management has increasingly favored earlier high-efficacy disease-modifying therapy (DMT). We examined diagnosis-era changes in relapse activity and disability accrual alongside evolving DMT use. We retrospectively analyzed two Italian cohorts of adults with MS onset in 2001-2024 across four diagnosis eras. Annualized relapse rate (ARR) was modeled by Poisson regression; confirmed disability accrual (CDA), relapse-associated worsening (RAW), and progression independent of relapse activity (PIRA) by Andersen-Gill Cox models. CDA was classified as RAW when relapse onset occurred from 90 days before through 30 days after the event, otherwise as PIRA. Treatment was time-varying: untreated, low-/moderate-efficacy therapy (LET/MET), or high-efficacy therapy (HET). Inverse probability-weighted models included residual adjustment. Sensitivity analyses examined a strict common 2-year horizon, MRI restriction/adjustment, relapsing-onset MS, first-event analyses, 90-day DMT lag, early-HET exclusion, pre-treatment versus never-treated person-time, visit frequency, and center stratification. Among 1096 patients (228, 214, 292, and 362 across eras 1-4), first-line HET use reached 45.9% in era 4. Each later diagnosis year was associated with lower ARR (RR 0.98, 95% CI 0.96-0.99; p < 0.001), with steeper calendar-time declines during LET/MET and HET than untreated person-time (joint interaction p < 0.001). Later diagnosis year was also associated with lower RAW (HR 0.94, 95% CI 0.92-0.97; p < 0.001) and modestly lower CDA over full follow-up (HR 0.98, 95% CI 0.96-1.00; p = 0.026), although CDA attenuated in weighted and common-horizon analyses. PIRA was not associated with diagnosis year (HR 1.01, 95% CI 0.99-1.04; p = 0.262). Lower ARR and RAW persisted across sensitivities, whereas the strict 2-year analysis suggested higher early PIRA in more recent eras. Later diagnosis-era cohorts had lower relapse activity and relapse-associated disability accrual, whereas overall disability accrual was less consistent and PIRA did not decline. Improvements in relapse-related disease activity were not accompanied by a comparable reduction in relapse-independent disability accrual.

title: Post Hoc MRI Analysis of Orbital Soft Tissue Volumes Pre- and Post-Teprotumumab in Patients with Chronic, Low-Activity Thyroid Eye Disease.
abstract: Introduction A previous phase 4 trial (Chronic) evaluated teprotumumab treatment in patients with chronic, low-activity thyroid eye disease (TED). In the current study, volumetric changes in the orbital soft tissues, lacrimal glands, and full facial fat were evaluated following teprotumumab in a subset of patients from this chronic TED trial who underwent magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). Methods This post hoc exploratory MRI analysis examined volumetric changes of extraocular muscles (EOMs), orbital fat (OF), lacrimal glands, and full facial fat pre- and post-teprotumumab (week 24) in patients from the phase 4 Chronic trial at one preselected trial site. Patients had a TED duration of 2-10 years, diagnosis of chronic, low-activity TED (clinical activity score ≤ 1), and received eight teprotumumab infusions administered once every 3 weeks. The study (more proptotic) and fellow orbit were evaluated separately and together via MRI. Results Of the six patients (female n = 5, male n = 1) undergoing MRI at baseline and week 24, the mean age and TED duration was 45.2 and 5.5 years, respectively. At baseline, patients had a mean proptosis of 25.25 mm (study orbits) and 24.00 mm (fellow orbits). Mean (%) changes from baseline (CFB) in total EOM and OF volumes in combined study and fellow orbits after 24 weeks of teprotumumab were - 1107.3 mm 3 (- 25.0%) and - 5017.1 mm 3 (- 34.6%), respectively. Mean (%) CFB in full facial fat and study and fellow lacrimal gland volumes were - 12,175.9 mm 3 (- 6.6%), - 116.7 mm 3 (- 21.9%), and - 150.5 mm 3 (- 26.4%), respectively. Proptosis response was observed in 100% (6/6) of study and 66.7% (4/6) of fellow orbits. Conclusion MRI demonstrated that teprotumumab effectively reduces orbital soft tissue, facial fat, and lacrimal gland volumes in study and fellow orbits of patients with chronic, low-activity TED. Trial registration ClinicalTrials.gov identifier NCT04583735.

title: An Agentic AI Workflow for Automated Macular Hole Diagnosis and Structured Report Generation.
abstract: Introduction Current AI models for optical coherence tomography (OCT) primarily focus on diagnosis as a standalone task. We developed and validated an end-to-end agentic AI workflow that integrates automated macular hole (MH) diagnosis from OCT images with structured patient-friendly report generation. Methods The proposed sequential workflow coordinated by a workflow orchestration agent consisted of an image diagnosis stage and a language generation step. The OCT version of RETFound, a self-supervised retinal foundation model, was fine-tuned for binary classification of macular OCT scans as MH or normal macula. Training, validation, and internal testing were performed using multiple public OCT datasets with patient-level stratified splitting, followed by external validation on two independent datasets. The performance of the fine-tuned foundation model was evaluated using accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, and receiver operating characteristic area under the curve (ROC AUC). For each new OCT image, the AI agent used the trained RETFound model to classify the image, received the diagnostic output, incorporated it into a structured prompt, and called the large language model (GPT-4) to generate the clinical report. Results On the internal test set (n = 180), the model achieved an accuracy of 100% (95% confidence interval (CI), 97.9-100%) with an AUC of 1.00. On external validation (n = 1014), accuracy was 98.8% (95% CI 97.9-99.3%), sensitivity was 97.9% (95% CI 96.3-98.8%), specificity was 100% (95% CI 99.2-100.0%), and AUC was 0.999 (95% CI 0.998-1.000). Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM) analysis showed that predictions were driven by relevant retinal regions, particularly the macular hole and adjacent layers. The end-to-end agentic AI workflow generated concise and standardized patient-friendly reports for all samples, without the language model influencing diagnostic decisions. Conclusions This study demonstrates the feasibility of an end-to-end AI workflow coordinated by a workflow orchestration agent for robust OCT-based MH diagnosis with a large language model for structured report generation. By separating image-based diagnosis from language generation, this approach offers a practical and scalable solution for virtual vitreoretinal clinics.

title: Retinal Microvascular Morphometry in Recreational Athletes Using Anabolic-Androgenic Steroids: A Cross-Sectional Study.
abstract: Introduction Illicit use of anabolic-androgenic steroids (AAS) is common among recreational athletes and is associated with cardiovascular complications and premature death. However, effects on the microvasculature have not been quantified. The retina provides non-invasive access to the systemic microvasculature, and retinal vessel morphometry has been associated with incident cardiovascular events. Methods We conducted a cross-sectional study of 151 recreational athletes from the Fitness Doping in Denmark study: 74 active AAS users, 26 former users who had ceased AAS use at least 3 months before enrollment, and 51 age- and sex-matched controls with no lifetime AAS exposure. Disc-centered fundus photographs were analyzed using semiautomated software to obtain the arteriovenous ratio (AVR), central retinal arteriolar and venular equivalents (CRAE/CRVE), arteriolar and venular fractal dimensions, and arteriolar and venular tortuosity. Associations of active AAS use and cumulative lifetime AAS exposure with retinal vessel morphometry were assessed through multivariable linear regression models adjusted for age, sex, and body fat percentage. Results Active users had a lower arteriolar fractal dimension than both controls (1.12 vs. 1.16, P < 0.05) and former users (1.12 vs. 1.18, P < 0.05), and a lower AVR than controls (0.67 vs. 0.70, P < 0.05) in multivariable models. Former users did not differ from controls on any retinal variable. Cumulative lifetime AAS exposure was not independently associated with any outcome. Conclusion Active AAS use was associated with lower arteriolar fractal dimension and lower AVR after adjustment. These differences were absent in former users and unrelated to cumulative exposure duration. The cross-sectional design precludes determining the prognostic significance of these differences. Trial registration ClinicalTrials.gov identifier NCT05178537.
