title: PET-Guided Dose Escalation for Stage III Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
abstract: Purpose Uniform radiation dose escalation has not improved outcomes in locally advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), and locoregional failure remains common despite multimodal therapy. We evaluated whether fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography (FDG-PET)-guided dose escalation to metabolically active tumor subvolumes reduces locoregional failure compared with standard chemoradiation. Methods and materials PET-BOOST was a multi-institutional, open-label, phase 2 randomized trial conducted at 7 Canadian centers (January 2017-May 2022). Eligible patients had inoperable, FDG-avid stage IIIA/IIIB NSCLC and an achievable boost dose of at least 65 Gy. Patients were randomized 1:1 to standard chemoradiation with 60 Gy in 30 fractions or metabolically adaptive radiotherapy with an integrated boost to FDG-avid subvolumes to a maximum of 85 Gy in 30 fractions. Concurrent platinum-based chemotherapy was planned, and consolidation durvalumab was permitted after 2018. The primary endpoint was 2-year locoregional failure; secondary endpoints included overall survival (OS), progression-free survival (PFS), grade ≥3 treatment-related toxicity, and quality of life (QOL). Results Seventy-eight patients were randomized: 40 to standard radiotherapy and 38 to dose escalation, with a median follow-up of 5.0 years. Median age was 64.4 years; 53% were male, 62% had stage IIIA disease, and 76% received consolidation durvalumab. Median prescription boost dose was 75 Gy. Two-year locoregional failure was 27.5% with standard radiotherapy versus 18.4% with dose escalation (P=.13). Two-year OS (72.5% vs. 73.7%; P=.91) and PFS (52.5% vs. 57.9%; P=.74) did not differ between arms. Grade ≥3 treatment-related toxicities occurred in 25% versus 37% of patients (P=.26), with one grade 5 pulmonary hemorrhage in the dose-escalation arm. QOL did not differ between arms. Conclusions Metabolically adaptive PET-guided radiotherapy dose escalation was feasible in the context of consolidation immunotherapy and resulted in a numerically lower rate of locoregional failure, but did not significantly improve locoregional control or survival. The lower-than-anticipated event rate may have limited statistical power, and larger studies would be required to determine whether selective dose escalation provides a clinically meaningful improvement in locoregional control.

title: Can radiological parameters predict failure of fixation in distal radius fractures treated with a volar locking plate?
abstract: Introduction Fractures of the distal radius are common, and volar locking plates are the most utilized fixation method. Failure of fixation, defined as post-operative fracture collapse leading to loss of reduction and/or screw penetration, is an undesirable outcome. We aimed to demonstrate whether preoperative and intraoperative radiographic parameters are associated with subsequent failure of fixation in order to produce a model that may be able to predict failure. Methods A retrospective case-control study of 23 cases of failure of fixation matched to controls from the same cohort by age, sex, and AO classification in a 3:1 ratio. Nine initial injury and 13 intraoperative radiological parameters were evaluated, and multi-variate regression analysis models were analysed to assess if they could reliably predict failure. Results A total of 92 patients were analysed (23 cases, 69 controls). Size of intraarticular gap was the only preoperative parameter to be associated failure with every 0.47 mm increase in fracture gap resulting in a 1.6 increase of odds ratio of failure. Based on intraoperative radiological parameters, three factors were associated with failure: dorsal capitate translation, intraarticular gap and step. Models based on these parameters do not accurately predict failure, however, models based on intraoperative factors are associated with risk of failure with high specificity but low sensitivity. Conclusion We conclude that the severity of the injury is less importantly associated with failure of fixation, whereas the quality of the surgical fixation and specifically the accuracy of the reduction are more important.

title: Effect of AI-assisted radiographic fracture detection on paediatric emergency department length of stay through fracture exclusion: A before-after cohort study.
abstract: Background Artificial intelligence-assisted radiographic fracture detection tools (AI-RFDT) have the potential to support confident fracture exclusion by physicians in the paediatric emergency department (ED), where presentations for suspected fractures substantially outnumber confirmed fractures. This study aimed to evaluate whether implementation of AI-RFDT in a paediatric ED is associated with reduced length of stay (LOS) among patients presenting with suspected fractures, and to determine whether any observed effect is specifically mediated through the fracture-exclusion pathway. Patients and methods This retrospective before-after cohort study was conducted at a single tertiary paediatric ED. AI-RFDT (BoneView, Gleamer, Paris, France) was deployed on 1 October 2023 as a passive, second-read decision-support tool. The study population comprised 4172 paediatric patients with rule-out fracture diagnoses (fracture-excluded; F-E) during standard working hours (08:00-15:59; pre-AI n = 2514; post-AI n = 1658). Fracture-confirmed (F-C) patients served as a pre-specified internal control (n = 1155). The primary outcome was ED LOS; secondary outcomes were orthopaedic consultation rate, LOS by consultation status, anatomical subgroup LOS, and 30-day re-admission. Results Orthopaedic consultation rates in the paediatric ED decreased from 73% to 68.3% (Δ -4.7 %age points, p = 0.002). The greatest reduction was observed in patients discharged without orthopaedic consultation (2.25→1.78 h, Δ -28 min, p < 0.001), while those with confirmed fractures demonstrated no significant change in LOS (Δ+3 min, p = 0.51). 30-day re-admission rates remained unchanged (6.9% vs 6.9%, p = 1.00). Wrist and forearm injuries demonstrated the greatest LOS reduction (Δ -24 min, p = 0.004). Conclusions Deployment of AI-RFDT in a paediatric ED was associated with a reduction in LOS that was concentrated among patients discharged without orthopaedic consultation. The absence of LOS change in confirmed-fracture controls supports a mechanism specific to fracture exclusion rather than generalised care acceleration.

title: Adjunct rim plating for selected pilon fracture patterns: Lessons from hyperextension tibial plateau fractures.
abstract: Background Pilon fractures frequently involve small anterior or anterolateral marginal fragments that are susceptible to shear displacement and may not be reliably controlled by conventional periarticular plates. Rim plating is a fragment-specific, low-profile juxta-articular buttress technique that has demonstrated favorable biomechanical and clinical results in selected tibial plateau fracture patterns. This review examines the rationale for extending this concept to selected pilon fracture patterns. Methods We performed a narrative review of clinical, cadaveric, and biomechanical studies describing rim-based constructs in tibial plateau fractures, with emphasis on hyperextension and posterolateral patterns, as well as computed tomography (CT)-based studies of pilon fracture morphology and fragment capture by precontoured plates. Relevant studies were identified through PubMed and reference screening and synthesized qualitatively to inform a technical proposal for adjunct rim plating in selected pilon fractures. Results The reviewed tibial plateau literature consistently identified peripheral regions that may remain unsupported by conventional periarticular plates, particularly in hyperextension and posterolateral fracture patterns, where adjunct rim plating has been associated with maintained reduction and favorable clinical outcomes. In the distal tibia, CT-based studies suggest that commonly used anatomically precontoured plates may not reliably capture the anterolateral (Tillaux-Chaput) fragment when fragment height is less than 15 mm. In this setting, an adjunct rim plate may serve as a peripheral buttress to improve support of the articular margin, distribute subchondral stress, and prevent displacement of the articular block. Conclusions Rim plating may be best conceptualized as a joint-line buttress strategy for improving peripheral containment of shear-dominant marginal fragments. Extrapolation of this concept to selected pilon fracture patterns is mechanically plausible and supported indirectly by CT-based fragment-capture data. This technique may be useful in carefully selected anterior or anterolateral distal tibial rim fractures that are not adequately controlled by standard periarticular plating.

title: Advancing early detection of Alzheimer's disease: from established biomarkers to future innovations.
abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a major form of dementia, imposes an escalating global burden on public health and social care. Pathological changes in AD occur years before clinical symptoms, defining a prolonged preclinical phase. Currently, there is no effective treatment exist for late-stage AD, making early diagnosis and intervention indispensable, in which biomarkers play a pivotal role. While cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) and positron emission tomography (PET) biomarkers improved AD diagnostic accuracy, their clinical application is limited by invasiveness, high costs. Advances in ultrasensitive immunoassay technologies has rendered peripheral blood biomarkers easily accessible, cost-effective, minimally invasive, and suitable for continuous monitoring, offering noval opportunities for AD screening, diagnosis and progression tracking. Additionally, non-invasive body fluids including saliva, urine and tears are being explored as potential biomarkers. Artificial intelligence (AI)-driven multimodal fusion, integrated with large-scale multimodal computing frameworks, significantly improve the accuracy of early AD diagnosis. Recent studies have identified a series of promising synaptic and neuronal biomarkers, such as neurofilament light chain (NFL), neurogranin (Ng), β-secretase 1 (BACE1) and synaptosomal-associated protein 25 (SNAP-25). Inflammatory mediators and genetic factors also contribute to AD pathological evaluation. This review systematically characterizes biomarker profiles of emerging non-invasive carriers (saliva, urine and tears). It further synthesizes cohort-derived quantitative diagnostic metrics (AUC, sensitivity, specificity) of multimodal AD biomarkers and conducts head-to-head comparison to clarify their respective strengths and translational limitations, aiming to provide evidence-based insights for optimizing early AD screening and diagnostic strategies.

title: Intelligent immunotherapy: AI-driven optimization of CAR-T therapy in hematologic malignancies.
abstract: Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-T cell therapy has transformed outcomes in selected hematologic malignancies, yet its delivery remains constrained by variable efficacy, acute and prolonged toxicities, and complex manufacturing logistics. Artificial intelligence (AI) is being applied across the CAR-T continuum at three distinct levels of evidentiary maturity. Externally validated parsimonious models built on routine clinical and laboratory data including CAR-HEMATOTOX, endothelial activation and stress index (EASIX) and m-EASIX, MyCARe, and gradient-boosting cytokine release syndrome predictors provide deployable risk stratification today. Methodologically sophisticated tools using deep-learning positron emission tomography (PET) segmentation, attention-based digital-pathology analysis, and multimodal fusion of imaging with laboratory and circulating tumor DNA features have demonstrated technical promise but generally lack the multi-center external validation required for clinical-grade deployment. Forward-looking applications, including digital-twin frameworks, large language models, and closed-loop adaptive therapy, remain at the prototype stage and have not yet been validated for CAR-T. This review synthesizes these three tiers, summarizes 18 published AI and statistical-modeling tools in a comparative performance table, and compares data characteristics and AI modeling paradigms across large B cell lymphoma, B cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia, and multiple myeloma. We also identify the implementation realities-absent regulatory clearance, demographic and racial bias in training data, and post-deployment model drift-that condition the field's evolution. The contribution of AI to CAR-T therapy, as the evidence currently stands, is the calibrated quantification of established risk factors rather than the discovery of novel biology, but the methodological and data infrastructure foundations are now in place for the broader transformation that the next decade may enable.

title: Habitat informed 3D deep learning predicts immunochemotherapy response in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma.
abstract: Immunochemotherapy (ICT) is a critical treatment for locally advanced esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (LA-ESCC), yet predicting individual response remains challenging. We developed a three-channel 3D deep learning framework integrating tumor habitat analysis for predicting ICT response. In this multicenter retrospective study of 277 patients, voxel-level clustering of pretreatment CT images segmented tumors into habitat subregions reflecting microenvironmental heterogeneity. A ResNet-50 model incorporating habitat maps, cropped tumor images, and ROI masks achieved an AUC of 0.927 (95% CI, 0.850-0.951) in the independent external test cohort, compared with 0.869 for habitat radiomics (DeLong p = 0.343). SHapley Additive exPlanations analysis identified texture features, particularly gray-level co-occurrence matrix correlation in habitat 3, as the primary contributors. This framework provides a noninvasive approach for predicting ICT response in LA-ESCC.

title: Assessing the incidence of retinal hemorrhage in pediatric patients following COVID-19 vaccination.
abstract: Background Retinal hemorrhages (RHs) are a cardinal finding in abusive head trauma (AHT) for which a broad differential diagnosis is appropriate to consider. The frequency of COVID-19 vaccination and reports of subsequent ocular manifestations have led to the consideration of whether COVID-19 vaccination should be included in the RH differential. This study aimed to investigate the frequency of RH following COVID-19 vaccination in children. Methods In this single-center, retrospective, observational cohort study, we reviewed the medical records of children ≤8 years of age who received a COVID-19 vaccine from July 1, 2020, to July 1, 2024, and underwent a fundus examination within 21 days of vaccination. The main outcome measure was incidence and characteristics of RH on fundus examination. Results Of 17,926 children vaccinated during this period, 203 subjects met inclusion criteria and underwent 212 unique examinations, with mean age of 4.56 years (0-8) at the time of first examination. Twenty examinations were also in the setting of prior COVID-19 infection. No examinations revealed RH. Based on Hanley's rule of zero incidence, the 95th percentile upper limit of incidence of RH after COVID-19 vaccination is 4.11% at 7 days, 2.04% at 14 days, and 1.42% at 21 days following vaccination. Conclusions RHs were not seen in any children within 21 days of COVID-19 vaccination. This suggests that RH is rare following COVID-19 vaccination and perhaps of little relevance to the differential diagnosis of RH in the evaluation for AHT.

title: Intraoperative and radiographic indicators of extraocular muscle aberrancy in syndromic craniosynostosis.
abstract: Background Strabismus is common in syndromic craniosynostosis, often attributed to abnormal extraocular muscle (EOM) trajectory, and orbital anatomy. Absent EOMs have been reported, but the spectrum of primary dysgenesis remains poorly understood. The purpose of this study was to characterize the range of EOM dysgenesis in a large cohort that had undergone strabismus surgery. Methods The medical records of patients with syndromic craniosynostosis treated at Boston Children's Hospital (2010-2023) were reviewed retrospectively to identify all cases with neuroimaging and history of strabismus surgery. Genetic testing results and EOM abnormalities noted on neuroimaging or during surgery were recorded. Imaging was reviewed to determine presence of each EOM. Superior oblique muscle (SO) size was classified as "normal" if its transverse diameter was at least one-half that of the adjacent medial rectus muscle. Results A total of 47 patients with syndromic craniosynostosis had undergone strabismus surgery, of whom 43 had available neuroimaging. Syndromic associations were as follows: 21 patients with Apert, 10 with Crouzon, 6 with Pfeiffer, 5 with Saethre-Chotzen, and 1 with Muenke. Rectus and inferior oblique muscles were universally present. SO size was normal in only 15 of 86 eyes (17%). EOM aberrancies were noted intraoperatively in 15 of 43 operative cases (35%), including diaphanous insertions, bifid or fused rectus muscles, and posterior inferior oblique insertions. Results of genetic testing were available for 26 patients, 24 of whom had FGFR2 mutations, including all 10 (of 15) patients with intraoperatively noted EOM aberrancies who underwent genetic testing. Conclusions In this cohort with syndromic craniosynostosis, thin-section or high-resolution orbital imaging demonstrated presence of all rectus muscles even when insertions were diaphanous. The SO was hypoplastic in 83%. Aberrancies noted intraoperatively in 35% likely underestimate the true incidence, because evaluation was limited to muscles targeted for surgery.

title: A Knowledge Graph Framework for Longitudinal Congenital Heart Disease Modeling: Methodology Corner.
abstract: Background Congenital heart disease (CHD) is characterized by evolving clinical trajectories; staged interventions; and complex relationships among diagnoses, procedures, and encounters. Conventional machine learning applied to electronic health record (EHR) data often rely on static feature representations that do not preserve the natural longitudinal disease progression or clinical context. Objectives The purpose of this study was to develop a knowledge graph-based framework for trajectory-aware representation and analysis of longitudinal CHD EHR data. Methods We constructed a longitudinal knowledge graph that integrates patients, encounters, diagnoses, and procedures while preserving temporal ordering across the care continuum. Term frequency-inverse document frequency and Word2Vec approaches were applied to encounter contexts extracted from the graph to generate longitudinal patient representations that supported phenotyping, patient similarity analysis, and retrospective classification. Results Using accumulated longitudinal EHR from a cardiovascular magnetic resonance cohort, we demonstrate that the framework captured clinically meaningful patterns and supported retrospective identification of single ventricle physiology as a representative use case. Conclusions This knowledge graph framework provides a scalable approach for preserving temporal and relational clinical context and enable trajectory-aware modeling of longitudinal cardiovascular EHR data in patients with CHD.

title: Absence of Fibrosis Influences Prognosis of Cardiac Resynchronization in Nonischemic Cardiomyopathy: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract: Background In patients with nonischemic cardiomyopathy (NICM) undergoing cardiac resynchronization therapy (CRT), there are no clear recommendations on selecting CRT with defibrillator (CRT-D) vs pacemaker (CRT-P). Patients with high probability of response to CRT and low arrhythmic risk may be ideal candidates to CRT-P. Objectives The objectives of the study was to evaluate if the absence of late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) is associated with CRT response and ventricular arrhythmia (VA) in NICM treated with CRT. Methods A systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted. Search of PubMed, Web of Science, and Scopus identified observational studies of NICM patients who underwent cardiac magnetic resonance before CRT implantation. Studies assessing echocardiographic response to CRT or VA stratified by LGE status were included. The VA endpoint comprised sustained ventricular tachycardia, appropriate implantable cardioverter-defibrillator therapy, resuscitated cardiac arrest, and sudden death. Results Ten studies were included: 9 (n = 831) for CRT response and 6 (745 patients) for arrhythmic risk. CRT response was significantly higher in patients without LGE than in patients with LGE (78.7% vs 50.7%; P < 0.001). The cumulative incidence of VA was extremely low in LGE cases, significantly lower than that of LGE+ ones (0.8% vs 21.1%, P < 0.001). The absence of LGE was strongly associated with higher CRT response (OR: 3.52; 95% CI: 2.54-4.88; P < 0.001) and much lower arrhythmic risk (OR: 0.06; 95% CI: 0.02-0.15; P < 0.001). Conclusions In NICM patients undergoing CRT, the absence of LGE is strongly associated with greater echocardiographic response and very low arrhythmic risk. In this subgroup the incremental benefit of CRT with defibrillator over CRT-P may be limited.

title: Endovascular Solution for Anastomotic Pseudoaneurysm of the Ascending Aorta.
abstract: Objective The objective was to demonstrate the feasibility of ascending thoracic endovascular aortic repair (a-TEVAR) as a minimally invasive treatment for an ascending anastomotic pseudoaneurysm in a patient unsuitable for redo open surgery. Key steps The steps included: 1) multidisciplinary evaluation and detailed computed tomography angiography-based anatomical planning; 2) assessment of proximal and distal landing zones, coronary ostia, and supra-aortic vessel anatomy; 3) selection of a Gore C-TAG endograft based on anatomical suitability; 4) percutaneous transfemoral a-TEVAR under rapid ventricular pacing with intraoperative angiographic guidance; and 5) confirmation of complete pseudoaneurysm exclusion while preserving coronary and supra-aortic vessel patency, followed by serial computed tomography angiography surveillance. Potential pitfalls Limited landing zones, proximity to the coronary ostia and supra-aortic vessels, inaccurate device deployment, and the absence of dedicated ascending aortic devices increase procedural complexity. Careful patient selection, meticulous preoperative planning, and rapid ventricular pacing are essential to minimize these risks. Take-home messages The a-TEVAR procedure is a feasible alternative to high-risk redo sternotomy in carefully selected patients with favorable anatomy. However, a-TEVAR of the ascending aorta continues to pose significant technical and clinical challenges, and further investigations are needed.

title: Extremely Severe Aortic Stenosis Mimicking Cardiac Amyloidosis on Multimodality Imaging.
abstract: Cardiac amyloidosis is increasingly recognized in older patients with severe aortic stenosis, yet advanced pressure-overload remodeling can produce overlapping imaging features that confound noninvasive diagnosis. A 70-year-old woman presented with progressive exertional dyspnea and markedly elevated cardiac biomarkers. Transthoracic echocardiography revealed extremely severe calcific aortic stenosis, increased left ventricular wall thickness, and severely reduced global longitudinal strain. Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated elevated native T1 and extracellular volume with late gadolinium enhancement, and cardiac amyloid radionuclide imaging showed Perugini grade 1 uptake. Despite clinical suspicion of cardiac amyloidosis, noninvasive findings remained inconclusive. The patient underwent surgical aortic valve replacement with intraoperative myocardial biopsy, which demonstrated cardiomyocyte hypertrophy and interstitial fibrosis without amyloid deposition, consistent with advanced pressure-overload remodeling rather than infiltrative disease. Extremely severe aortic stenosis can mimic cardiac amyloidosis across multiple imaging modalities. Histologic confirmation remains essential when noninvasive findings are discordant or inconclusive. Severe aortic stenosis may closely mimic cardiac amyloidosis on multimodality imaging. Histological confirmation can be decisive in resolving diagnostic uncertainty.

title: PCCT and IVUS-NIRS for High-Risk Plaque Management.
abstract: Background High-risk coronary plaque may be underrecognized in patients with atypical symptoms and negative biomarkers. Advanced coronary imaging can add anatomical and prognostic information. Case summary A 59-year-old woman presented with acute chest pain, mild ischemic electrocardiographic changes, and negative high-sensitivity troponin. Photon-counting computed tomography (PCCT) showed a predominantly noncalcified, lipid-rich-appearing plaque in the left anterior descending artery despite a low risk profile. Angiography confirmed significant stenosis, and intravascular ultrasound with near-infrared spectroscopy (NIRS) demonstrated a high-risk plaque phenotype with maximum lipid core burden index over 4 mm of 347. Percutaneous coronary intervention used distal drug-coated balloon treatment and proximal-to-mid drug-eluting stent implantation. Postprocedural imaging confirmed adequate stent expansion and lower NIRS lipid signal. Discussion This case highlights the complementary role of PCCT and intravascular imaging for identifying and managing vulnerable coronary plaque. Take-home message PCCT for noninvasive plaque characterization and intravascular ultrasound-NIRS for intraprocedural guidance provide a complementary strategy for personalized management of vulnerable coronary plaque.

title: Giant Aneurysm of a Classic Blalock-Taussig Shunt in Adult Tetralogy of Fallot.
abstract: Background Giant aneurysmal degeneration of a classic Blalock-Taussig (BT) shunt is a rare, life-threatening late complication of tetralogy of Fallot (TOF) palliation. Case A 47-year-old woman with unrepaired TOF palliated in childhood presented with exertional dyspnea and a right thoracic mass. Echocardiography revealed severe right ventricular outflow tract obstruction, a large ventricular septal defect, and a pulsatile extracardiac structure. Computed tomography and cardiac magnetic resonance imaging confirmed a giant (72 × 66 mm) true aneurysm of a right BT shunt. She underwent successful aneurysm excision, ventricular septal defect closure, right ventricular outflow tract reconstruction, and pulmonary valve replacement. Discussion This case demonstrates a rare late complication of a classic BT shunt decades after TOF palliation. Conclusion Classic BT shunts may develop life-threatening aneurysmal degeneration decades after palliation, emphasizing lifelong surveillance and timely definitive management. Take-home message Lifelong imaging surveillance and multimodality imaging are essential for detecting late vascular complications.

title: Durable Vessel Patency Achieved by Drug-Coated Balloon-Only Percutaneous Coronary Intervention in Triglyceride Deposit Cardiomyovasculopathy.
abstract: Background Triglyceride deposit cardiomyovasculopathy (TGCV) causes triglyceride accumulation in cardiomyocytes and vascular smooth muscle cells, leading to diffuse coronary artery disease and frequent restenosis after percutaneous coronary intervention. Case summary A 37-year-old man with diabetes mellitus presented with diffuse 3-vessel coronary disease. Angiography and computed tomography revealed concentric diffuse coronary stenoses, and intravascular ultrasound demonstrated periadventitial low-echoic structures. Iodine-123-β-methyl-iodophenyl pentadecanoic acid scintigraphy showed a severely reduced washout rate, supporting the diagnosis of TGCV. The patient underwent percutaneous coronary intervention using a cutting balloon followed by drug-coated balloon angioplasty without stent implantation. No restenosis was observed by angiography at 1 year or computed tomography at 3 years. Discussion This case suggests that a stentless revascularization strategy using a drug-coated balloon may be a feasible option in TGCV, potentially avoiding pathological vascular responses associated with permanent metallic scaffolds. Take-home message Stentless intervention may represent a promising therapeutic option in patients with TGCV.

title: Cardiac CT Planning of Surgical Treatment of Multiple Coronary-Pulmonary Fistulas With Chronic Coronary Occlusion.
abstract: Anatomy Coronary fistulas are rare congenital anomalies that may lead to myocardial ischemia through a coronary steal phenomenon, particularly when associated with coronary artery disease. Pathology We describe a case of cardiac computed tomography angiography (CCTA) diagnosis of multiple coronary-pulmonary artery fistulas associated with chronic occlusion of the right coronary artery, in a 66-year-old man presenting with unstable angina. Imaging correlation CCTA and echocardiography were used for evaluation of procedural planning in an acute setting. Treatment The fistulas were effectively treated with surgical exclusion combined with coronary artery bypass grafting, yielding an optimal result on the postoperative computed tomography scan. Take-home messages Coronary fistulas are rare but important causes of myocardial ischemia. This case highlights the importance of CCTA definition of anatomical complexity and multidisciplinary decision-making in the management of complex coronary fistulas. Surgical repair remains the preferred approach in complex anatomy cases or associated coronary artery disease requiring revascularization.

title: Multisource Coronary Artery Fistula Draining Into the Coronary Sinus: Multimodality Imaging and Surgical Repair.
abstract: Background Coronary artery fistula (CAF) is a rare congenital coronary anomaly. Multisource CAF draining into the coronary sinus is exceptionally uncommon and anatomically complex. Case presentation A woman presented with progressive exertional dyspnea and right-sided heart failure. Multimodality imaging, including transthoracic echocardiography, coronary computed tomography angiography, and invasive coronary angiography, demonstrated multisource CAFs arising from the right coronary artery and left circumflex artery draining into the coronary sinus with diffuse aneurysmal coronary dilatation. The patient underwent surgical ligation of the dominant right CAF with concomitant tricuspid annuloplasty. Postoperative imaging demonstrated successful closure of the dominant right CAF with thrombus formation within the ligated fistulous tract, whereas the smaller left circumflex artery fistula persisted, and serial follow-up demonstrated clinical improvement. Conclusion Multimodality imaging is essential for diagnosis, treatment planning, and postoperative surveillance of complex CAF. Surgical repair remains an effective treatment strategy for anatomically complex fistulas associated with significant hemodynamic consequences.

title: Reducing Clinician Annotation Fatigue in Open-Set Federated Learning: A Client-Adaptive Vision-Language Gatekeeper.
abstract: Purpose Federated learning enables breast-imaging sites to jointly train mammography artificial intelligence (AI) without sharing images, but radiologists at each site must still annotate selected images during active-learning rounds. We developed and evaluated a client-adaptive vision-language gatekeeper that withholds radiopaque artifact-containing images considered unsuitable for a breast-density annotation objective and quantified its effect on annotation time, queue quality, and label reliability. Methods In this retrospective, scanner-partitioned study, we used FedEMBED, derived from the public Emory Breast Imaging Dataset (222,700 training and 65,891 test images; four scanners; artifact prevalence 4.8%-13.1% per scanner). PromptGate adapted a biomedical vision-language model with site-specific learnable prompts and classified each image as relevant in-distribution (ID) or irrelevant out-of-distribution (OOD) using the class with the highest softmax probability. A single radiologist who is a member of the study team and has 2 years of breast imaging experience independently read a patient-separated, artifact-enriched cohort of 500 single mammographic views (ID, n=346; OOD, n=154). Cases were randomized, ID and OOD images were intermixed, and the reader was blinded to reference labels, PromptGate decisions, enrichment status, and scanner metadata. Results PromptGate withheld 101 of 154 artifact-containing images and 54 of 346 ID images, corresponding to 65.6% artifact sensitivity, 84.4% ID retention, and a 15.6% false-removal rate among ID images. Gross annotation time decreased by ∼30% (3.82 to 2.68 hours; 1.14 hours) in the enriched cohort; an analysis crediting only correctly removed artifacts yielded an estimated 20.0% reduction. A simple prevalence-based extrapolation suggests an approximate 20- to 65-min saving per 500 images at the observed scanner-specific prevalence, although the absolute benefit is expected to be smaller than in the enriched cohort. Artifact discrimination reached an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.85. Reader agreement with the manual artifact reference was 93.6% (κ=0.85), whereas agreement with the clinical-record density label was 60.9% exact (κ=0.48). Queue purity reached 92.5%, compared with 88.5% without filtering and 87.0% with a static vision-language model filter, while downstream density accuracy remained similar to the unfiltered condition. Conclusion In this retrospective proof-of-concept study, a privacy-oriented, scanner-adaptive vision-language gate improved the concentration of task-relevant images in federated breast-density annotation queues and reduced gross reading time. Because some ID images were incorrectly withheld and the reader study used an artifact-enriched cohort, a prospective multireader and multi-institutional evaluation is needed before operational deployment.

title: Mapping International Lung Cancer Screening Quality Indicators to the American College of Radiology Lung Cancer Screening Registry: A Crosswalk Analysis.
abstract: The International Association for the Study of Lung Cancer (IASLC) established 26 consensus quality indicators (QIs) for lung cancer screening (LCS) programs, of which 20 were rated as essential and 6 as desirable by the expert panel. We evaluated the extent to which the American College of Radiology (ACR) Lung Cancer Screening Registry (LCSR), the largest LCS registry in the U.S., can support measurement of the IASLC QIs. We performed a crosswalk analysis, mapping all 26 IASLC QIs to the LCSR Data Dictionary and its 46 clinical performance measures, classifying each as directly measurable, derivable, or not measurable. The crosswalk was reviewed and independently validated by members of the ACR Early Lung Cancer Detection Registry Quality and Education Committee. Eight QIs (30.8%) were directly measurable, 10 (38.5%) were derivable, and 8 (30.8%) were not measurable from LCSR data alone. The LCSR therefore contains sufficient data elements to support measurement of approximately 69% of IASLC QIs. Remaining gaps involve screening uptake, clinical investigation, procedure complications, curative-intent treatment, treatment equity, diagnostic investigation equity and selected wait-time measures and would require additional registry fields or external data linkage.

title: Timeliness of an Expedited Diagnostic Pathway for Screening Mammography Recalls.
abstract: Objective To compare diagnostic and biopsy timeliness, malignancy yield, and cancer characteristics between expedited and standard screening mammography recall pathways. Methods An expedited recall workflow implemented in Epic enabled radiologists to flag highly suspicious BI-RADS 0 findings for telephone scheduling into reserved appointments, targeting diagnostic evaluation within one week. We retrospectively reviewed recalls from 11/1/2024-1/31/2026. Primary outcomes were time from screening to diagnostic evaluation and malignancy yield (PPV1 and PPV3). Secondary outcomes included diagnostic-to-biopsy and screening-to-biopsy intervals, delayed diagnostic imaging (≥30 days from screening), delayed biopsy (≥30 days from diagnostic), and malignancy characteristics. Intervals were measured in calendar days. Results Among 36,384 screening mammograms, 4,647 were BI-RADS 0 (recall rate 12.8%); 57 (1.2%) were expedited. After excluding 247 standard pathway cases without follow-up, 4,400 were analyzed. Expedited patients were older (median 64.6 vs 52.5 years, p<0.001) with shorter median screening-to-diagnostic (7 vs 25 days), diagnostic-to-biopsy (14 vs 19 days), and screening-to-biopsy intervals (24 vs 45 days; all p<0.001). Delayed diagnostic imaging (7.0% vs 38.2%, p<0.001) and biopsy (1.8% vs 14.5%, p=0.004) were less frequent. Expedited cases had higher BI-RADS 4/5 rates (96.5% vs 30.1%, p<0.001) and malignancy yield (PPV1 91.2% vs 5.2%; PPV3 94.5% vs 18.2%; p<0.001). Multivariable logistic regression among 278 cancers identified mass findings (OR 3.36, p<0.001) and imaging size (OR 1.03/mm, p=0.003) as predictors of expedited routing. Discussion Radiologists identified highly suspicious screening mammography findings for expedited evaluation. Expedited routing was associated with shorter diagnostic and biopsy intervals and high malignancy yield, supporting diagnostic resource prioritization.

title: LungCheck: Pilot Testing a Theory-Informed Multicomponent Strategy to Increase Lung Cancer Screening in Primary Care Settings.
abstract: Objective Lung cancer screening (LCS) with low-dose computed tomography (LDCT) reduces lung cancer-specific and all-cause mortality, yet uptake remains low. This study evaluates LungCheck, a theory-informed multicomponent behavior change and implementation strategy designed to increase LDCT ordering in two diverse primary care settings. Methods This pilot study compared 16-month pilot and pre-pilot periods at a federally qualified health center (FQHC) and an academic faculty practice in New York City. LungCheck comprised educational meetings, materials and clinician reminders, an implementation blueprint, patient navigation, and EHR modifications. LDCT ordering rates (primary outcome) were compared using generalized estimating equations (GEE). Post-implementation surveys assessed acceptability, appropriateness, and feasibility. Results A total of 5,918 patient-period observations were included (1,569 academic; 4,349 FQHC). Among patients with documented LCS eligibility, the odds of LDCT ordering were significantly higher during the pilot at both the academic practice (OR, 2.67; 95% CI, 1.47-4.85; p=0.001) and FQHC (OR, 4.53; 95% CI, 2.29-8.94; p<0.001). A combined-site multivariable model adjusting for site, age, sex, and race confirmed higher odds of LDCT ordering during the pilot (OR, 1.95; 95% CI, 1.44-2.63; p<0.001). Among patients with an LDCT order, completion was 71.4% (10/14) pre-pilot versus 35.7% (15/42) during the pilot at the academic practice and 42.9% (18/42; 95% CI, 28%-59%) versus 39.3% (24/61; 95% CI, 27%-53%) at the FQHC. The strategy was rated as highly acceptable (AIM, 4.47/5), appropriate (IAM, 4.44/5), and feasible (FIM, 4.41/5). Discussion LungCheck was associated with significantly increased LDCT ordering at both sites, high acceptability, feasibility, and appropriateness ratings and high provider knowledge, confidence, and perceived skills related to LCS. Although a corresponding improvement in LDCT completion was not observed, the small number of LDCT orders limited the precision of completion estimates. Persistent environmental and patient-level barriers underscore the need to adapt LungCheck into a multilevel intervention addressing patient-, provider, and system-level barriers across the LCS continuum, to be evaluated in a future cluster randomized trial.

title: Right putaminal gray matter change tracks psychomotor recovery after accelerated iTBS in melancholic treatment-resistant depression.
abstract: Background Psychomotor retardation is a prominent and disabling feature of melancholic depression. Accelerated intermittent theta-burst stimulation (aiTBS) may hasten antidepressant effects, but neural substrates of early symptom improvement remain unclear. Given the central role of frontostriatal circuitry in motivation and behavioral activation, structural alterations in the striatum may represent a possible neural substrate of early therapeutic change. Methods Structural MRI was acquired from 61 patients with melancholic TRD and 77 healthy controls, and voxel-based morphometry was used to assess baseline striatal gray matter volume differences. Patients then underwent a randomized, double-blind, sham-controlled trial of left dorsolateral prefrontal aiTBS, comprising 20 sessions over four days. In 50 patients with complete pre- and post-treatment data, we tested whether GMV change in the baseline-identified striatal region was associated with clinical change in the active and sham groups (n = 25 each). Results Patients showed greater right putamen GMV than controls at baseline. After active aiTBS, greater right putamen GMV increase was associated with greater psychomotor retardation improvement. This association was absent after sham stimulation and was not observed for overall depression severity. Conclusion The right putamen appears structurally altered in melancholic TRD. After active aiTBS, short-term putamen GMV increase was associated with psychomotor rather than broader depressive improvement. This pattern should not be interpreted as structural normalization but may reflect a relationship between putaminal change and early psychomotor recovery.

title: Quantifying digital volume correlation strain uncertainty at the bone-pedicle screw interface: an ex-vivo zero-strain analysis.
abstract: Pedicle screws are essential for postoperative construct stability in spinal fusion surgeries. However, screw loosening remains a common clinical complication, often linked to excessive loading that induces damaging trabecular bone strains surrounding the pedicle screw. Toward improving pre-clinical assessment of pedicle screw fixation, this study combines micro-CT imaging, U-Net deep learning segmentation, and digital volume correlation (DVC) techniques to quantify the errors associated with measuring full-field strains at the screw-bone interface under nominal zero-strain conditions. Pedicle screws were surgically implanted into six human lumbar vertebrae specimens. Each specimen underwent micro-CT imaging. For three specimens, paired unloaded scans were acquired and analyzed using a standard DVC uncertainty workflow. To mitigate local bone-metal artifacts, bone segmentation was performed using a U-Net model, and segmentation accuracy was quantified using the Sørensen-Dice similarity coefficient. The U-Net model reproduced manual segmentations with high fidelity (average Dice = 0.94 ± 0.01). DVC accuracy and precision depended on the spatial resolution of strain measurement; at a DVC spatial resolution of 1.8 mm, strain estimates around the screw were reliable with low error (accuracy = 387 ± 110 µε; precision = 222 ± 82 µε). This study establishes the feasibility of a micro-CT-based DVC workflow and characterizes the strain measurement errors within trabecular bone surrounding pedicle screws using a zero-strain analysis. This workflow provides a foundation for future studies involving loaded tests, further optimization of segmentation to suppress artifacts, and validation across larger cohorts and implant designs.

title: Diagnostic performance of shuttle-mode myocardial CT late enhancement: Comparison with late gadolinium enhancement cardiovascular MR.
abstract: Objectives Although myocardial CT late enhancement (CT-LE) has been reported in various studies, its diagnostic performance using shuttle-mode dual-source CT has not been fully validated for detecting myocardial infarction (MI) and assessing its transmural extent against late gadolinium enhancement cardiovascular MR (LGE-CMR). This study aimed to evaluate the diagnostic performance of shuttle-mode myocardial CT-LE in detecting MI with LGE-CMR as a reference standard. Materials & methods This study included 56 patients with suspected or known coronary artery disease who underwent both comprehensive cardiac CT, including myocardial CT-LE, and LGE-CMR from a prospective, multicenter trial (AMPLIFiED). Sixteen myocardial segments per patient (excluding the apical cap based on AHA classification) were assessed. Segments were classified as having or not having MI; segments with MI were further categorized by transmural extent: <50%, 50-99%, or 100%. Two observers independently assessed myocardial CT-LE images. LGE-CMR findings were determined by consensus between two observers. Results In the segment-based analysis (n = 896), myocardial CT-LE showed a sensitivity of 97.6% and a positive predictive value (PPV) of 93.0%-94.1% for MI detection (specificity, 99.3%-99.4%; negative predictive value [NPV], 99.8%). Agreement for transmural extent was high (weighted kappa, 0.82-0.83). Inter-reader reproducibility for binary MI detection was excellent (agreement, 99.4%; kappa, 0.97). In an exploratory patient-level analysis based on 19 LGE-CMR-positive patients, sensitivity was 94.7% (95% confidence interval [CI], 74.0%-99.9%) for Observer A and 100% (95% CI, 82.4%-100%) for Observer B; the corresponding PPVs were 94.7% and 90.5%. Conclusion Shuttle-mode myocardial CT-LE demonstrated excellent agreement with LGE-CMR for the detection and transmural assessment of MI. Its high sensitivity for subendocardial MI supports its value as a reliable alternative to LGE-CMR.

title: Feasibility and Restenosis Predictors of Optical Frequency Domain Imaging-Guided Drug-Coated Balloon Treatment for Femoropopliteal Lesions.
abstract: Background The clinical utility of optical frequency domain imaging (OFDI) for guiding endovascular therapy in femoropopliteal lesions has not been established. Additionally, the prognostic value of OFDI findings during drug-coated balloon (DCB) treatment for femoropopliteal lesions has never been evaluated. Objectives This study aimed to clarify the feasibility of OFDI-guided DCB treatment and investigate the OFDI findings associated with restenosis after DCB treatment in femoropopliteal lesions. Methods This multicenter, prospective, observational study included patients with symptomatic, nonseverely calcified femoropopliteal lesions who underwent DCB treatment under OFDI guidance. Procedural success was defined as residual stenosis of less than 30% without flow compromise and without any procedural complications. The primary outcome was restenosis of the target lesion, defined as a peak systolic velocity ratio of ≥2.5, as measured by duplex ultrasound at rest or target lesion revascularization. Results A total of 202 lesions were initially enrolled, of which 35 (17.3%) were excluded primarily because of severe calcification or inadequate OFDI data. Among the 167 analyzable lesions included in the present analysis, the procedural success rate and 1-year freedom from restenosis were 91.6% and 85.5%, respectively. In the procedural OFDI findings, a calcified nodule in the target lesion (subdistribution hazard ratio: 3.25; 95% CI: 1.01-10.42; P = 0.048) was associated with restenosis. Conclusions OFDI-guided DCB treatment is feasible in selected femoropopliteal lesions. An OFDI-detected calcified nodule is associated with an increased risk of restenosis after DCB treatment for femoropopliteal lesions.

title: Exploratory structure-function associations in retinal vein occlusion-associated macular edema using deep learning-based quantification of OCT biomarkers and microperimetry.
abstract: Objective To investigate associations between disease-specific OCT biomarkers and pointwise retinal sensitivity (PWS) in retinal vein occlusion (RVO) derived from 2 microperimetry (MP) devices. Design Exploratory, prospective, cross-sectional study. Participants Twenty eyes of 20 patients with macular edema secondary to RVO. Methods Patients underwent spectral-domain OCT (Spectralis; Heidelberg Engineering) and 2 examinations with each MP device (MAIA2, iCare; MP-3, Nidek). Intraretinal fluid (IRF), subretinal fluid (SRF), and ellipsoid-zone thickness (EZT) were segmented using deep-learning-based algorithms; disorganisation of inner retinal layers (DRIL) and intraretinal hemorrhage were annotated manually. Co-registration of OCT volumes and MP grids enabled pointwise structure-function analyses. Mixed-effects models assessed the associations of biomarkers with PWS, pointwise EZT, and fixation stability (FS). Results Mean age was 66 ± 13 years, 13 patients were male, and 11 eyes had branch and 9 central RVO. Greater EZT was associated with greater PWS (+0.14 dB/µm), whereas greater IRF volume (-1.15 dB/nL) and the presence of SRF (-2.35 dB), DRIL (-3.29 dB), and hemorrhage (-9.33 dB) were associated with lower PWS (all P < 0.001). Greater IRF volume (-0.46 µm/nL) and SRF presence (-6.76 µm) were associated with lower pointwise EZT (both P < 0.001). Conclusions IRF, SRF, hemorrhage, DRIL, and EZT showed associations with PWS, whereas IRF and SRF were associated with lower EZT in RVO. MP may improve understanding of structure-function associations in RVO.

title: Multimodality Cardiovascular Imaging in the Evaluation of Cardiac Sarcoidosis.
abstract: Cardiac sarcoidosis (CS) is a granulomatous disease associated with increased cardiovascular risk, including symptomatic high-grade atrioventricular block, ventricular arrhythmia, heart failure, and sudden cardiac death. Diagnosis can be challenging and requires a high index of suspicion. Although endomyocardial biopsy demonstrating noncaseating granulomas can diagnose CS with high specificity, sampling error leads to low sensitivity. CS is typically diagnosed using a combination of clinical criteria and advanced cardiac imaging, such as cardiac magnetic resonance and positron emission tomography, which can detect myocardial inflammation and fibrosis seen in CS. Recent advances in cardiac magnetic resonance and positron emission tomography have not only substantially improved the diagnosis of CS, but have also improved prognostic assessment, monitoring of treatment response, and guidance of other clinical decision-making, such as immunosuppressive and device therapy. Advanced cardiac imaging has been incorporated into recent international guidelines on inflammatory heart disease, and holds great promise to reshape contemporary clinical care for patients with CS.

title: Optimizing Echocardiographic Evaluation of Chronic Mitral Regurgitation: Comparison With Cardiac Magnetic Resonance Imaging and Implications for Guideline Recommendations.
abstract: Background The ASE (American Society of Echocardiography) guidelines recommend the presence of at least 4 specific criteria to confirm a diagnosis of definite severe mitral regurgitation (MR). However, the performance of these criteria, particularly when <4 are present, remains unclear. Objectives This study aims to evaluate and optimize the ASE native MR guidelines by comparing them with quantitative cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR), considered the reference standard for MR assessment. Methods In this prospective study, 177 patients underwent near-simultaneous CMR and transthoracic echocardiography for the assessment of MR. MR severity was classified using a 4-grade scale based on CMR-derived regurgitant volume, which was calculated as the difference between total left ventricular (LV) stroke volume and aortic forward flow. MR severity was similarly graded using the ASE algorithm, with quantification performed when necessary, by averaging the regurgitant volume from 3 methods: 1) the proximal isovelocity surface area method; 2) the biplane LV volumetric method; and 3) the mitral valve volumetric method. Results The study cohort had a median age of 61.7 years, with 55% being men. Primary MR was the predominant pathology (73% of patients), with 42% having mitral valve prolapse and 25% presenting with flail leaflets. There was exact agreement between transthoracic echocardiography and CMR MR grading in 51% of cases, whereas agreement within 1 grade was observed in 89%. Patients who met any of the ASE severe MR criteria were predominantly classified as having grades 3 to 4 MR by CMR. The following ASE parameters demonstrated high specificity for identifying grade 4 MR by CMR: pulmonary vein systolic flow reversal (specificity 88%), enlarged LV with normal systolic function (specificity 85%), proximal isovelocity surface area radius ≥1.0 cm (specificity 83%), and vena contracta width ≥0.7 cm (specificity 80%). Combining color Doppler with either pulmonary vein systolic reversal or enlarged LV with normal function resulted in 91%-95% specificity for severe MR. Importantly, reliance on fewer ASE criteria reduced the need for quantification from 86% (4 criteria) to 73% (3 criteria) and 59% (2 criteria), thereby enhancing diagnostic efficiency. Conclusions Certain ASE criteria, especially when used in combination, are highly specific for diagnosing severe MR, even when <4 criteria are present. This study suggests that in many cases, the reliance on extensive quantification may be reduced, streamlining the diagnostic process and improving clinical workflow.

title: Adverse Remodeling and Fibrosis Predict Outcomes in Excessive Trabeculation of the Left Ventricle: A Multiparametric CMR Risk Score.
abstract: Background Excessive trabeculation of the left ventricle (ETLV) is a heterogeneous and controversial phenotype that overlaps with both physiological remodeling and cardiomyopathy. Objectives This study sought to develop and validate a cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR)-based model to predict major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) and to assess the incremental prognostic value of trabeculation metrics. Methods In this international retrospective study, 589 patients with ETLV across 17 centers underwent core-laboratory CMR analysis. The composite MACE endpoint included heart failure, ventricular arrhythmia, systemic embolism, or all-cause death. A prediction model was derived from morphofunctional CMR parameters and validated in an independent cohort. The incremental value of trabeculation indices was then assessed. Outcomes were further compared with a propensity-matched cohort of 197 patients with dilated cardiomyopathy. Results Mean age was 43 ± 18 years, 43% were women, mean left ventricular (LV) ejection fraction was 48% ± 14%, and 12% had late gadolinium enhancement (LGE). Over a median follow-up of 3.6 years, 121 (21%) patients experienced MACE. A model including indexed LV end-diastolic volume, LV global longitudinal strain, and LGE extent demonstrated moderate prognostic performance (C-statistic 0.77 in derivation; 0.70 in validation) and calibration. Addition of trabeculated mass percentage (TM%) modestly improved discrimination (C-statistic 0.79 in derivation, P = 0.012; 0.72 in validation); an exploratory TM% ≥28% identified higher-risk patients. However, TM% was not predictive among individuals with normal indexed LV end-diastolic volume, preserved LV global longitudinal strain, and minimal LGE, who exhibited excellent outcomes. Prognosis was comparable in propensity-matched ETLV and dilated cardiomyopathy cohorts (P = 0.557). Conclusions CMR-based risk stratification in ETLV is primarily driven by adverse LV remodeling and fibrosis, whereas trabeculation indices provide only modest incremental prognostic value. In the absence of high-risk imaging features, ETLV likely represents a benign morphologic trait. This pragmatic multiparametric CMR score may support clinical decision-making in this debated phenotype.

title: Identifying the High-Risk Arrhythmic Mitral Valve Prolapse Phenotype by Imaging.
abstract: Within arrhythmogenic mitral valve prolapse (AMVP), a distinct subset of mitral valve prolapse (MVP), there is a small group that carries a higher risk of malignant ventricular arrhythmias and sudden cardiac death called malignant MVP. The malignant MVP phenotype is over-represented in young women with unexplained sudden cardiac death on autopsy. AMVP is defined by myxomatous, often bileaflet MVP with mitral annular disjunction, abnormal valvular-myocardial mechanics, complex ventricular ectopy, and nonsustained ventricular tachycardia. Excessive mechanical force from systolic annular expansion, papillary muscle traction, and basal inferolateral "curling" promotes focal replacement and diffuse interstitial fibrosis, creating an arrhythmogenic substrate. Premature ventricular contractions act as triggers, whereas autonomic modulation influences the timing of ventricular arrhythmia initiation and progression to ventricular fibrillation or sustained monomorphic ventricular tachycardia. Baseline evaluation with an electrocardiogram and transthoracic echocardiography is necessary to identify AMVP, exclude severe mitral regurgitation, and identify high-risk markers. If no premature ventricular contractions are found on a resting electrocardiogram, exercise stress testing and extended rhythm monitoring can help bring out ventricular premature contractions, which are triggers of ventricular arrhythmias. Cardiac magnetic resonance provides incremental prognostic value with late gadolinium enhancement reflecting replacement fibrosis and T1 mapping identifying diffuse fibrosis, even in those with no late gadolinium enhancement. Machine-learning analysis may further refine risk stratification by integrating high-risk features such as mitral annular disjunction, fibrosis extent, and location that outperform symptom-based assessment. As transcatheter and surgical mitral interventions expand, accurate phenotyping of AMVP is increasingly important, as hemodynamic correction of mitral regurgitation alone does not eliminate the underlying arrhythmogenic substrate. Comprehensive multimodality imaging and integrated rhythm assessment are therefore central to individualized risk stratification and management in this vulnerable population.

title: Oral peri-implant tissue as a neoplastic bed: a systematic review of clinicopathology, pathogenesis, and survival outcomes.
abstract: Background Peri-implant neoplasia (PIN) is a descriptive term introduced in this review to categorize neoplasms present adjacent to dental implants. Understanding its clinicopathological spectrum and pathogenesis is essential for timely diagnosis and management. Objective This systematic review evaluated evidence on the clinicopathological features, risk factors, pathogenetic mechanisms, and survival outcomes of peri-implant neoplasia. Methods Following PRISMA guidelines (PROSPERO ID: CRD42024586140), a systematic search of PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science identified studies published until December 2025. Eligible studies included case reports, case series, and cross-sectional studies with histopathologically confirmed peri-implant neoplasia. Extracted data included demographics, clinical presentation, risk factors, histopathology, treatment, and outcomes. Risk of bias was assessed using Joanna Briggs Institute checklists, and pooled survival analysis was performed using Kaplan-Meier curves. Results Fifty-six studies involving 187 patients were included. Malignant epithelial neoplasms accounted for 92.3% of lesions, with oral squamous cell carcinoma predominating. The mean patient age was 66.3 years, with a slight female predominance. The mandible was the most common implant and lesion site, and most cases occurred within 1-5 years post-implantation. Clinical misdiagnosis as peri-implantitis occurred in 54% of cases. Factors associated with recurrence or death included prior OPMD/malignancy, radiographic bone loss, and treatment modality. Kaplan-Meier analysis showed mean survival time of 64.1 months (95% CI: 46.8-81.4), with poorer outcomes for sarcoma and metastasis. Conclusions Peri-implant neoplasia is predominantly malignant and often mimics peri-implantitis. Clinicians should promptly biopsy non-healing peri-implant lesions and ensure close surveillance in high-risk patients.

title: Translational and rotational accuracy of the mandibular proximal segment after virtual surgical planning-guided bilateral sagittal split ramus osteotomy in skeletal Class III patients.
abstract: Previous studies on proximal segment accuracy after bilateral sagittal split ramus osteotomy have mainly focused on condylar position. This retrospective cohort study evaluated landmark-specific and direction-sensitive proximal segment discrepancies relative to the virtual surgical plan in 108 skeletal Class III patients who underwent virtual surgical planning-guided orthognathic surgery with bilateral sagittal split ramus osteotomy. Postoperative cone-beam computed tomography data obtained within 1 week after surgery were superimposed on the planned dataset. Five landmarks were evaluated on each proximal segment: condyle, coronoid process, anterior ramus, posterior ramus, and cutting edge. Translational discrepancies were assessed using signed X-, Y-, and Z-axis differences and three-dimensional (3D) discrepancies, and signed angular discrepancies in pitch, roll, and yaw were analyzed. Condylar landmarks showed relatively small 3D discrepancies, whereas larger discrepancies were observed at the posterior ramus and cutting edge landmarks, resulting in an overall 3D discrepancy of 1.94 ± 0.54 mm. Landmark-specific signed analysis demonstrated medial convergence of the coronoid processes, lateral deviation of the posterior ramus landmarks, and anterior deviation of the anterior ramus, posterior ramus, and cutting edge landmarks. These findings suggest that condylar accuracy alone may underestimate residual proximal segment discrepancy and support careful intraoperative assessment of passive proximal segment seating when proximal-distal segment interference is suspected.

title: Technical Note - A patient-specific implant for orbital wall reconstruction with infraorbital rim extension: Accuracy and proof-of-principle evaluation of an "one-fit-only" design.
abstract: Accurate intraoperative positioning of patient-specific implants (PSI) in orbital wall reconstruction remains challenging due to residual translational and rotational freedom. The aim of this proof-of-principle study was to introduce an orbital PSI design refinement incorporating infraorbital rim extensions based on the "one-fit-only" principle and to evaluate its positioning accuracy using a comprehensive 3D analysis. A patient with an unilateral and isolated left-sided orbital floor fracture underwent primary orbital reconstruction in a fully digital 3D workflow using a CAD/CAM-manufactured titanium PSI with three infraorbital rim extensions. Virtual surgical planning (VSP) was performed based on high-resolution computed tomography (CT). Accuracy assessment was performed using intraoperative cone beam computed tomography (CBCT) by superimposing the planned and achieved implant positions and analyzing them with open-source software 3D Slicer. Positioning accuracy was quantified using the Dice similarity coefficient (DSC), Hausdorff distance (HD), mean surface distance (MSD), rotational deviation (RD) and distance between centers (DBC). The PSI demonstrated high positional accuracy with low translational and rotational deviations. MSD was 0.63 mm and mean HD was 0.23 mm (maximum 0.79 mm) indicating close geometric congruence without clinically relevant focal malpositioning. Total RD was 1.53° and global translational deviation was 0.58 mm with submillimetric axis-specific components. At extended follow-up (4 months postoperatively), no implant-related complications and stable ophthalmological outcomes were observed. The presented orbital PSI design with infraorbital rim extensions demonstrates technical feasibility of accurate intraoperative positioning within a fully digital workflow. The proposed 3D outcome measures provide a framework for objective assessment of PSI positioning accuracy. Due to the single-case design, no conclusions can be drawn regarding workflow simplification, learning curve or equivalence to other techniques such as intraoperative navigation. This study should be interpreted as a proof-of-principle technical note based on a single-case.

A patient with an unilateral and isolated left-sided orbital floor fracture underwent primary orbital reconstruction in a fully digital 3D workflow using a CAD/CAM-manufactured titanium PSI with three infraorbital rim extensions. Virtual surgical planning (VSP) was performed based on high-resolution computed tomography (CT). Accuracy assessment was performed using intraoperative cone beam computed tomography (CBCT) by superimposing the planned and achieved implant positions and analyzing them with open-source software 3D Slicer. Positioning accuracy was quantified using the Dice similarity coefficient (DSC), Hausdorff distance (HD), mean surface distance (MSD), rotational deviation (RD) and distance between centers (DBC). The PSI demonstrated high positional accuracy with low translational and rotational deviations. MSD was 0.63 mm and mean HD was 0.23 mm (maximum 0.79 mm) indicating close geometric congruence without clinically relevant focal malpositioning. Total RD was 1.53° and global translational deviation was 0.58 mm with submillimetric axis-specific components. At extended follow-up (4 months postoperatively), no implant-related complications and stable ophthalmological outcomes were observed. The presented orbital PSI design with infraorbital rim extensions demonstrates technical feasibility of accurate intraoperative positioning within a fully digital workflow. The proposed 3D outcome measures provide a framework for objective assessment of PSI positioning accuracy. Due to the single-case design, no conclusions can be drawn regarding workflow simplification, learning curve or equivalence to other techniques such as intraoperative navigation. This study should be interpreted as a proof-of-principle technical note based on a single-case.

title: Orbital soft-tissue remodeling after bony decompression in thyroid-associated orbitopathy: a CT-based analysis of extraocular muscles volume.
abstract: The study evaluated changes in extraocular muscles (EOMs) following orbital decompression in patients with thyroid-associated orbitopathy (TAO) using computed tomography (CT)-based volumetric analysis. Patients who underwent orbital decompression with available preoperative and postoperative orbital CT scans were retrospectively reviewed. Decompression procedures were classified as medial, inferomedial, balanced, or three-wall decompression. Volumes of individual EOMs were calculated from coronal CT images, and temporal changes were assessed by locally estimated scatterplot smoothing regression, with associated clinical factors analyzed using multivariate linear regression. A total of 307 orbits from 171 patients were analyzed. Medial rectus muscle volume increased significantly across all surgical groups, while superior rectus volume decreased after three-wall decompression and inferior rectus volume decreased following medial and balanced decompression. EOM volumetric changes stabilized approximately 150 days postoperatively. Female sex, prior high-dose intravenous (IV) steroid therapy, and prolonged duration of TAO were independently associated with increased postoperative EOM volume, whereas smoking showed a borderline association. These findings indicate that orbital decompression induces distinct and time-dependent EOM volumetric changes, reflecting postoperative soft-tissue remodeling influenced by specific clinical factors.

title: Combining imaging strategies with physiologically-based pharmacokinetic modeling to improve precision dosing & drug delivery in brain tumors.
abstract: Small molecule targeted therapies frequently fail to control brain metastases and primary brain tumors even when systemic exposure reaches toxicity-limiting levels. Systemic exposure-response relationships are often absent, which is well documented for tyrosine kinase inhibitors. Target-site information is therefore needed, since the concentration reached in the tumor is determined not by plasma exposure, but by passive and active transport across the blood-brain barrier and by intratumoral heterogeneity. Physiologically-based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) modeling provides the mechanistic framework to describe this. Models built solely on in vitro-to-in vivo extrapolation of permeability and transport have repeatedly required correction factors derived from rodent data, and their evaluation in humans still depends on invasive sampling or microdialysis. Microdialysis performs poorly for lipophilic, highly protein-bound drugs. We argue that quantitative imaging can supply the missing in vivo input. In a hybrid strategy, in vitro-derived transport parameters serve as the starting point, while blood-brain barrier influx and efflux are recalibrated on positron emission tomography (PET) microdose measurements in patients. This could lead to improved prediction of brain concentrations at therapeutic doses and allows simulated target-site exposure to be weighed against in vitro potency for compound and dose selection. Beyond whole-brain averages, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) can provide permeability and perfusion parameters longitudinally and in larger cohorts, whereas mass spectrometry imaging (MSI) techniques can map intratumoral heterogeneity in drug distribution in the tumor microenvironment and identify potential sanctuary sites. We map each modality onto the specific PBPK parameters it can inform, and argue that imaging-informed, spatially resolved PBPK is a realistic route toward model-informed precision dosing in neuro-oncology.

title: Patient-specific pharmacokinetics of intratumoral cisplatin track pathologic necrosis in early-stage lung cancer.
abstract: Intratumoral injection of cisplatin into lung cancer is feasible and can increase local drug exposure while reducing systemic toxicity. However, its success relies on achieving sufficient drug exposure to the tumor, which has not been quantitatively evaluated in a clinical setting. In the context of a Phase I clinical trial of intratumoral cisplatin injections into resectable lung tumors via robotic bronchoscopy (N = 6), we developed a quantitative framework to assess delivery effectiveness and long-term cisplatin exposure in tumors. Initial injectate retention was estimated using a novel image analytics pipeline based on intraoperative cone-beam computed tomography scans, by assuming that emerging high-attenuation regions are due to injectate deposition. Long-term drug exposure was estimated using a novel pharmacokinetic model tailored for intratumoral drug delivery and informed by sequential venous blood draws following the injections. The area under the platinum concentration curve in the tumor compartment at t = 3-21 h and platinum concentration in the tumor compartment (t = 3-6 h), estimated from the fitted pharmacokinetic model, showed a strong monotonic association with percentage pathological necrosis assessed post-resection by three independent, blinded pathologists (Spearman's ρ = 0.93, 95% bootstrap CI 0.67-1.00, unadjusted exact p = 0.033), which was not statistically significant when corrected for multiple comparisons (adjusted p = 0.17). No other pharmacokinetic variable correlated was significantly correlated with necrosis or other pathological response metrics prior to multiple comparison correction. This result aligns with the known time-concentration dependency of cisplatin action in tumor. Further studies will be needed to evaluate this observation for repeatability and clinical relevance. Our approach provides a framework for estimating intratumoral drug exposure in clinical settings, which may help with the interpretation of clinical trial outcomes and future evaluation of injection strategies.

title: Lung ultrasound findings in ARDS based on the 2023 global definition: Characteristics and prognostic value of different LUS scores.
abstract: Objective The primary objective was to describe the distribution characteristics of lung ultrasound (LUS) findings in patients meeting the 2023 global definition of acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS). The secondary, exploratory aim was to evaluate the prognostic association of LUS scores with 28-day mortality. Methods This prospective study included 224 patients admitted to the ICU/EICU of Ningxia Medical University General Hospital from January to September 2025. LUS signs (regional/total scores, pleural line abnormalities) were collected within 24 h of admission. Prognostic value was assessed using ROC curve analysis. Results The 28-day mortality rate was 29.46% (66/224). Total LUS aeration score correlated positively with pleural line abnormalities (r = 0.505, P < 0.001). Survivors showed higher proportions of A-lines and normal pleural lines, while non-survivors had more fused B-lines. Pleural line abnormalities showed the strongest exploratory association with 28-day mortality (AUC = 0.617, 95% CI: 0.550-0.681, P = 0.008). Conclusion Early LUS signs differ significantly between survivors and non-survivors among patients meeting the 2023 ARDS definition. Pleural line abnormalities showed an exploratory association with 28-day mortality, suggesting potential value for bedside risk stratification.This study was registered with the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (Registration Number:ChiCTR2600117533).

title: A Novel AI-Assisted 3D Hybrid Soft and Hard Tissue Model for Peri-implant Diagnosis and Treatment Planning: A Proof-of-Concept Study of Immediate Implant Planning in the Anterior Maxilla.
abstract: Objectives Immediate implant placement in the maxillary esthetic zone requires precise three-dimensional (3D) positioning within compromised sockets. Conventional planning platforms integrate cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) and intraoral scanning (IOS) data but exclude critical parameters such as gingival phenotype and thickness. This study aimed to develop and evaluate a novel patient-specific virtual 3D peri-implant model (PIM) that converts AI-segmented dental hard- and soft-tissue data into a realistic 3D soft- and hard-tissue model for peri-implant diagnosis and treatment planning, fusing AI-segmented CBCT, IOS, and gingival tissue data into a single implant planning framework. Methods Thirty patients requiring tooth extraction and immediate implant placement of a maxillary anterior tooth were retrospectively included. CBCT and IOS datasets were processed through an AI-driven platform to segment teeth, alveolar bone, gingiva, and surrounding structures, which were then integrated into a patient-specific 3D virtual model. Virtual tooth removal created a simulated post-extraction socket, allowing prosthetically driven implant planning. Three specialist clinicians from oral surgery, prosthodontics, and periodontics independently performed implant planning under two conditions: conventional CBCT and IOS alone, and PIM-assisted planning. Inter-operator variability and agreement were evaluated across coronal, apical, and angular dimensions using continuous and ordinal outcome measures. Results PIM workflow feasibility (successful model generation and implant planning) was 100% (30/30 cases). PIM was associated with lower mean inter-operator deviations for apical (Holm-adjusted p = .009) and angular positioning (Holm-adjusted p < .001), but not coronal positioning (Holm-adjusted p = .10). Major angular deviations decreased from 40.0% to 6.7% of implants (Holm-adjusted p = .028), with no categorical difference for coronal or apical deviation. Conclusion Converting AI-segmented dental hard- and soft-tissue data into a realistic hybrid 3D tissue model was feasible and significantly reduced mean apical and angular inter-operator deviations, with the ordinal benefit most evident for angular positioning. These findings support further prospective evaluation of the PIM workflow. Clinical significance By fusing bony and gingival characteristics into a single realistic 3D digital tissue model, PIM may support more informed decisions regarding implant position, grafting, abutment selection, emergence profile design, and restorative planning before surgery.

title: Artificial intelligence for radiographic assessment and severity grading of peri-implant marginal bone loss: A systematic review and methodological appraisal.
abstract: Objectives To systematically evaluate the diagnostic performance, methodological quality, reporting transparency, and descriptive translational staging of Artificial Intelligence (AI) models applied to dental imaging for the radiographic assessment and severity grading of peri-implant marginal bone loss. Study selection The review was conducted according to PRISMA 2020 and PRISMA-DTA. PubMed (MEDLINE), Scopus, Web of Science, and Embase were searched without date restrictions. Ten studies met the eligibility criteria. Results Nine studies used retrospective single-center designs, and one included multicenter data without independent external validation. AI tasks included landmark detection, quantitative measurement, segmentation, bone-loss detection, and severity grading. Reported performance was generally favorable but highly task-specific. Implant detection reached an average precision of approximately 0.99 in one study, whereas average precision for marginal bone-loss lesion detection was 0.47. Implant segmentation achieved a Dice similarity coefficient of 0.986, while reported F1-scores reached 97.1%. Sensitivity and specificity were reported in only a subset of diagnostic evaluations and varied according to the unit of analysis. Quantitatively interpretable measurement-error reporting was limited; only one study reported deviations that could be converted to approximately 0.17 mm using the study-specific image calibration. No study provided a complete set of clinically interpretable absolute marginal bone-loss measurement-agreement outcomes in millimetres. Substantial heterogeneity was observed in annotation protocols, validation strategies, dataset partitioning, task definitions, and performance reporting. No study performed prospective evaluation or independent external multicenter validation. Conclusions Current AI systems show promising technical capability for radiographic assessment of peri-implant marginal bone loss. However, the evidence remains limited by retrospective study designs, incomplete reproducibility, lack of external validation, and uncertain clinical generalizability. Clinical relevance The clinical utility of AI as an adjunctive tool for radiographic interpretation or longitudinal monitoring was not tested in the included studies and remains to be established through prospective evaluation, external validation, and direct assessment of clinician-AI interaction.
