title: Multi-omics liquid biopsy for leptomeningeal metastases in lung cancer: from molecular mechanisms to precision diagnosis and treatment.
abstract: Lung cancer remains the leading cause of cancer-related deaths worldwide. Leptomeningeal metastasis (LM), a serious complication of advanced lung cancer, poses significant challenges in both clinical diagnosis and treatment monitoring, and is associated with a poor prognosis. Conventional diagnostic methods include magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) cytology; however, their sensitivity is limited, particularly in the early stages of the disease. Against this backdrop, liquid biopsy has emerged as a minimally invasive and practical approach for molecular assessment and longitudinal monitoring of LM. Recent studies have reported that, in selected cohorts of patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) and LM, CSF-derived circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) detects driver and resistance-associated alterations more frequently than paired plasma, while epithelial cell adhesion molecule (EpCAM)-based CSF circulating tumor cell (CTC) assays have reported sensitivities of 76%-100% and specificities of 84%-100%, compared with a first-lumbar-puncture sensitivity of 44%-67% for conventional CSF cytology. These performance estimates should be interpreted in the context of selected cohorts and heterogeneous reference frameworks. Furthermore, cerebrospinal fluid circulating tumor cell (CSF-CTC) burden holds prognostic value, with higher CTC levels associated with poorer survival outcomes. This review summarizes recent advances in liquid biopsy biomarkers including ctDNA, DNA methylation, microRNA (miRNA), proteins, and circulating tumor cells (CTCs), focusing on their applications in the diagnosis, treatment monitoring, and prognostic assessment of lung cancer-associated LM, and provides a comparative discussion of liquid biopsy based on plasma and cerebrospinal fluid specimens. It further explores the potential, current challenges, and directions for clinical translation of multi-omics integration in the personalized management of LM.

title: Serum extracellular vesicle-associated SNORD54 adds diagnostic information to CEA and CYFRA21-1 in non-small cell lung cancer: a case-control development study.
abstract: Background Blood-based biomarkers that complement established serum markers may improve molecular classification of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). We evaluated whether SNORD54 and SNORD41 measured in a serum extracellular vesicle (EV)-enriched fraction provided incremental discrimination beyond carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA) and cytokeratin 19 fragment 21-1 (CYFRA21-1). Methods This single-center case-control biomarker-development study included serum samples from patients with histologically or cytologically confirmed NSCLC and contemporaneous healthy controls. Supporting expression evidence was assessed in paired lung adenocarcinoma and lung squamous cell carcinoma datasets and in 48 paired formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded NSCLC specimens. Serum analyses included gene-specific cohorts and a common complete-case cohort with SNORD54, SNORD41, CEA, and CYFRA21-1 measurements. Logistic regression models were compared using paired DeLong tests. Model parsimony, adjustment for age, sex, and smoking, locked Stage I-II and Stage I subgroup analyses, U6-normalization sensitivity analyses, and 2000-resample bootstrap internal validation were performed. Results The complete-case cohort comprised 98 patients with NSCLC and 79 healthy controls. Adding SNORD54 to CEA and CYFRA21-1 increased the AUC from 0.851(95% confidence interval [CI], 0.795-0.907) to 0.951 (95% CI, 0.920-0.982; ΔAUC, 0.100; 95% CI, 0.050-0.150; P < 0.001). At the development-derived cutoff, the three-marker model achieved 85.7% sensitivity and 94.9% specificity. SNORD41 did not improve the SNORD54-containing model (ΔAUC, 0.0003; P = 0.480; likelihood-ratio P = 0.953) and increased both Akaike and Bayesian information criteria. With coefficients and the cutoff fixed from the overall cohort, the three-marker model achieved AUCs of 0.904 (95% CI, 0.843-0.964) for Stage I-II disease and 0.882 (95% CI, 0.804-0.960) for Stage I disease. SNORD54 remained informative after adjustment for age, sex, and smoking. The optimism-corrected AUC was 0.948. U6 Ct values differed between diagnostic groups; associations of both snoRNAs with case status persisted in sensitivity models accounting for U6 Ct. Conclusions SNORD54 measured in a serum EV-enriched fraction provided incremental discrimination beyond CEA and CYFRA21-1 in this NSCLC case-control cohort. The parsimonious SNORD54 + CEA + CYFRA21-1 model retained discrimination in locked early-stage subgroup analyses and showed limited apparent optimism after bootstrap correction. Independent validation in cohorts that include benign pulmonary nodules and other relevant lung diseases, together with standardized EV processing and validated RNA normalization, will define the clinical transportability of this three-marker panel.

Logistic regression models were compared using paired DeLong tests. The complete-case cohort comprised 98 patients with NSCLC and 79 healthy controls. Adding SNORD54 to CEA and CYFRA21-1 increased the AUC from 0.851(95% confidence interval [CI], 0.795-0.907) to 0.951 (95% CI, 0.920-0.982; ΔAUC, 0.100; 95% CI, 0.050-0.150; P < 0.001). SNORD41 did not improve the SNORD54-containing model (ΔAUC, 0.0003; P = 0.480; likelihood-ratio P = 0.953) and increased both Akaike and Bayesian information criteria. With coefficients and the cutoff fixed from the overall cohort, the three-marker model achieved AUCs of 0.904 (95% CI, 0.843-0.964) for Stage I-II disease and 0.882 (95% CI, 0.804-0.960) for Stage I disease. SNORD54 measured in a serum EV-enriched fraction provided incremental discrimination beyond CEA and CYFRA21-1 in this NSCLC case-control cohort. The parsimonious SNORD54 + CEA + CYFRA21-1 model retained discrimination in locked early-stage subgroup analyses and showed limited apparent optimism after bootstrap correction. Independent validation in cohorts that include benign pulmonary nodules and other relevant lung diseases, together with standardized EV processing and validated RNA normalization, will define the clinical transportability of this three-marker panel.

title: Advanced neuroimaging in rare diseases: The paradigm of quantification in the era of personalized medicine.
abstract: Rare diseases frequently involve the central nervous system, posing significant diagnostic and monitoring challenges. Recent advances in Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) and neuroradiology have expanded the tools available for RD assessment, encompassing improvements in image acquisition, postprocessing techniques, and functional MRI sequences. Advanced postprocessing methods allow radiologists to derive additional quantitative information from conventional morphological images, including the segmentation and volumetric analysis of brain structures such as gray matter. Functional MRI techniques, such as Diffusion Weighted Imaging, Perfusion Weighted Imaging, or Magnetic Resonance Spectroscopy, further contribute objective metrics reflecting underlying pathophysiological processes, including water diffusion and tissue perfusion. Within the framework of personalized medicine, integrating these advanced neuroimaging approaches may improve diagnostic precision and support treatment monitoring, follow-up, and disease surveillance. This review highlights the application of advanced neuroimaging tools across a range of clinical scenarios relevant to rare diseases, including cranial and structural abnormalities, white matter disorders, tumor assessment, and vascular conditions.

title: A clinical evaluation of spiral 4DCT and intelligent 4DCT sequence scanning.
abstract: Accurate 4DCT imaging is essential for radiotherapy planning but is often degraded by breathing irregularities. Phantom studies show that intelligent four-dimensional computed tomography (Direct i4D) sequence scanning can significantly reduce artifacts related to breathing irregularity compared to traditional spiral 4DCT. Direct i4D is a sequence-based acquisition mode in which beam-on time is adapted in real time to an individual patient's breathing pattern to optimize projection data coverage. In this study, we compared Direct i4D and spiral 4DCT scan image quality between Direct i4D and spiral 4DCT in a paired design, with both scans acquired for the same patient during a single simulation session. Spiral 4DCT and Direct i4D scans from 33 patients with pre-identified irregular breathing patterns were collected retrospectively. Breathing irregularities included variations in amplitude, frequency, or both. Spiral 4DCT scans were used for motion evaluation, while the Direct i4D scans were acquired for treatment planning. To compare the internal target volume (ITV) on both 4DCT datasets, a radiation oncologist manually contoured all ITVs de novo. Residual sorting artifacts were visually evaluated and scored by a radiation oncologist and medical physicist on a scale of 1 to 5 (where higher scores indicate lower presence of artifacts and better image quality). Visual evaluation of 4DCT phases showed that 36% of spiral 4DCT and 3% of Direct i4D scans would require resimulation. Meanwhile, 18% and of spiral 4DCT and 27% of Direct i4D scans were artifact-free (p-value < 0.1). The ITV comparison between the 2 4DCT techniques revealed mean and standard deviation (STD) Dice similarity coefficients of 0.59 and 0.18, respectively. ITV mean CT value difference varies between 0.80 HU and 158.41 HU (Mean ± STD: 39.41HU ± 40.02 HU). Real-time adaptation of the scan time and rebinning by Direct i4D enhanced the image quality for individual 4DCT phases. Irregular breathing patterns can degrade spiral 4DCT image quality and tumor delineation. The novel Direct i4D technique provides a reliable solution to reduce such artifacts significantly.

title: Mind the Gap: A survey of chronic wound datasets, methods, and clinical translation.
abstract: Chronic wounds, including diabetic foot ulcers, venous ulcers, arterial ulcers and pressure ulcers, represent a growing global health challenge with significant morbidity, mortality, and economic burden. Advancements in medical image analysis have shown promise in automating wound detection, segmentation, and measurement. However, translation of these research advances into clinical practice through mobile applications remains limited. This survey presents systematic analysis of the relationship between chronic wound datasets, deep learning methods, and mobile wound assessment applications. We analyse 20 datasets (14 public/partially public and 6 private), including iterative challenge datasets that extend image pool through synthetic augmentation. We review 50 deep learning methods spanning encoder-decoder architectures to self-supervised learning approaches, and evaluate 13 mobile applications (commercially deployed clinical tools and research prototypes). We examine the alignment between publicly available chronic wound datasets and the documented capabilities of mobile wound assessment mobile applications. Our analysis reveals critical misalignments between datasets, algorithms and mobile applications. Existing datasets are typically designed for algorithm benchmarking rather than clinical deployment, and therefore lack standardised acquisition protocols, scale calibration markers, depth information, detailed tissue composition annotations, and representation of diverse skin types. Conversely, reviewed mobile applications report capabilities, including automatic tissue classification, calibrated wound measurement and depth estimation, for which publicly available data is insufficient. We map documented dataset characteristics to capabilities reported among reviewed mobile applications, identify unresolved methodological challenges, and outline key priorities for the field. Based on these insights, we propose actionable recommendations for developing clinically translatable computer vision system for wound assessment. This survey is intended to serve as a reference for researchers and practitioners seeking to bridge the gap between medical imaging methodologies and practical demands of clinical wound care.

title: A self-navigated framework for motion detection and spoke-reordering musculoskeletal dynamic reconstruction in 3D radial MRI.
abstract: Motion remains a major challenge and active research focus in MRI, as both involuntary (e.g., head movement) and voluntary (e.g., joint motion) motion can degrade image quality or, alternatively, provide opportunities for dynamic assessment. Existing motion sensing approaches - such as external tracking or navigator sequences - often require additional hardware, increase SAR, or necessitate sequence modifications, thereby limiting clinical flexibility. In this work, we propose a self-navigated motion sensing framework for 3D radial MRI. Motion surrogates are first extracted directly from multi-coil k-space data. A sliding-window summation is then applied to enhance robustness, followed by a second principal component (PC2)-based strategy to derive a 1D motion-sensitive signal that reflects subject position over time. Beyond conventional head motion correction, we demonstrate the utility of the proposed framework in improving dynamic 4D MRI of the ankle and knee under both stepwise and continuous motion protocols. By reordering spokes based on motion-derived position rather than acquisition time, the method enables motion-resolved reconstructions with improved anatomical clarity. Overall, this approach facilitates efficient motion detection and supports broader adoption of motion-aware dynamic MRI. The source code of this framework is available at https://github.com/EricLin1993/SpEMSK.

title: A unified and domain-robust framework enables controllable multimodal brain MRI synthesis.
abstract: Multimodal magnetic resonance image (MRI) synthesis can shorten examinations, reduce cost, and furnish contrasts that are difficult or impossible to acquire, but current models remain hard to control and brittle to shifts in scanner, protocol, and pathology. We present a unified, domain-robust synthesis framework that modulates spatial carriers with physically informed, domain-stable statistical guidance. A balanced soft-plus-hard conditioning scheme enables a single model to perform diverse contrast mapping, while allowing smooth user adjustment of contrast weighting. Evaluated on 991 test subjects from five public and three private datasets spanning cross-dataset, cross-protocol, and related cross-pathology scenarios, our approach matches or outperforms advanced baselines for both in-domain synthesis and inference under unseen domains without finetuning. Clinician Turing test and downstream glioma grading experiments further indicate realistic appearance, preservation of pathology-relevant information, and potential practical value under clinically heterogeneous conditions. By jointly delivering controllability, robustness to real-world variability, and physically informed, domain-stable guidance within one architecture, this work advances MRI synthesis toward deployment in heterogeneous clinical environments.

title: Performance uncertainty in medical image analysis: A large-scale investigation of confidence intervals.
abstract: Performance uncertainty quantification is essential for reliable validation and eventual clinical translation of medical imaging artificial intelligence (AI). Confidence intervals (CIs) play a central role in this process by indicating how precise a reported performance estimate is. Yet, due to the limited amount of work examining CI behavior in medical imaging, the community remains largely unaware of how many diverse CI methods exist and how they behave in specific settings. The purpose of this study is to close this gap. To this end, we conducted a large-scale empirical analysis across a total of 24 segmentation and classification tasks, using 19 trained models per task group, a broad spectrum of commonly used performance metrics, multiple aggregation strategies, and several widely adopted CI methods. Reliability (coverage) and precision (width) of each CI method were estimated across all settings to characterize their dependence on study characteristics. Our analysis revealed five principal findings: (1) the sample size required for reliable CIs varies from a few dozens to several thousands of cases depending on study parameters; (2) CI behavior is strongly affected by the choice of performance metric; (3) aggregation strategy substantially influences the reliability of CIs, e.g. they require more observations for macro than for micro; (4) the machine learning problem (segmentation versus classification) modulates these effects; (5) different CI methods are not equally reliable and precise depending on the use case. Finally, we derived practical implications of this study in the form of a decision tree which shall prove useful to the community. This paves the way for future consensus guidelines on reporting performance uncertainty.

title: Streamline pathology foundation model by cross-magnification distillation.
abstract: Foundation models (FM) have transformed computational pathology but remain computationally prohibitive for clinical deployment due to their massive parameter counts and high-magnification processing requirements. Here, we introduce XMAG, a lightweight FM developed through cross-magnification distillation that transfers knowledge from a state-of-the-art 20x magnification teacher to an efficient 5x magnification student architecture. XMAG employs a compact backbone and operates entirely at 5x, requiring 11.3 times fewer patches per whole slide image (WSI) compared to existing approaches. Our novel distillation framework incorporates dual-level knowledge transfer, aligning both global image representations and local spatial features across magnification levels through carefully designed projection heads and spatial token mapping. We trained XMAG on 3.49 million images curated from publicly available datasets and evaluated performance across seven clinically relevant histopathology analysis tasks spanning multiple cancer types. Across four WSI-level classification tasks, XMAG achieved an average AUC within 1% of substantially larger foundation models while delivering up to 29.5-fold faster encoder-level processing, corresponding to an encoder throughput of 8.8 WSIs per minute in a controlled patch-encoding benchmark. We also found that performance differences remained task-dependent, with larger gaps observed for fine-grained tasks such as ISUP grading and patch-level phenotyping. We further explore end-to-end XMAG training as a direction for task-specific adaptation of the compact model. These results suggest that cross-magnification distillation is a promising strategy for developing efficient low-magnification pathology foundation models and may support more scalable WSI analysis in computationally constrained research and translational settings.

title: ROI-SSIM guided framework for 3D knee MRI reconstruction under artifact degradation.
abstract: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) reconstruction is highly sensitive to undersampling and acquisition artifacts. Although deep learning-based approaches have significantly improved reconstruction quality, they are typically optimized using global fidelity metrics that may not fully reflect reconstruction quality within clinically important structures such as the anterior cruciate ligament (ACL), meniscus, and articular cartilage. This study proposes a region-aware MRI reconstruction framework based on a Vision Transformer autoencoder (ViT-AE) guided by an ROI Structural Similarity (ROI-SSIM) loss. The method leverages fastMRI+ bounding-box annotations and incorporates a hybrid artifact simulation framework spanning k-space and image-domain degradations. Experiments on the fastMRI knee single-coil validation set (PD contrast, R=4) show that the proposed ViT-AE achieves reconstruction fidelity competitive with established baselines (SSIM 0.823, Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR) 32.4dB , Normalized Mean Squared Error (NMSE) 0.0147), while ROI-SSIM supervision improves structural fidelity within clinically relevant annotated regions. Under mixed artifact conditions, region-specific structural similarity decreased by only 2.9% , compared with a 6.8% decrease in global SSIM. These findings support the use of region-aware supervision for artifact-robust MRI reconstruction. Overall, the method presented in this paper:Introduces ROI-SSIM supervision for region-aware MRI reconstruction.Develops a hybrid artifact simulation framework spanning k-space and image-domain degradations.Demonstrates improved anatomical preservation under artifact conditions.

title: Ex vivo fluorescence confocal microscopy for real-time margin assessment of nonmelanoma skin cancer in Mohs surgery: A prospective interventional study.
abstract: New-generation ex vivo fluorescence confocal microscopy (EVFCM) generates hematoxylin-eosin-like images directly comparable to conventional histopathology. Its interobserver performance with a novel acquisition mode in non-melanoma skin cancer (NMSC) micrographically controlled surgery remains to be defined. In this prospective interventional study, 42 tumors from 39 patients undergoing Mohs surgery between January and October 2025 were examined with EVFCM. Specimens were orthogonally sectioned, stained, and acquired in digital-stain mode. Peripheral and deep margins were independently and blindly reviewed by a dermatologist and a pathologist, both trained in EVFCM interpretation. Concordant negative margins were considered tumor-free, whereas positive, discordant, or equivocal findings prompted re-excision and re-evaluation. Diagnostic agreement with histopathology was assessed using Cohen's κ statistic. A total of 261 margins were evaluated. Inter-reader agreement between the dermatologist and pathologist was almost perfect for both margin assessment (κ=0.863; SE 0.067; p<0.001; observed agreement 98.6%) and histotype assessment (κ=0.882; SE 0.031; p<0.001; observed agreement 97.6%). Compared with histopathology, EVFCM showed high performance, with an overall diagnostic accuracy of 96.4%. The AUC for the combined assessment was 0.875 (SE 0.074; 95% CI 0.730-1.000). Only two discrepancies were observed between EVFCM and histopathology: one false-negative margin assessment and one discordance attributable to differences in sample processing. These findings support EVFCM as a reliable tool for intraoperative margin assessment in NMSC. Comparable performance between dermatologist and pathologist readers supports its potential integration into Mohs surgery workflows; however, potential workflow advantages of the standardized sample-processing approach require prospective validation using quantitative time metrics.

title: Adaptive local region super-resolution for high-field MRI: A diffusion-based approach with structural and frequency-domain constraints.
abstract: High-field MRI offers superior SNR but is constrained by the trade-off between spatial resolution and acquisition time. Existing global deep learning super-resolution (SR) methods often incur computational overhead by ignoring regional image content. This motivates an adaptive local SR strategy to optimize efficiency and detail preservation. To address this, we developed a local SR method that adaptively allocates computational resources to information-rich regions. The proposed framework regularized an entropy-based local region processing strategy with a diffusion model fortified by frequency-domain and structural constraints. We retrospectively evaluated our method on two diverse datasets: a proprietary 7.0 T dental MRI dataset (25 T2-weighted DESS sequences from 10 beagle dogs) and a public 5.0 T brain MRI dataset (Diff5T, 50 diffusion-weighted sequences). Image quality was quantified using PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS, and FID. On the 7.0 T dental test dataset (2 subjects), our method achieved a PSNR of 27.31 [26.83, 27.79] dB and the lowest LPIPS of 0.19 [0.18, 0.20]. On the 5.0 T brain test dataset (10 subjects), the method achieved a PSNR of 27.15 ± 0.10 dB, an LPIPS of 0.14 ± 0.00 and an FID of 54.01, with lower perceptual metrics than the evaluated baselines. Ablation studies indicated that the proposed frequency-domain and structural constraints reduced LPIPS and FID, with trade-offs in PSNR and SSIM. In conclusion, the evaluated framework showed improvements in perceptual metrics by integrating targeted local processing with frequency-domain and structural regularization, accompanied by a trade-off in pixel-wise fidelity metrics, supporting the technical feasibility of addressing the resolution-time trade-off in high-field MRI. Future work will focus on expanding the dataset and evaluating the framework in human dental cohorts to address anatomical differences between the current canine model and human dental anatomy.

title: Multicenter external validation of a multimodal MRI deep-learning model to predict meningioma bone invasion.
abstract: Background Preoperative detection of meningioma bone invasion lacks objective biomarkers and relies on subjective radiological assessment, posing a risk of excessive bone resection or residual tumor. We therefore developed and externally validated a parsimonious six-feature DenseNet121 signature derived from multiparametric MRI across two independent institutions. Methods In this retrospective diagnostic accuracy study, 438 consecutive patients (mean age, 53 ± 11 years; 77% women) with histologically confirmed meningioma were allocated to training (n = 182), internal validation (n = 77), and external test (n = 179) sets. Following N4 bias-field correction and isotropic resampling, contrast-enhanced T1-weighted, T2-weighted, and diffusion-weighted volumes were fed into a DenseNet121 architecture to extract a six-feature signature via nested cross-validation. Discrimination (area under the ROC curve, AUC), calibration (Hosmer-Lemeshow test), and clinical utility (decision-curve analysis) were evaluated. Results In the external cohort (prevalence 11%), the signature achieved an AUC of 0.82 (95% CI 0.73-0.91), sensitivity 75%, specificity 77% and negative predictive value 96%, with an AUC improvement of 0.155 over conventional radiomics (95% CI, 0.01-0.30; p = 0.035). At a 20% risk threshold, decision-curve analysis confirmed a positive net clinical benefit, primarily driven by the high negative predictive value. SHAP analysis demonstrated the dominant and consistent contribution of low-ADC features. Conclusion The DenseNet121-derived six-feature signature serves as a reliable rule-out aid for preoperative meningioma bone invasion, with a high negative predictive value that may safely support decisions to avoid extensive bone resection in predicted-negative cases. Positive predictions require confirmatory CT or intraoperative biopsy to mitigate false positives. This tool could assist nurses and surgeons in preoperative planning, facilitating personalized patient care and potentially reducing operative time and complications.

title: A hierarchical residual Swin transformer with dual-level locality compensation for accelerated MRI reconstruction.
abstract: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) provides high spatial resolution, excellent soft-tissue contrast, and reliable anatomical discrimination, and is therefore widely used in clinical diagnosis. However, long acquisition time still limits imaging efficiency and clinical throughput. Although convolutional neural network (CNN)-based deep learning approaches have shown considerable promise for reconstructing images from undersampled k-space data, existing methods frequently fail to preserve fine structural details and texture continuity under aggressive undersampling conditions. In this study, we propose a novel reconstruction network based on the Swin Transformer, which integrates three key components: (i) long residual connections to facilitate the recovery of high-frequency details; (ii) a dual-level locality compensation mechanism to restore local spatial information; and (iii) a channel recalibration module to explicitly capture global dependencies among channels, thereby enhancing global feature extraction. Extensive experiments conducted on the IXI and MICCAI 2013 datasets demonstrate that the proposed method consistently outperforms several compared generative adversarial network (GAN)-based approaches for MRI reconstruction across all undersampling mask types, achieving a PSNR improvement of approximately 0.6-1 dB over the best competing method under various settings. The implementation code is available at https://github.com/cvgjhuor/HR-SwinGAN.

title: A deep learning radiomics model based on multiparametric MRI for predicting the efficacy of neoadjuvant chemotherapy in axillary lymph nodes of breast cancer.
abstract: Objectives In this study, we developed and validated a deep learning radiomics clinical (DLRC) model integrating multiparametric MRI (mpMRI) and clinical data to predict axillary pathological complete response (apCR) in cN+ breast cancer patients receiving neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NAC). Materials and methods We retrospectively collected data from 221 eligible breast cancer patients. The DLRC model integrated radiomics features and deep learning scores (DL-Scores) derived from mpMRI, together with clinical risk factors, to predict apCR. Seven classifiers were employed for model construction, and the optimal classifier was selected based on classification performance to build the final model. Model performance was evaluated using the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve, area under the curve (AUC), calibration curve, and decision curve analysis (DCA). Classification performance was assessed via the confusion matrix. Additionally, SHAP plots were utilized for interpretability analysis of the model. Results Multivariate analysis confirmed that progesterone receptor (PR), human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2), clinical T stage (OR = 0.258), and time-intensity curve (TIC) were significantly associated with apCR. The mpMRI based DLRC model achieved AUCs of 0.949 (95% CI, 0.912-0.986) and 0.932 (95% CI, 0.867-0.998) in the training and validation sets. SHAP analysis further revealed the interpretability of the model. The confusion matrix visually demonstrated the consistency between the predicted results and the true labels, validating the classification performance of the model. Conclusion The DLRC model effectively predicts apCR in breast cancer patients after NAC. It can serve as an auxiliary tool for clinicians in identifying potential candidates for axillary de-escalation, offering support for personalized precision treatment. We present this article in accordance with the TRIPOD-AI reporting checklist.

title: The utility of magnetic resonance imaging of the spinal cord in paediatric transverse myelitis: A systematic review.
abstract: Background Spinal cord magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is central to the diagnosis of paediatric acute transverse myelitis (ATM), yet its true diagnostic yield, concordance with cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) inflammation, and prognostic value remain unclear. Objective To quantify the diagnostic yield of spinal cord MRI in paediatric ATM, evaluate agreement with CSF inflammatory markers, and explore associations between MRI features and clinical outcomes. Methods A systematic review was conducted in accordance with PRISMA guidelines and prospectively registered (CRD42024504846). MEDLINE, EMBASE, CINAHL, PsycINFO and CENTRAL were searched from 2006 to October 2025. Observational studies including ≥5 children (≤18 years) with monophasic ATM who underwent spinal cord MRI were eligible. The primary outcome was the proportion of clinically diagnosed ATM cases demonstrating inflammatory spinal cord lesions on MRI. Secondary outcomes included MRI-CSF concordance and associations between imaging findings and long-term outcomes. Risk of bias was assessed using QUADAS-2. Results Twelve studies comprising 330 children were included. The pooled diagnostic yield of spinal cord MRI was 97.6% (95% CI 92.2 to 100.0%), with substantial heterogeneity (I²=71.8%) and a wide 95% prediction interval of 71.2 to 99.6%, indicating that a future paediatric cohort could plausibly report a yield anywhere within that range. Longitudinally extensive transverse myelitis and gadolinium enhancement were the most frequently reported features. Paired MRI-CSF data were available for 61 patients; discordance was observed in 36%, most commonly MRI-positive with normal CSF. Follow-up data (n = 237) showed 64% achieved good recovery, whereas 30% had severe residual deficits; persistent bladder dysfunction occurred in 31%. Baseline MRI positivity did not reliably predict outcome. Conclusions Spinal cord MRI demonstrates a high diagnostic yield in imaged children with clinically diagnosed ATM, but imaging was a condition of cohort entry in most included studies and the pooled estimate is strongly influenced by study design. MRI should be interpreted alongside CSF findings, and baseline imaging alone does not reliably stratify prognosis. Standardised prospective studies are required to refine the diagnostic and prognostic role of MRI in paediatric inflammatory myelopathies.

title: Histomorphometric analysis of invasive fungal infections.
abstract: Background Invasive fungal infections represent a growing global health challenge, making rapid and accurate diagnosis essential for timely initiation of appropriate therapy. Histopathology remains central to distinguishing true infection from colonization or contamination, and morphometric analysis may facilitate fungal identification. Furthermore, advances in digital pathology, artificial intelligence (AI), and machine learning have increased interest in morphometric approaches for fungal differentiation. However, their application requires the identification of morphometric parameters that reliably discriminate between fungal genera. Method In the present study 8772 measurements across nine morphometric parameters in 76 human and veterinary histological cases of invasive fungal infections caused by Candida, Aspergillus, and Mucorales were performed. Aim The aims were to comprehensively characterize fungal morphology, evaluate the diagnostic utility of different morphometric parameters, and develop a simple decision tree for fungal differentiation. Results Overall, the measurements made in this study demonstrated good interobserver agreement. Only minor morphometric variation was observed throughout the tissue blocks, indicating that assessment of a single histological section can be sufficient for morphometric analysis. In addition, discriminatory morphometric parameters were identified, enabling the development of a diagnostic decision tree that differentiated Mucorales from Aspergillus and Candida in 95% of the cases. Conclusions These findings demonstrate that quantitative morphometry provides reliable and clinically relevant information for fungal identification in histological sections. The identified morphometric parameters may form the basis for future image analysis and machine learning approaches, enabling faster and more accurate diagnosis of invasive fungal infections.

title: Maternal edible THC consumption alters offspring neurodevelopment and emotional behavior in rhesus macaques.
abstract: Background Prenatal cannabis exposure is associated with adverse offspring outcomes including altered neurodevelopment. However, there is insufficient evidence to establish a direct association. We sought to determine the impact of chronic prenatal delta-9-tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) exposure on offspring neurodevelopment and emotional behavior in a translational rhesus macaque model. Methods Animals were divided into two groups, control and THC-exposed, with both groups receiving a daily edible (placebo or THC) pre-conception, throughout pregnancy, and postnatally. MRI was performed longitudinally across gestation and infancy to assess volumetric and microstructural brain development. Serial behavioral testing, including motor and emotional assessments, was performed postnatally. At 6 months of age, brain tissue was collected for histology, immunohistochemistry (IHC), whole genome bisulfite sequencing (WGBS), and bulk RNA-sequencing. Findings Analysis of the MRI images showed white matter changes with higher fractional anisotropy in the corpus callosum (CC) and centrum semiovale in THC-exposed infants. However, there were no significant differences in regional brain volumes. Behavioral testing demonstrated that THC-exposed infants displayed increased vocalizations and decreased independence. WGBS identified differentially methylated regions (DMRs) associated with THC exposure in the cerebellum and prefrontal cortex, annotated to genes involved in synaptic organization and brain development. RNA-sequencing confirmed differential expression of genes related to axon development and glutamatergic synapse, with expression correlating with methylation levels. Interpretation Chronic prenatal edible THC exposure in the rhesus macaque was associated with changes in white matter development, effects on infant behavior with signs of increased stress and anxiety, and brain DNA methylation and expression of genes involved in neurodevelopment. Funding NIH, March of Dimes, Silver Family Innovation.

title: Resting-state fMRI biomarkers of surgical outcome in temporal lobe epilepsy: Network reorganization, rsfMRI-based prediction models, and cognition - A systematic review.
abstract: Temporal lobe epilepsy (TLE) is a network disorder extending beyond the structurally defined epileptogenic zone. Resting-state functional MRI (rsfMRI) may provide information on brain network alterations relevant to seizure outcome and cognitive risk after epilepsy surgery. We reviewed rsfMRI studies in TLE surgical cohorts to evaluate postoperative network changes, preoperative predictors of seizure outcome, and associations between functional connectivity and cognition. This systematic review followed PRISMA guidelines and was registered in PROSPERO. Fifteen studies were included, comprising 474 TLE patients who underwent resective epilepsy surgery and had at least 1 year of follow-up. Studies were reviewed for patient population, surgery, rsfMRI methodology, networks or regions, outcome definition, postoperative network changes, and cognitive assessments. Despite heterogeneity in patient selection, surgery, rsfMRI analysis, and outcome definition, studies consistently reported reduced DMN-related connectivity in TLE compared with healthy controls. Postoperative functional connectivity in seizure-free patients shifted toward healthy controls patterns in few studies. Preoperative rsfMRI-based prediction models showed promising accuracy for predicting seizure outcome but were generally developed in small cohorts and lacked external validation. Evidence relating rsfMRI to cognition was limited, but implicated thalamic, ascending reticular activating system, and thalamo-occipital connectivity in attention, language, and executive functions. RsfMRI is a promising research biomarker for network-level risk stratification in TLE surgery, particularly for seizure outcome prediction and postoperative network reorganization. Current evidence remains insufficient for clinical implementation. Future studies require larger homogeneous multicenter cohorts, standardized acquisition and preprocessing, consistent outcome definitions, systematic postoperative rsfMRI, neuropsychological assessment, and external validation of prediction models.

title: Latent knowledge-driven unified representation learning for brain tumor segmentation with missing modalities.
abstract: Gliomas are the most common primary malignant brain tumors, characterized by high heterogeneity, diffuse infiltration, and poor prognosis. Accurate tumor segmentation plays a fundamental role in diagnosis, treatment planning, and quantitative analysis. Although multimodal MRI provides rich anatomical and functional information, missing imaging modalities are frequently encountered in real-world clinical practice. Here, we propose a Latent Knowledge-driven Unified Representation Learning (LK-URL) framework for robust glioma segmentation under missing-modality conditions. LK-URL incorporates a Dynamic Adaptive Unified Interaction Module (DAUIM) to model intra- and inter-modality interactions, enabling enhanced tumor-aware feature representation and cross-modal compensation. Furthermore, a Latent Knowledge Collaborative Learning (LKCL) strategy is introduced to transfer structural knowledge from complete to incomplete modality settings via internal full-modality supervision, thereby improving the consistency of feature representations across diverse modality combinations and enhancing segmentation robustness. Extensive experiments on three datasets demonstrate that the proposed method consistently outperforms state-of-the-art approaches under missing-modality scenarios, while exhibiting strong generalization ability in real-world clinical settings. The code is available at https://github.com/joey-AI-medical-learning/LK-URL.

title: TMRKP: Trustworthy MRI-based radiology knowledge-aware prediction framework for stroke-associated pneumonia and hemorrhagic transformation.
abstract: Prediction of stroke-associated pneumonia (SAP) and hemorrhagic transformation (HT) is critical for improving the prognosis of acute ischemic stroke patients. However, current brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-based models narrowly focus on generic visual patterns, and frequently overlook the radiology-informed knowledge critical for predicting SAP and HT. To address this limitation, we propose a trustworthy MRI-based radiology knowledge-aware prediction (TMRKP) framework equipped with radiology knowledge-aware masked modeling (RKMM) and evidential multi-sequence fusion (EMF). Specifically, TMRKP first organizes four MRI sequences into a 2 × 2 super-sequence configuration, mimicking the diagnostic perspective of radiologists who simultaneously analyze multiple imaging modalities. Second, to introduce radiology knowledge into representation learning, we focus on white matter hyperintensities (WMH), a well-established biomarker of chronic small-vessel disease and long-term ischemic injury that is clinically relevant to SAP and HT. During pre-training, RKMM segments WMH masks from the MRI sequence to steer the model toward WMH regions, enabling it to learn meaningful representations of these clinically relevant pathological areas. Third, for SAP and HT prediction, EMF models the predictive uncertainty using evidence derived from both the super-sequence and the WMH-aware masked super-sequence, and fuses the resulting multi-sequence evidence based on Dempster-Shafer theory (DST). Extensive experiments on the collected Jiangdu dataset, together with independent external validation on the Zhongda dataset, demonstrate the superiority and generalizability of TMRKP over the state-of-the-art models.

title: Brain volume analysis-guided basic research in psychiatry.
abstract: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) volumetric analysis is among the few tools able to probe the living human brain, offering a route from clinical findings back to basic neuroscience. Here we propose a reverse-translational framework for psychiatric research that links human MRI findings to their underlying molecular mechanisms in model animals. The framework rests on three "liaisons": a species liaison, confirming that a volume change identified in humans is also observed in mice using the same imaging and analytical method; a scale liaison, in which a histological pipeline explains the macroscopic volume change in terms of cell number and cell volume; and a causal liaison, in which molecular or cell-biological intervention converts correlative histological findings into causal evidence by inducing or reversing the volume change. We further propose that unbiased, whole-brain MRI volumetric analysis in mice can serve as an exploratory region-screening method, identifying disease- or treatment-related regions without a predefined region of interest, and capturing the maintained structural outcome of an intervention rather than its immediate functional trace. Together, the three-liaison framework and the region-screening approach outline a general strategy by which MRI-guided reverse and forward translation can uncover the structural and molecular basis of psychiatric diseases and their treatments.

title: Characterizing age-dependent diamagnetic and paramagnetic susceptibility properties in 5xFAD Alzheimer's mouse brain using high-resolution MRI.
abstract: Background and purpose Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a devastating and progressive neurodegenerative disorder and the most common cause of dementia. This study aimed to characterize magnetic susceptibility changes associated with beta-amyloid (Aβ) plaques during AD progression using diamagnetic and paramagnetic susceptibility measurements in the 5xFAD mouse model. Methods Ex vivo multi-echo gradient-echo imaging (MGRE) with a spatial resolution of 40 × 40 × 40 μm 3 was performed in three age groups of 5xFAD mice (4, 12, and 18 months) using a 9.4T Bruker MRI scanner. Quantitative susceptibility mapping (QSM) was reconstructed, and DECOMPOSE-QSM was applied to derive diamagnetic component susceptibility (DCS) and paramagnetic component susceptibility (PCS). Aβ plaques were automatically detected based on DCS and quantified to assess age-dependent plaque accumulation, changes in plaque burden, and associated susceptibility alterations. Cortical regions were further segmented into plaque-detected and plaque-undetected regions to assess regional susceptibility variations among the three age groups. In addition, Aβ/ferritin immunostaining was performed on the imaged murine brains. Results The results demonstrated progressive, spatially heterogeneous, age-dependent accumulation of amyloid plaques, as evidenced by significant increases in plaque burden. In plaque-detected and whole-region cortical areas, DCS consistently shifted toward more negative values (greater diamagnetic susceptibility) with disease progression, while PCS became more positive (greater paramagnetic susceptibility). The concurrent increase in plaque burden, together with progressively more negative DCS and more positive PCS within plaques, are consistent with increasing diamagnetic and paramagnetic tissue contributions associated with amyloid and iron-related pathology, respectively. Histological analysis showed colocalized Aβ aggregation and ferritin deposition within plaques, both of which increased with age. Conclusions The decomposed susceptibility components, DCS and PCS, provide complementary biophysical information beyond conventional QSM, enabling improved characterization of plaque-associated susceptibility changes during AD progression. High-resolution MRI facilitates the visualization and detection of individual plaques, allowing detailed analysis of their susceptibility properties. These findings highlight the importance of high-resolution MRI and the potential of diamagnetic and paramagnetic susceptibility measures as sensitive imaging biomarkers for monitoring neurodegenerative pathology.

title: The Visual Cortex and Beyond: Investigating Long-Term Cortical Plasticity Following Monocular Deprivation.
abstract: Aim To characterise short- and long-term plastic changes in cortical and subcortical structures induced by ultra-long (five-day) monocular deprivation (MD), and to assess the extent and regional specificity of structural changes and their reversibility following the restoration of binocular vision. Methods In this single-arm longitudinal study, 21 healthy adults underwent five structural MRI sessions: at baseline, during MD on days 1, 3 and 5, and after a seven-day recovery period (day 12). MD was induced by occluding the right eye with a translucent eye patch for five consecutive days. Grey matter volume (GMV) changes were analysed using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) for whole-brain effects and generalised estimating equations (GEE) to model temporal trajectories in predefined cortical and subcortical regions. Results Ultra-long MD induced dynamic GMV changes in primary and higher visual cortices, with exploratory changes also in subcortical and cerebellar structures. VBM showed cumulative volume increases in bilateral occipital cortex, including calcarine, lateral occipital and fusiform regions, and adjacent cerebellar lobules, peaking between days 3 and 5. Region-wise modelling resolved the temporal build-up of these changes across visual, subcortical and sensorimotor regions; after correction for multiple comparisons, a time-dependent effect remained in occipital and ventral occipito-temporal cortex (occipital pole, fusiform and calcarine cortex), converging with the voxel-wise result. Following binocular restoration, an exploratory GMV decrease was observed selectively in the left middle occipital gyrus, while an exploratory increase was observed in the left hippocampus, compatible with persistent plasticity in associative memory networks. Conclusion Prolonged sensory imbalance via ultra-long MD induces rapid, region-specific and possibly persistent GMV plasticity in the adult brain. These changes follow temporally stratified trajectories across visual, subcortical and integrative systems, consistent with models of homeostatic and hierarchical plasticity. Corrected evidence supports cumulative occipital plasticity during deprivation; whether the exploratory extra-visual and post-recovery changes reflect persistent adaptation requires confirmation. MD-based paradigms thus offer a controlled window on structural plasticity in both healthy individuals and clinical populations.

title: Achieving detailed medial temporal lobe segmentation with upsampled isotropic training from implicit neural representation.
abstract: Imaging biomarkers in magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) are important tools for diagnosing, tracking and treating Alzheimer's disease (AD). Neurofibrillary tau pathology in AD is closely linked to neurodegeneration and generally follows a pattern of spread in the brain, with early stages involving subregions of the medial temporal lobe (MTL). Accurate segmentation of MTL subregions is needed to extract granular biomarkers of AD progression. MTL subregions are often imaged using T2-weighted (T2w) MRI scans that are highly anisotropic due to constraints of MRI physics and image acquisition, making it difficult to reliably model MTL subregions geometrically and extract morphological measures, such as thickness. In this study, we propose a segmentation framework for MTL subregions in isotropic space, in which an implicit neural representation is used to construct the isotropic training atlas from the anisotropic low-resolution T2w data, with T1w MRI as an auxiliary modality to support the INR and segmentation. In an independent test set, the morphological measures extracted using this isotropic model showed stronger effect sizes than those from models trained on anisotropic data in distinguishing participants with mild cognitive impairment (MCI) from cognitively unimpaired individuals. In the test-retest analysis, the morphological measures extracted using the isotropic model showed greater stability than those from the anisotropic segmentation. This study demonstrates improved reliability of MRI-derived MTL subregion biomarkers without additional atlas annotation effort, which may more accurately quantify and track the relationship between AD pathology and brain atrophy for monitoring disease progression.

title: Atlas-assisted segment anything model for fetal brain MRI (FeTal-SAM).
abstract: This paper presents FeTal-SAM, a novel adaptation of the Segment Anything Model (SAM) tailored for fetal brain MRI segmentation. Traditional deep learning methods often require large annotated datasets for a fixed set of labels, making them inflexible when clinical or research needs change. By integrating atlas-based prompts and foundation-model principles, FeTal-SAM addresses two key limitations in fetal brain MRI segmentation: (1) the need to retrain models for varying label definitions, and (2) the lack of insight into whether segmentations are driven by genuine image contrast or merely inferred by learned spatial priors. We leverage multi-atlas registration to generate spatially aligned label templates that serve as dense prompts, alongside a bounding-box prompt, for SAM's segmentation decoder. This strategy enables binary segmentation on a per-structure basis, which is subsequently fused to reconstruct the full 3D segmentation volumes. Evaluations on two datasets, the dHCP dataset and an in-house dataset demonstrate FeTal-SAM's robust performance across gestational ages. Notably, it achieves Dice scores comparable to state-of-the-art baselines which were trained for each dataset and label definition for well-contrasted structures like cortical plate and cerebellum, while maintaining the flexibility to segment anatomical structures that could be templated by compatible atlas image and label sample pairs. Although slightly lower accuracy is observed for subtle, low-contrast structures (e.g., hippocampus, amygdala), our results highlight FeTal-SAM's potential as a flexible atlas-conditioned segmentation framework without requiring a separately trained model for each supported parcellation. This method thus constitutes a promising step toward clinically adaptable fetal brain MRI analysis tools.

title: Therapeutic potential and toxicological trade-offs of nanoparticle-enhanced valproic acid in glioblastoma: Behavioral and oxidative insights.
abstract: Background Glioblastoma (GBM) is a highly aggressive brain tumor with a poor prognosis. In the current research, the therapeutic and behavioral efficacy of valproic acid (VPA) and its nanoparticles (Nano VPA) with or without temozolomide (TMZ) was investigated in the C6 glioblastoma rat model. Methods We divided eighty-four adult male Wistar rats into seven groups (n = 12/group): sham, tumor, TMZ, VPA, nano VPA, VPA + TMZ, and nano VPA + TMZ. To induce tumors, C6 cells were injected into the brains of the rats. On days 12 to 15, behavioral performance was assessed using the social interaction test, elevated plus maze, open field, rotarod, and passive avoidance. On day 18, tumor size, edema, and histopathology were examined. Oxidative stress parameters in brain tissue and serum were measured by ELISA. Results VPA and Nano VPA significantly inhibited tumor growth, either alone or with TMZ. All treatments except Nano VPA + TMZ improved survival compared with tumor controls. Treated groups showed enhanced anxiety regulation, sociability, learning, and memory. Motor coordination improved following VPA or Nano VPA therapy. Tumor induction reduced serum SOD, CAT, and TAC levels; treatments raised serum TAC and lowered brain MDA, but further reduced serum SOD. Conclusion Our results suggest that oxidative stress modulation may contribute to the neurobehavioral and antitumor effects of both VPA and nano-VPA. While nano-VPA showed greater tumor reduction, conventional VPA was more effective in improving survival. Combining VPA with TMZ may enhance outcomes, and support further study of Nano VPA as an adjuvant therapy for GBM.

title: CAG repeat length shapes bidirectional functional connectome alterations in spinocerebellar ataxia type 3: a multimodal MRI study.
abstract: The ATXN3 gene is the primary driver of brain damage in spinocerebellar ataxia type 3 (SCA3). We aimed to elucidate the patterns of connectome alterations shaped by cytosine-adenine-guanine (CAG) repeat length in SCA3. Eighty-nine genetically confirmed patients with SCA3 and 89 age-, sex-, education-matched healthy controls underwent multimodal MRI and comprehensive clinical assessments. Connectome-based predictive modeling (CPM) was used to identify functional connectivity patterns associated with CAG repeat length. Structural brain damage was assessed using voxel-based morphometry. Mediation analysis was performed to examine the role of structural impairment in connectivity changes. CPM identified a positive and a negative network, whose connectivity strength increased or decreased with CAG repeat length. The positive network (r = 0.397, P < 0.001) was mainly localized within the cerebello-motor circuit and was positively associated with ataxia severity and functional disability. The negative network (r = 0.243, P = 0.022) was distributed across large-scale networks, with selective vulnerability of interhemispheric connectivity, and was associated with motor dysfunction. Besides the canonical motor pathways, limbic-related connectivity was related to motor impairment. Structural analyses revealed widespread gray matter atrophy centered on the cerebellum. Cerebellar atrophy statistically mediated the association between CAG repeat length and connectivity decreases. CAG repeat length is associated with a bidirectional connectopathy in SCA3. Cerebellar atrophy may mediate the connectivity decreases. Future longitudinal studies are required to examine the underlying causal pathway.

title: Machine learning of connectome-wide functional connectivity in spinal muscular atrophy.
abstract: While traditional view posed SMA as a pure motor neuron disorder, accumulating evidence pointed to the broader involvement of central nervous system. This study aimed to combined connectome-wide resting-state functional connectivity with machine learning algorithms to investigate the underlying brain mechanisms in SMA and capture the potential neuroimaging biomarker. Resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging were acquired from 43 SMA (26 SMA type 2 and 17 type 3) and 45 healthy controls (HCs). Connectome-wide functional connectivity, defined based on the Automated Anatomical Labeling 116 atlas (AAL116), combined with machine learning algorithms including logistic regression (LR), support vector machine (SVM) and random forest (RF) were conducted for SMA vs HCs and SMA type 2 vs 3 classification. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) algorithm was used to quantify the contribution of individual connections. Connectome-wide functional connectivity allowed individual classification of SMA and HCs with stable performance across machine learning models. The majority of the most discriminative functional connectivity involved the high-level associative regions and cerebellum, subserving sensory and motor processing. Furthermore, the functional connectivity between right superior parietal gyrus and right inferior temporal gyrus was positively correlated with motor function. In conclusion, our study provided connectome-wide evidence that functional connectivity patterns involving high-level associative cortices and the cerebellum could distinguish SMA from HCs using machine learning. The identified connectivity features offer new insight into the distributed brain pathology of SMA beyond the traditional classical motor neuron view, and may serve as promising neuroimaging marker for this disease.

title: Dynamic multi-scale topology learning and cross-modal graph fusion for autism spectrum disorder diagnosis.
abstract: Multi-modal fusion methods have demonstrated potential in integrating complementary information from different data modalities. However, existing methods often rely on static fusion strategies, failing to capture the heterogeneous interactions across modalities. To address this challenge, we propose the dynamic multi-scale topology learning and cross-modal interaction graph fusion network (DMTL-Net) for autism spectrum disorder (ASD) diagnosis. The model is designed to extract distinctive and complementary features from brain functional and structural networks while capturing their dynamic topological organization. Specifically, the structural radiomics similarity network (RSN) and functional connectivity network (FCN) are constructed from structural magnetic resonance imaging (sMRI) and functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI), respectively. Multi-modal graph initialization is performed by the cross-modal inclusive integration and consensus filtering to balance sensitivity and specificity. Then we propose the dynamic topology learning mechanism that integrates multi-scale feature extraction with adaptive channel-wise and spatial-wise fusion, effectively capturing complex inter-modal interactions. Additionally, focal loss is used to reduce the contribution of easy-to-classify samples and emphasize hard examples during optimization. Evaluated on the Autism Brain Imaging Data Exchange dataset, the proposed DMTL-Net demonstrates superior performance and consistently outperforms the state-of-the-art methods.

title: Meningioma in the modern era: Updates in stratification and therapeutic approaches.
abstract: Meningioma is the most common primary intracranial tumor in adults. Most meningiomas have an indolent growth pattern, but some can grow quickly. The World Health Organization (WHO) classification system is the gold standard for tumor grading and relies predominantly on histopathology and limited molecular alterations. It is increasingly recognized that the variability in tumor behaviour is incompletely captured using traditional systems. Contemporary advances have expanded tumor stratification beyond starting WHO grading, providing a more comprehensive framework for understanding tumor biology. Molecular profiling has identified independent biological classification systems and molecular signatures that capture important prognostic information beyond histopathology. Magnetic resonance imaging-based analyses and radiomics have enabled non-invasive characterization of tumor phenotype and growth potential. Therapeutically, surgical resection and radiation therapy remain the foundation of management, with evolving paradigms emphasizing maximal safe resection and risk-adapted radiotherapy strategies informed by integrated tumor characteristics. Systemic therapies have historically shown limited efficacy; however, recent efforts are shifting toward biomarker-driven, precision approaches guided by molecular alterations. Future directions focus on integrating multimodal data into unified, clinically actionable models that more accurately predict recurrence, progression, and treatment response. Such approaches aim to move beyond parallel classification systems toward individualized management strategies, ultimately advancing meningioma care into a precision-based paradigm.

title: Diagnostic performance and methodological heterogeneity of neuromelanin-sensitive MRI in Parkinson's disease: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: Background Parkinson's disease (PD) diagnosis remains primarily clinical and is often delayed until substantial neurodegeneration has occurred. Neuromelanin-sensitive MRI (NM-MRI) assesses the integrity of neuromelanin-rich nuclei affected in PD, the substantia nigra pars compacta (SNpc) and locus coeruleus (LC), but its diagnostic performance, technical determinants, and translational applicability remain unclear amid heterogeneity. We aimed to quantify diagnostic accuracy, determine whether performance varies across methodological approaches, and contextualise evidence from clinically relevant settings. Methods We systematically reviewed NM-MRI diagnostic studies through December 2025. QUADAS-2 assessed risk of bias. Sensitivity and specificity were jointly pooled using a bivariate model, and AUC using random-effects meta-analysis. Subgroup analyses and exploratory meta-regressions assessed methodological heterogeneity; broader clinical evidence was synthesised qualitatively. Results Thirty-nine studies were included. Across 20 PD-versus-healthy-control (HC) studies (878 PD; 690 HCs), pooled sensitivity was 89.03% (95% CI 86.01-91.45%), specificity 87.02% (95% CI 82.76-90.34%), PLR 6.86, NLR 0.126, and DOR 54.37. Across 32 studies (1411 PD; 1086 HCs), pooled AUC was 0.909 (95% CI 0.884-0.929; I 2 = 64.6%). No significant unadjusted differences emerged by sequence, dimensionality, segmentation, or measurement type. NM-MRI abnormalities were detectable across prodromal, early- and advanced-stage PD, although global measures showed limited discrimination between disease stages. Subregional measures captured phenotypic variation, genotype discrimination was limited, and PD-versus-ET/APS performance was promising but variable, within small, heterogeneous evidence bases. Conclusion NM-MRI is a promising non-invasive imaging biomarker for PD, with strong discrimination across diverse methodological approaches. Harmonised acquisition and analysis, externally validated diagnostic thresholds, and prospective multicentre studies in clinically representative populations are needed to support future clinical implementation.

title: Investigation of CardioFreeze Motion Correction for Cardiac PET/CT.
abstract: Background Cardiac imaging with positron emission tomography and computed tomography (PET/CT) is a principal technique in the diagnosis and prognostication of coronary artery disease. PET/CT image quality can be negatively impacted by patient, cardiac, and respiratory motion. Methods We evaluated images from 102 patients clinically referred for cardiac rest/stress Rb-82 PET/CT myocardial perfusion imaging. Patient images were processed with a prototype data-driven motion detection algorithm and stratified by motion severity. Images were subjected to cardiac (CS) or cardiac and respiratory (CD) motion correction via a novel reconstruction tool. Validated image quality markers including target-to-background ratio (TBR) were assessed between corrected and non-corrected images and analyzed via student's t-tests. Results The motion detection algorithm identified 36 (35.3%) patients with significant motion. Image processing via CS yielded a statistically significant increase in mean image contrast (TBR 3.65±0.07, p<0.01) and intensified when respiratory motion correction was applied (3.78±0.07, p<0.005). Motion correction is more effective when applied to images containing greater motion, improving mean TBR by 3% (p<0.05) in non-motion scans but >10% (p<0.01) in significant motion cases. Three months post-imaging, 18 patients underwent clinically indicated coronary angiography: seven patients demonstrated significant motion, and CD motion correction improved their image quality to that of patients with no motion. Conclusions Over 1/3 of patients undergoing cardiac PET/CT have detectible motion leading to potential artifacts with clinical significance. Cardiac and respiratory motion correction improves image quality and may improve diagnostic accuracy, particularly when respiratory motion is severe. Further studies are critical to investigate the clinical impacts of improved image quality.

title: Applied nutritional investigation determinants of lower quadriceps skeletal muscle measured by ultrasound at ICU admission: a cross-sectional analysis.
abstract: Background Low skeletal muscle (SM) is common at ICU admission and is associated with worse prognosis. Early identification of at-risk patients is essential, but determinants of low SM in critically ill patients remains unclear. Objective To identify sociodemographic, nutritional, and clinical characteristics associated with low SM at ICU admission. Methods This cross-sectional analysis included critically ill patients ≥18 years admitted within 24 hours. Sociodemographic and nutritional data were obtained through anamnesis, while clinical data were extracted from records. Quadriceps muscle layer thickness (QMLT) was measured using a B-mode US. Lower QMLT was defined as values below the sex-specific 25th percentile of the sample. Binary logistic regression was performed. Results 399 patients were included (age 61.4 ± 14.9 years; 56.6% male). Older age (OR = 1.02; CI 95% 1.0-1.04), previous unintentional weight loss (OR = 1.64; CI 95% 1.03-2.61), reduced food intake before admission (OR = 2.32; CI 95% 1.44-3.74), and pressure injuries (OR = 1.83; CI 95% 1.05-3.20) were associated with low QMLT. However, in multivariate analysis, only older age (OR = 1.02; CI 95% 1.00-1.04) and reduced food intake (OR = 2.26; CI 95% 1.22-4.18) remained independent determinants. Conclusion Older age and reduced food intake were independently associated with lower QMLT at ICU admission. These findings highlight the need for early screening and targeted strategies to mitigate muscle loss and improve outcomes in critically ill patients.

title: OpenMSK: A modular open-source framework for comprehensive analysis of imaging biomarkers in knee osteoarthritis.
abstract: Objective To develop and validate a fully automated, extendable, open-source AI-driven pipeline capable of knee magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) segmentation and quantitative extraction of MRI and positron emission tomography (PET) imaging biomarkers. Design For model training, open-source knee MRI data from 347 knees acquired across 7 scanners using multiple gradient-echo sequences were used. An independent test set of 20 knees from 3T PET-MRI examinations were used for evaluation in this prospective reliability and agreement study. The pipeline segmented femoral, tibial, and patellar bones and cartilage, and medial and lateral menisci using three different deep learning models. Quantitative outputs included cartilage thickness and T 2 relaxation times, meniscus volume and T 2 ∗ relaxation times, bone shape scores, and static and kinetic subchondral bone PET measures. Manual segmentations from two annotators served as reference standards. Segmentation performance was assessed using Dice similarity coefficients (DSC), average symmetric surface distances, and volume differences. Quantitative outcome agreement was evaluated using intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC), Pearson correlations, and root mean square error. Results Automated segmentations demonstrated high spatial agreement with manual annotations, with DSCs ranging from 0.84 to 0.98 across all tissues. Quantitative PET-MRI biomarkers generally demonstrated high agreement, although confidence intervals were wide for several biomarkers. Conclusion OpenMSK enables multi-tissue knee segmentation and generation of quantitative MRI and PET biomarkers, with performance assessed against two independent annotators and across different U-Net-based segmentation architectures. As a freely available, modular platform, OpenMSK lowers technical barriers to whole-joint quantitative imaging and provides a standardized foundation for OA research and clinical translation.

title: Optic disc drusen as a diagnostic confounder in a child with Alice in Wonderland syndrome.
abstract: We report the case of a 10-year-old boy referred for transient visual episodes compatible with Alice in Wonderland syndrome, described as a sensation that objects were moving away. Ophthalmic examination showed preserved visual acuity and an unremarkable anterior segment, but revealed elevation of the left optic disc, prompting evaluation for true papilledema. Macular OCT was normal, whereas optic nerve head OCT demonstrated structural asymmetry consistent with pseudopapilledema. Brain and orbital MRI showed isolated enlargement of both optic nerve sheaths and mild elevation of the left optic disc, without additional findings suggestive of intracranial hypertension. Orbital ultrasonography identified a hyperechogenic focus suggestive of optic disc drusen. The stable clinical and structural course supported the diagnosis of unilateral pseudopapilledema due to optic disc drusen, probably unrelated to the perceptual symptoms.

title: Advances in precision medicine for the anterior segment: therapeutic applications using CRISPR-Cas9.
abstract: CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing has emerged as one of the most promising strategies in precision medicine applied to ophthalmology. Although its initial development focused on inherited retinal diseases, recent advances have increasingly targeted anterior segment disorders, including herpetic keratitis, hereditary corneal dystrophies, and genetically associated glaucoma. The ability to modify specific DNA or RNA sequences enables direct intervention in molecular pathways involved in inflammatory, degenerative, and infectious disease progression. This review summarizes the biological basis of CRISPR-Cas systems and discusses the main preclinical and translational findings related to corneal and glaucomatous diseases. Current limitations, including off-target effects, immunogenicity, and challenges associated with molecular delivery into ocular tissues, are also addressed. Available evidence suggests that CRISPR-Cas9 may significantly transform the future management of multiple anterior segment diseases.

title: Predicting taste alteration in head and neck cancer patients using 3D transformer-based deep learning model.
abstract: Purpose Taste alteration is a common post-treatment side effect of head and neck cancer (HNC) radiotherapy. Accurate normal tissue complication probability (NTCP) models can support treatment planning aimed at reducing side effects that impair quality-of-life. Deep learning (DL) offers opportunities to incorporate full 3D dose, CT, and organofinterest (OOI) data. Using a large prospective cohort, this study explores whether CNN and transformerbased DL models can outperform a conventional logistic regression model for predicting taste alteration 6 months after radiotherapy. Material/methods Data from 972 patients was used, with the endpoint being moderatetosevere patientreported taste alteration at six months (EORTC QLQH&N35). DL models were trained using 3D dose distributions, planning CT, OOI segmentations and clinical features. A conventional NTCP model using oral cavity mean dose, parotid mean dose, and age served as reference. Attention maps were evaluated for the transformer-based DL model to quantify the model attention to specific regions of the head and neck area. In addition, two cropping approaches for the 3D data were compared. Results The CNN and transformer DL models performed comparable to the reference NTCP model in the test set (Reference: AUC = 0.71; ResNet: AUC = 0.68; TransRP: AUC = 0.71), though calibration was best for the reference model. Shifting the crop improved DL performance and transformer attention focused on supraglottic and submandibular regions. Conclusion This study showed that the prediction of taste alteration can be achieved using DL models, particularly transformer-based models which, in contrast to CNNs, can account for global features of comprehensive 3D information of dose distribution, CT-images and organs-of-interest segmentations.

title: Systematic Review of Clinical Utility of Multimodal Imaging in Infectious Posterior Uveitis. Multimodal imaging in Uveitis (MUV) Taskforce Report 12.
abstract: Topic To systematically evaluate the clinical utility of multimodal imaging (MMI) for the diagnosis, activity assessment, longitudinal monitoring, and detection of complications in the five most prevalent infectious posterior uveitides. Design Systematic review and evidence-based quality appraisal. Participants Original research studies published between January 2018 and September 2025(primary cohort) and 2012-2017(supplemental cohort) evaluating MMI in ocular toxoplasmosis(TOXO), cytomegalovirus retinitis(CMVR), ocular tuberculosis(TB), syphilitic uveitis(SYPH), and acute retinal necrosis(ARN). Methods MEDLINE, Embase, Cochrane, and Scopus were systematically searched. Independent reviewers extracted reported imaging findings and clinical utility statements for: color fundus photography (CFP), fundus autofluorescence (FAF), optical coherence tomography (OCT), fundus fluorescein angiography (FFA), indocyanine green angiography (ICGA), and OCT angiography (OCTA). Methodological quality was assessed using the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool (MMAT), and certainty of evidence was graded using a bespoke consensus-based scheme informed by GRADE principles. Main outcome measures (1)reported imaging findings for each entity and modality; and (2)statements of clinical utility for diagnosis, detection of disease activity, longitudinal monitoring, and detection of complications. Results Among 122 included studies (82 primary and 40 supplemental), the primary studies contributed 5,522 individual patient examinations and 574 imaging statements, while the supplemental studies provided corroborating evidence. Overall, 366 clinical utility statements were identified across the four prespecified domains, including 30 statements supporting synergistic MMI strategies. CFP, including studies using ultra-widefield imaging, achieved high certainty for diagnosis and longitudinal monitoring in four of five entities (4/5, 80%), with moderate certainty in ARN. OCT achieved high certainty across all four clinical utility domains for four of five entities (4/5, 80%), with lower certainty in ARN owing to its limited evidence base. FFA achieved high certainty for complication detection in three of five entities. FAF achieved high certainty for disease activity in four of five entities. OCTA achieved high certainty in at least one domain for two of five entities, whereas ICGA achieved high certainty in at least one domain for only one of five entities. Conclusions Substantial evidence exists regarding the imaging findings and clinical utility of MMI in infectious posterior uveitis. Combined MMI enables integrated structural, vascular, and choroidal assessment beyond conventional clinical examination.
