title: Ultrasound of the salivary glands in Sjögren's syndrome: a narrative review of its diagnostic and prognostic utility and clinical role.
abstract: Sjögren's Disease (SjD) is a systemic autoimmune disease whose classification criteria include a minor salivary gland biopsy (MSGB), an invasive procedure. Salivary gland ultrasound (SGUS) has emerged as a non-invasive, accessible and reliable tool for the evaluation of SjD. This narrative review analyses the evolution of SGUS, from the first scoring systems to the current consensus of the OMERACT group, which has enabled standardisation of the evaluation. The evidence on the diagnostic accuracy of SGUS, its correlation with MSGB and autoantibodies, and its ability to predict patient classification according to the 2016 ACR/EULAR criteria are analysed. In selected patients, SGUS may reduce the need for minor salivary gland biopsy, particularly in those positive for anti-Ro/SSA antibodies. In addition, it explores its potential role in prognostic stratification, lymphoma prediction, and treatment response monitoring, proposing an algorithm for its integration into daily clinical practice.

title: [Translated article] Accuracy of the Akmese sign as a diagnostic method for posterior root tears of the medial meniscus in Peruvian healthcare facilities.
abstract: Background Medial meniscus injuries are the most prevalent knee injuries, frequently causing pain, instability, and orthopaedic surgeries. Although several clinical tests are used for meniscal pathology, most were developed for general meniscal lesions rather than specifically for medial meniscus posterior root tears (MMPRT). Evidence on root-specific physical examination signs remains limited. Recently, the Akmese manoeuvre has been introduced as a non-invasive diagnostic tool, assessing pain or tenderness during physical examination. This study aimed to determine the accuracy of the Akmese sign for the clinical diagnosis of MMPRT. Methods This prospective cohort diagnostic study included patients aged 18-55 years scheduled for arthroscopic surgery following a clinical diagnosis of medial meniscus injury between January 2022 and July 2023. Diagnostic performance metrics, including sensitivity, specificity, positive and negative predictive values (PPV, NPV), and likelihood ratios (LR+, LR-), were calculated, using arthroscopy as the reference standard. The interobserver reliability of the Akmese manoeuvre was assessed using the kappa coefficient. Results A total of 201 individuals met the eligibility criteria, with a mean age of 38.4 ± 9.8 years. The Akmese sign was positive in 26 patients, and MMPRT was confirmed by arthroscopy in 28 patients. The Akmese sign demonstrated a sensitivity of 85.7%, specificity of 98.8%, PPV of 92.3%, NPV of 97.7%, LR+ of 74.1, and a LR- of 0.15. Conclusion In this selected surgical population, the Akmese manoeuvre showed promising diagnostic performance and very good interobserver reliability for identifying MMPRT. The sign may be useful as an adjunctive clinical tool to support preoperative suspicion, targeted MRI review, and surgical planning, but it should not be considered a replacement for MRI or arthroscopic assessment.

title: Airway mucus plugs and ventilatory support during exacerbations, with subsequent outcomes, in patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease or emphysema.
abstract: Background Airway mucus plugs are associated with airflow obstruction and exacerbations in stable chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD); however, their roles during exacerbations remain unclear. This study aimed to examine whether mucus plugs during exacerbations are associated with ventilatory support requirements and prognosis in patients with COPD. Methods This single-center retrospective study included patients with COPD, defined by airflow limitation on spirometry or emphysema on computed tomography (CT), who presented to the emergency department, and were diagnosed with COPD exacerbation. Mucus plugs during exacerbations were visually assessed on CT and analyzed in relation to the need for ventilatory support (primary outcome). Results Of 86 patients with a median mucus plug score of 3.5 (interquartile range, 1-7), 26 (30.2%) received ventilatory support. In multivariable logistic regression analysis, a higher mucus plug score (odds ratio [OR], 1.34; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.16-1.59) and higher C-reactive protein level were significantly associated with the need for ventilatory support. In a Cox proportional hazards model, a higher mucus plug score (hazard ratio [HR], 1.17; 95% CI, 1.07-1.29) and long-term oxygen therapy use were significantly associated with a shorter time to re-exacerbation or all-cause death within 1 year. Mucus plugs significantly decreased from the exacerbation to the recovery phases in a sub-analysis of 20 patients who underwent CT in both phases. Conclusion A higher mucus plug score was associated with the need for ventilatory support and poorer clinical outcomes, suggesting that mucus plugs may impair ventilation and worsen the prognosis of COPD exacerbations.

title: Carcinomatous meningitis: Current insights into diagnosis, prognosis and management.
abstract: Carcinomatous meningitis, or leptomeningeal metastasis, is a severe neurological complication of solid and haematological malignancies caused by dissemination of tumour cells within the leptomeninges and cerebrospinal fluid pathways. Clinical presentation is heterogeneous, including headache, intracranial hypertension, cranial nerve palsies or radiculopathy, which frequently leads to diagnostic delay. Diagnosis relies on converging clinical, radiological, and cerebrospinal fluid findings, with gadolinium-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging of the brain and spine and cerebrospinal fluid cytology remaining central despite imperfect sensitivity. Emerging tools, particularly cerebrospinal fluid circulating tumour cells and circulating tumour DNA, may improve early detection and molecular characterisation. Prognosis remains poor, with survival usually measured in months. Management should be individualised according to performance status, tumour subtype, and systemic disease control, and may combine symptomatic measures, radiotherapy, targeted systemic therapies, and, in selected patients, intrathecal chemotherapy. Early integration of palliative care remains a key component of management.

title: Pulmonary artery intimal sarcoma masquerading as pulmonary embolism during therapeutic apixaban: A case report.
abstract: Pulmonary artery intimal sarcoma (PAIS) is a rare intravascular malignancy that can closely resemble pulmonary embolism (PE). A 65-year-old man receiving therapeutic apixaban for atrial fibrillation presented with 3 weeks of progressive exertional dyspnea. Computed tomography pulmonary angiography showed a large unilateral filling defect in the left main pulmonary artery with occlusion of the left upper- and lower-lobe branches, initially interpreted as PE. However, the D-dimer was low, bilateral lower-extremity ultrasonography showed no deep venous thrombosis, cardiac biomarkers were normal, and echocardiography showed preserved right ventricular size and function without pulmonary hypertension. Contrast-enhanced chest magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated an enhancing lobulated, frond-like proximal pulmonary artery mass with mild arterial expansion and a separate distal nonenhancing component consistent with bland thrombus. Pulmonary thromboendarterectomy with tumor debulking confirmed high-grade PAIS. The patient subsequently received doxorubicin, ifosfamide, and mesna with pembrolizumab followed by proton radiotherapy. This case emphasizes that a unilateral central pulmonary artery filling defect should prompt tumor-directed imaging when the thromboembolic burden is discordant with biomarkers, venous imaging, and right-heart physiology.

title: Pulmonary arterial volume and mortality in smokers without chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.
abstract: Background Pulmonary vascular remodelling is a recognised consequence of chronic tobacco exposure and may have prognostic associations even without airway obstruction. The association between the extraparenchymal pulmonary artery (ePA) and all-cause mortality in current and ex-smokers without COPD has not been demonstrated and replicated in large cohort studies. Study design and methods Retrospective analysis of prospective data from the COPDGene cohort, with validation in the SUMMIT lung cancer screening trial. ePA volume and lung volume were measured on chest CT using automated deep learning-based segmentation. All-cause mortality risk was estimated using Cox proportional hazards models, adjusted for age, gender, body mass index, smoking status, pack-years, emphysema extent, Charlson Comorbidity Index, ILA presence, and FEV 1 . Results 4719 participants without COPD were included in the discovery COPDGene cohort (median age 56 [51-63] years, 50% male) and 3391 in the SUMMIT validation cohort (median age 64 [59-69] years, 61% male). There were 600 deaths (13%; 39,531 person-years) in COPDGene and 214 deaths (6.3%; 16,629 person-years) in SUMMIT. title: Pleuroparenchymal fibroelastosis in a UK tertiary ILD centre: determinants of radiological progression and survival.
abstract: Pleuroparenchymal fibroelastosis (PPFE) is a rare form of interstitial lung disease (ILD). Some studies have shown that IPF patients with PPFE-like features have accelerated progression, poorer prognosis, and shorter telomeres. We examined the clinical, radiological, and physiological features of a UK PPFE cohort to identify the predictors of clinical outcomes. Methods A retrospective analysis was performed of consecutive patients with a multidisciplinary team (MDT) diagnosis of PPFE (February 2018 - 2026). A convenience sample of 70 consecutive IPF (Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis) patients was used as a comparator cohort. Baseline demographics, complications, pulmonary function decline at 1-year, radiological progression, and mortality were assessed. Radiological progression was determined by visual scoring of serial CT scans. Kaplan-Meier survival analysis with log-rank testing compared survival between cohorts, and multivariable Cox regression identified predictors of PPFE radiological progression and mortality. Results Forty-three patients had an MDT diagnosis of PPFE. Compared with IPF patients, those with PPFE were younger (71 vs 75 years), more frequently female (55.8% vs 15.7%), and more likely to be never-smokers (60.5% vs 18.6%). PPFE patients had lower BMI, lower FEV1, higher TLCO, and were more likely to have a history of recurrent infections, pneumothorax, or pneumomediastinum (all p<0.05), while FVC was comparable between groups. Co-existing ILD was present in 53% of PPFE patients, most commonly definite or probable UIP (65%). Among patients who underwent genetic testing, 88% (7/8) had a telomere biology-related gene variant. There were no significant differences in one-year lung function decline or overall survival between PPFE and IPF patients, irrespective of co-existing ILD. Baseline FVC% predicted independently predicted radiological progression, while age, baseline FVC% predicted, and change in FVC% predicted were independent predictors of mortality in PPFE. Conclusions PPFE exhibits a distinctive phenotype characterised by younger age, female predominance, low BMI and frequent pleural complications, survival was comparable to IPF. Baseline FVC emerged as a common predictor of both mortality and radiological progression , supporting its use as a pragmatic prognostic marker while highlighting the need for prospective validation.

title: Advances in Prognostic Assessment of Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis: From Clinical-Physiological Parameters and Molecular Biomarkers to Multimodal Models.
abstract: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) is a chronic progressive fibrotic lung disease with an extremely poor prognosis, and the rate of disease progression varies significantly among patients. Therefore, accurate prognostic assessment is crucial for clinical management. Traditional pulmonary function parameters, such as the absolute value of forced vital capacity (FVC) and the rate of decline in FVC as a percentage of predicted value (FVC%), serve as important bases for predicting disease progression and mortality. In recent years, prognostic prediction models have evolved from single indicators to composite scoring systems that integrate physiological, imaging, clinical manifestations, and even biomarkers. Furthermore, emerging indicators such as quantitative assessment of fibrosis extent on high-resolution computed tomography (HRCT), serum biomarkers, and artificial intelligence-based radiomics analysis provide powerful tools for earlier and more accurate identification of patients at risk of rapid disease progression. However, how to effectively incorporate these emerging indicators into clinical practice and clinical trials remains a current challenge. Future research should focus on validating and optimizing multi-omics prediction models, exploring their application value in individualized risk stratification and guiding treatment decisions for patients, with the ultimate goal of improving the long-term prognosis of IPF patients.

title: Diaphragm ultrasound beyond numbers: A call for Bayesian reasoning in critical care.
abstract: Diaphragm ultrasound (DUS) has become a widely available tool in critical care for assessing respiratory muscle function, monitoring ventilator-induced diaphragm dysfunction (VIDD), and supporting weaning prediction. However, its expanding use as a routine or screening examination, including in clinical scenarios where the pre-test probability of clinically relevant diaphragm dysfunction is low, raises concerns about diagnostic overuse. This narrative opinion article argues that DUS should be understood through the lens of Bayesian reasoning applied to clinical decision-making. The framework is intended to strengthen clinical reasoning rather than to assert superiority over alternative diagnostic strategies. Without explicit estimation of pre-test probability and prior definition of decision thresholds, the positive predictive value of DUS decreases, favoring false-positive findings, physiological overinterpretation, and potentially inappropriate clinical decisions. The available evidence indicates substantial heterogeneity in protocols, populations, and cut-off values, limiting the generalizability of findings and reinforcing the need for clinical contextualization. We propose a conceptual repositioning of DUS as a confirmatory and integrative tool, grounded in genuine clinical uncertainty, explicit Bayesian reasoning, and value-based care.

title: Foot-to-foot lower-limb phase angle as a predictor of reduced exercise capacity in patients with interstitial lung disease: A comparative study with muscle mass and pulmonary function.
abstract: Background Reduced exercise capacity, measured by the 6-min walk distance (6MWD), is a critical prognostic factor in interstitial lung disease (ILD). However, conventional physiological markers often fail to identify early functional decline. We aimed to evaluate whether the foot-to-foot lower-limb phase angle (F-F PhA), a non-invasive surrogate marker of muscle quality, predicts reduced exercise capacity better than traditional muscle mass and pulmonary function indices. Methods In this retrospective study of 68 patients with ILD, F-F PhA was measured using bioelectrical impedance analysis, and erector spinae muscle area (ESM_CSA) via computed tomography. Reduced exercise capacity was defined as 6MWD < 450 m. Multivariable logistic regression models adjusted for age and pulmonary function (%DL CO or %FVC), with internal validation performed via 1000-resample bootstrapping. Results In multivariable analysis, F-F PhA was independently associated with a 6MWD < 450 m when adjusted for age and %DL CO (OR: 0.228, 95% CI: 0.088-0.591, p = 0.002; bootstrap p = 0.005) or %FVC (OR: 0.213, 95% CI: 0.091-0.496, p = 0.001; bootstrap p = 0.001). ROC analysis showed F-F PhA had the highest discriminative accuracy (AUC: 0.802), outperforming %DL CO (AUC: 0.729) and ESM_CSA (AUC: 0.701). Combining age, %DL CO , and F-F PhA achieved the highest performance (AUC: 0.833). Conclusions F-F PhA serves as a robust, independent indicator for predicting reduced exercise capacity in ILD, outperforming conventional muscle mass. As a non-invasive tool, F-F PhA complements established functional tests in screening for early physical decline.

title: Predicting Progressive Pulmonary Fibrosis in Idiopathic Inflammatory Myopathy-associated Interstitial Lung Disease: A Machine Learning Approach Integrating Quantitative CT and Clinical Features.
abstract: Background The prognosis of progressive pulmonary fibrosis (PPF) in idiopathic inflammatory myopathy-associated interstitial lung disease (IIM-ILD) is poor, and current strategies for predicting its development are limited. This study aimed to use machine learning to integrate quantitative computed tomography (QCT) and clinical features to predict PPF in patients with IIM-ILD. Methods We retrospectively included 180 IIM-ILD patients, of whom 86 developed PPF. We randomly assigned patients to training and validation sets in a 7:3 ratio. Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression and univariate analysis were employed to select the most predictive features. We independently trained 8 machine learning algorithms. Model performance was evaluated by receiver operating characteristic curves, area under the curve (AUC) values, and decision curve analysis. Results 16 key clinical features and 7 QCT variables were selected for model development. The 10 variables with the highest contribution values were subsequently selected for the PPF prediction model. The clinical variables included Krebs von den Lungen-6, interleukin-6, percent-predicted forced expiratory volume in 1 second, carcinoembryonic antigen, ferritin, CD3 + T cells, natural killer cells, and CD19 + B cells. The QCT signatures included ILD Honeycomb Volume (%) Lt Lower + Rt Lower and ILD Consolidation Volume (%) Whole Lung. Among the 8 machine learning algorithms, the Random Forest model demonstrated the best predictive performance, with AUCs of 0.821 (95% CI: 0.680-0.925) in the training cohort and 0.943 (95% CI: 0.866-0.982) in the validation cohort. Conclusions The integration of QCT and clinical features using machine learning offers a potential non-invasive approach for predicting PPF in patients with IIM-ILD. This strategy may facilitate the early identification of individuals at high risk of PPF and potentially support timely clinical intervention.

title: Astrocytic activity in treatment-resistant and ultra-treatment-resistant schizophrenia.
abstract: Astrocytic dysfunction has been implicated in schizophrenia, but biomarkers of astrocytic activity have shown inconsistent patterns. Studies on disease heterogeneity, specifically treatment-resistant schizophrenia (TRS) and ultra-treatment-resistant schizophrenia (UTRS) are lacking. In this study, plasma glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP) was measured using an ultrasensitive Simoa assay in 174 participants (58 controls, 35 first-degree relatives, and 81 patients with TRS, according to Treatment Response and Resistance in Psychosis (TRRIP) criteria. A further n = 35 fulfilled TRRIP criteria for UTRS. Data included symptom severity, cognition, and functioning assessments. Cortical thickness was measured with magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). Associations between GFAP and demographic, clinical, cognitive, and imaging variables were examined using regression models adjusted for age, sex, and BMI. Plasma GFAP concentrations did not differ between controls and TRS or UTRS participants. GFAP showed no associations with symptom severity, cognition, functioning, or cortical thickness. Duration of illness showed a significant interaction with UTRS diagnosis associated to higher GFAP levels (b = 3.67, 95% CI 1.62-5.72, p < 0.001), while individuals with TRS showed the opposite pattern. The axonal marker neurofilament light chain (NfL), showed a positive relationship with disease duration in both disease categories. The results suggest that plasma GFAP does not act as diagnostic or severity marker in schizophrenia, but can highlight astroglial-related processes where UTRS and TRS show different trajectories.

title: NU-1025 modulates immunogenic cell death in bladder cancer: A multi-omics insight.
abstract: Immune checkpoint blockade has shown limited efficacy in bladder cancer, underscoring the need for therapeutic strategies that enhance tumor immunogenicity. Immunogenic cell death (ICD) can stimulate adaptive immunity and remodel the tumor microenvironment, yet its comprehensive landscape and druggable potential in bladder cancer remain unexplored. Here, we performed integrative bioinformatics analysis of transcriptomic data from TCGA and GEO bladder cancer cohorts to characterize ICD-associated subtypes, construct a prognostic risk model, and analyze immune infiltration. Connectivity Map (CMap) database and the XSum algorithm were employed for computational drug screening. Molecular docking was used to predict interactions between candidate compounds and immune checkpoint proteins. In silico ADMET and toxicology profiles were evaluated. The clinical relevance was assessed through independent CT urography imaging and PD-L1 immunohistochemistry data. Two ICD molecular subtypes were identified with distinct prognostic and microenvironment features. An eight-gene ICD risk model was established and validated, effectively stratifying patients into high- and low-risk groups with differential survival, immune cell infiltration, and tumor mutational burden. Through computational screening, NU-1025 was nominated as a top candidate capable of reversing the high-risk gene expression pattern. In silico profiling indicated favorable drug-like properties and low toxicity risk. Clinical data analysis revealed that high-grade bladder tumors frequently exhibit low PD-L1 expression, aligning with the predicted need for ICD-inducing agents. Overall, this research decodes the ICD landscape in bladder cancer and, via a computational drug repurposing pipeline, nominates NU-1025 as a novel candidate with predicted ICD-inducing and/or immune checkpoint modulatory activity.

title: Association of Spinal Epidural Lipomatosis With Systemic Lipid Metabolism in Patients With Lumbar Spinal Stenosis: A Propensity Score-Matched Study.
abstract: Background context Spinal epidural lipomatosis (SEL) is often regarded as a local consequence of obesity, yet its relationship with systemic lipid metabolism and symptom severity in lumbar spinal stenosis remains unclear. Apolipoprotein B (ApoB) is central to atherogenic lipid transport and ectopic fat deposition. Examining the association between systemic lipid metabolic abnormalities, including elevated ApoB levels, and epidural fat accumulation may provide insights into the metabolic pathogenesis and clinical relevance of SEL. Purpose To determine whether SEL is associated with systemic lipid metabolic abnormalities and greater preoperative symptom burden in patients undergoing surgery for lumbar spinal stenosis (LSS). Study design Retrospective, propensity score-matched cohort study. Patient sample A consecutive series of 1,145 patients who underwent posterior decompression for symptomatic LSS between December 2023 and December 2025. After 1:1 propensity score matching, 90 patients with SEL were compared with 90 patients without SEL. Outcome measures Serum lipid and other biochemical markers, epidural fat/spinal canal (EF/SpC) index on lumbar magnetic resonance imaging, Oswestry Disability Index (ODI), and visual analog scale (VAS) scores for leg and back pain. Methods SEL was diagnosed and graded on preoperative lumbar MRI according to the Borré classification, using the epidural fat/spinal canal index. Propensity score matching was performed for age, sex, body mass index (BMI), smoking history, drinking history, hypertension, and diabetes. Biochemical variables and preoperative clinical scores were compared between matched SEL and non-SEL patients. Conditional logistic regression was used to identify factors associated with SEL. BMI-adjusted partial Spearman correlation analyses were performed to evaluate associations between the EF/SpC index and biochemical markers. Regression-based trend analyses were conducted to assess changes in lipid-related markers across increasing SEL severity grades. Results Among 1,145 patients with LSS, 105 (9.2%) met the diagnostic criteria for SEL. After matching, 90 patients with SEL were compared with 90 non-SEL controls. The SEL group had higher apolipoprotein B (ApoB) levels than controls, as well as higher low-density lipoprotein cholesterol, triglycerides, and total cholesterol. ApoB remained independently associated with SEL in conditional logistic regression (odds ratio per 0.1 g/L, 1.141; 95% confidence interval, 1.019-1.277; P=0.022). Within the SEL group, the EF/SpC index correlated positively with triglycerides (ρ=0.43, q<0.001) and ApoB (ρ=0.40, q=0.002), while atherogenic lipid markers increased progressively with SEL severity. Patients with SEL also showed higher Oswestry Disability Index and leg-pain visual analog scale scores, whereas back-pain scores were similar between groups. Conclusion In patients undergoing surgery for LSS, SEL was associated with a more atherogenic lipid profile after matching for BMI and other major baseline characteristics, as well as greater preoperative disability and leg pain. The association of ApoB with SEL, together with the graded relationships of ApoB and triglycerides with epidural fat burden, suggests that SEL may reflect systemic lipid metabolic dysfunction rather than local epidural fat deposition alone.

title: Postembolization CT Digital Subtraction Angiography for Assessing Spinal Tumor Devascularization: Concordance With Catheter Angiography and Association With Surgical Blood Loss.
abstract: Background context The adequacy of preoperative embolization for spinal tumors is commonly assessed using selective catheter angiography, but standardized criteria remain lacking. Postembolization CT digital subtraction angiography (CT-DSA) may provide complementary whole-tumor assessment of residual enhancement. Purpose To evaluate concordance between postembolization CT-DSA and catheter angiography, examine associations between CT-DSA findings and surgical blood loss, and identify factors associated with less favorable CT-DSA findings. Design Retrospective single-center observational cohort study. Patient sample Seventy-two adults who underwent preoperative embolization and postembolization CT-DSA before spinal tumor surgery, including 62 patients with metastatic tumors and 10 with primary spinal neoplasms. Outcome measures Concordance between CT-DSA and catheter angiographic devascularization categories, estimated blood loss (EBL), quantitative CT-DSA peak enhancement index, and factors associated with less favorable CT-DSA categories. Methods Postembolization devascularization was classified as complete, subtotal, or partial using modality-specific criteria. Concordance was evaluated using cross-classification and linearly weighted κ. Associations between CT-DSA findings and EBL were analyzed in patients with metastatic tumors using multivariable regression adjusted for surgical invasiveness and baseline angiographic hypervascularity. Proportional-odds ordinal regression was used to explore factors associated with less favorable CT-DSA categories. Results CT-DSA and catheter angiography assigned the same devascularization category in 39 of 72 patients (54.2%), with moderate weighted concordance (κ=0.423; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.265-0.580). Among patients with metastatic tumors, median EBL was 1,000 mL for complete, 1,650 mL for subtotal, and 1,975 mL for partial devascularization (P=.214). The adjusted overall association between CT-DSA category and EBL was not statistically significant (P=.167). Compared with complete devascularization, partial devascularization showed a directionally higher but imprecise EBL estimate (adjusted EBL ratio, 1.582; 95% CI, 0.861-2.907; P=.139). The quantitative peak enhancement index was not associated with EBL. Greater baseline angiographic hypervascularity (adjusted odds ratio [OR] per grade, 3.243; 95% CI, 1.782-5.902) and a same-level spinal artery (adjusted OR, 10.236; 95% CI, 2.477-42.293) were associated with less favorable CT-DSA categories. Conclusions Postembolization CT-DSA showed moderate concordance with catheter angiography and may complement selective angiographic assessment by depicting residual enhancement throughout the tumor. Partial devascularization showed a directionally higher but imprecise association with surgical blood loss in metastatic tumors and requires further validation.

title: Robotic-assisted transduodenal ampullectomy for a neuroendocrine tumour: A step-by-step surgical video.
abstract: Background When endoscopic resection of ampullary neuroendocrine tumors (NETs) is not feasible due to tumour size or location, transduodenal ampullectomy can offer a parenchymal-sparing alternative to a formal pancreaticoduodenectomy (Whipple procedure) [1,2]. We present a robotic-assisted transduodenal ampullectomy (RATA) in a 71-year-old male with an incidental 14 mm ampullary NET found during routine screening. Preoperative 68 Ga-DOTATATE PET-CT demonstrated intense somatostatin-receptor avidity (SUVmax 66.8) and absent FDG uptake. The MDT recommended surgical excision due to size and Ki-67 4%. Methods Following right colonic flexure mobilisation and a Kocher maneuver, the cystic duct was isolated and cannulated with a 4 Fr catheter to guide biliary identification. After a longitudinal duodenotomy, the ampullary lesion was visualized. Submucosal saline-adrenaline was injected in the submucosal plane. Diathermy scissors were used to perform a circumferential mucosal and muscularis dissection. Biliary and pancreatic ducts were sharply divided and reconstructed using interrupted 5/0 polydioxanone sutures between the pancreatobiliary ducts and the duodenal mucosa after positioning a 6 Fr catheter in the pancreatic duct. The duodenotomy was closed in two layers using a 4/0 absorbable barbed suture, and a methylene blue leak test through the nasogastric tube confirmed duodenal integrity. Results The procedure was completed successfully with no intraoperative complications. A postoperative contrast-enhanced CT on day 5 demonstrated no collections and no oral contrast extravasation. Oral feeding was gradually reintroduced, the abdominal drain was removed, and the patient was discharged on day 7. Following a brief readmission on day 13 for a pulmonary microembolism successfully treated with medical therapy, the patient recovered fully and remains disease-free 7 months after surgery. Conclusion RATA can represent a safe, feasible, and pancreas-preserving alternative to formal pancreaticoduodenectomy for well-differentiated ampullary NETs in selected patients. The robotic platform enhances three-dimensional visualization and wrist articulation, optimizing the delicate micro-reconstruction of the pancreaticobiliary junction.

title: Diagnostic accuracy and clinical impact of ocular fundus imaging in the emergency department: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: Ocular fundus visualization is often limited in emergency departments (EDs), where direct ophthalmoscopy is infrequently performed and may fail to detect vision- or life-threatening pathology. Fundus imaging offers digitally-acquired, remotely-viewable images that may address this gap, but evidence remains fragmented. We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis to evaluate diagnostic performance, image gradeability, and operational outcomes of emergency department (ED) fundus imaging. Following PROSPERO registration (CRD420251126786), we searched ten databases from inception to September 2026, in accordance with PRISMA and PRISMA-DTA guidelines. Studies on diagnostic performance, image gradability, or operational impact of ED fundus imaging were included. Pooled diagnostic sensitivity, specificity, and hierarchical summary receiver operating characteristic area under the curve (HSROC AUC) were estimated using a bivariate random-effects model. Risk of bias was assessed using QUADAS-2 and ROBINS-I, and certainty of evidence using GRADE. In total, 33 studies (6593 patients) met the inclusion criteria. Low-certainty evidence suggested moderate-to-good diagnostic performance. Pooled sensitivity was 0.78 (95% CI: 0.66-0.87), pooled specificity was 0.91 (95% CI: 0.86-0.94), and HSROC AUC was 0.93. Diagnostic performance appeared broadly consistent across imaging modalities, indications, readers, and interpretation settings. Very-low-certainty evidence suggested high pooled image gradability (0.854, 95% CI: 0.796-0.897). In-person ophthalmology consultation was avoided in a pooled 0.416 (95% CI: 0.326-0.512) of consultation requests. Pooled results suggest moderate-to-good diagnostic performance and high image gradability of ED fundus imaging, with possible operational impact. These findings support further evaluation of fundus imaging as a tool to facilitate emergency ophthalmic and teleophthalmology-enabled care pathways.

title: Artificial intelligence in diabetic retinopathy: From deep learning to foundation models, clinical translation, and real-world deployment.
abstract: Diabetic retinopathy (DR) remains a leading cause of preventable vision impairment worldwide, with its burden increasing in parallel with the global diabetes pandemic. As a progressive microvascular disorder with neurovascular unit involvement, DR is driven by retinal ischemia, inflammation, and pathological neovascularization, while diabetic macular edema (DME) continues to represent a principal cause of vision loss. This structured narrative review provides a critical synthesis of advances in diabetic retinopathy diagnosis, retinal imaging, treatment strategies, and artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled screening published from January 2020 through March 2026, while selectively incorporating earlier landmark studies to provide clinical and methodological context. We summarize contemporary screening pathways and emerging retinal imaging modalities, including ultra-widefield photography (up to ~200° field of view), optical coherence tomography (OCT), and OCT angiography, examining how complementary structural and vascular biomarkers are reshaping disease severity assessment and DME characterization. We then review the evolution of AI methodologies, highlighting a transition from task-specific convolutional neural network pipelines toward transformer-based and self-supervised representation learning, including retina-specific foundation models designed to reduce annotation burden and improve robustness and generalizability under domain shift. Beyond algorithmic performance on curated benchmarks, we emphasize key translational requirements for clinical adoption, including model calibration, uncertainty-aware triage, image quality control, and external validation across imaging devices and diverse populations. Recent prospective and implementation studies across diverse healthcare systems demonstrate that the real-world effectiveness of AI-enabled DR screening depends not only on diagnostic accuracy but also on image gradability, clinically appropriate operating thresholds, uncertainty management, external validation, referral capacity, and integration with established care pathways. Evidence from the Asia-Pacific region provides important examples of these implementation challenges in heterogeneous and resource-constrained screening environments. Specific attention is given to the identification and mitigation strategies for fundus pigmentation-related performance disparities and the governance of autonomous versus hybrid human-AI screening models within evolving regulatory frameworks. Finally, we examine emerging work in oculomics for systemic risk stratification and propose a pragmatic clinical readiness framework centered on validation hierarchy, safety monitoring, and workflow integration. Particular emphasis is placed on the translational readiness of foundation models, multimodal retinal intelligence, and emerging technologies for large-scale screening, therapeutic decision-making, and longitudinal disease monitoring.

title: Peripheral exudative hemorrhagic chorioretinopathy: A comprehensive review of clinical features, differential diagnosis, pathogenesis-related disease spectra, and management.
abstract: Peripheral exudative hemorrhagic chorioretinopathy (PEHCR) is a peripheral chorioretinopathy characterized by retinal pigment epithelium detachment with either blood, exudation, or both, and may present with macular hemorrhage, macular exudation, and vitreous hemorrhage. PEHCR exhibits a variety of features on fundus fluorescein angiography, indocyanine green angiography, and ultrasound examinations. The hemorrhagic type PEHCR may greatly resemble malignant melanoma, whereas the exudative type can mimics primary vitreoretinal lymphoma making differential diagnosis of great importance. The pathogenesis may involve choroidal neovascularization. Early studies suggested a link to age-related macular degeneration, while subsequent research has revealed a close association with polypoidal choroidal vasculopathy and pachychoroid disease spectrum. Most cases of PEHCR are self-limiting and may be observed alone. For those complicated by, or at risk of, macular exudation, macular hemorrhage, as well as vitreous hemorrhage, management strategies include intravitreal anti-vascular endothelial growth factor injections, vitrectomy, laser photocoagulation, photodynamic therapy, and cryotherapy.

title: Pediatric acute myocarditis: current evidence and practical recommendations.
abstract: Acute myocarditis (AM) in children and adolescents remains a diagnostic and therapeutic challenge because of its heterogeneous presentation, overlap with dilated cardiomyopathy, and potential for fulminant deterioration, with approximately 5.9% risk of early mortality. We performed a narrative review integrating contemporary guidelines, consensus documents, and weighted analyses from systematically selected large pediatric cohorts to summarize current evidence on epidemiology, diagnosis, risk stratification, and treatment. Pediatric AM shows a male predominance and a bimodal age distribution. Early recognition is often difficult because initial manifestations may be non-specific and the differential diagnosis varies across age groups. Younger children more often present with dilated phenotypes and prominent gastrointestinal symptoms, frequently reflecting low cardiac output and systemic congestion, whereas adolescents may present with an uncomplicated phenotype characterized by chest pain and regional wall motion abnormalities. Severe disease remains a relevant burden, with fulminant myocarditis accounting for approximately one quarter of cases and carrying markedly higher mortality. Initial evaluation should therefore focus on early risk stratification, integrating clinical severity, biomarkers, electrocardiogram, echocardiography, and etiological testing. This approach may help identify high-risk viral phenotypes associated with enteroviruses or parvovirus B19, while also recognizing systemic inflammatory syndromes such as multisystem inflammatory syndrome in children, which may mimic AM but usually responds to timely immunomodulatory treatment. We propose a practical risk-based strategy that classifies patients into low-, intermediate-, and high-risk groups to guide monitoring, referral, cardiac magnetic resonance, endomyocardial biopsy, and therapy. High-risk patients require early referral to tertiary centers with pediatric intensive care, cardiac surgery, and temporary mechanical circulatory support availability. Treatment should be individualized according to risk, ranging from supportive care to mechanical circulatory support, transplant evaluation, and selected immunomodulation. Prospective registries and randomized trials are needed to validate risk-based pathways and define evidence-based therapies.

title: Singleton freemartinism in cattle: A structured narrative review and historical case reappraisal.
abstract: Freemartinism classically affects a female calf gestated with a male co-twin. A female may be born as an apparent singleton when a male co-conceptus is lost after placental vascular communication has permitted cellular exchange and exposure to testicular products. This structured narrative review and historical case reappraisal evaluates evidence for singleton freemartinism, clarifies diagnostic boundaries and reassesses a 1995 case following multiple-embryo transfer. PubMed, Scopus and FAO AGRIS were searched through 14 September 2026, supplemented by citation searching. Evidence supports the existence of singleton freemartinism but does not establish its prevalence. An apparent singleton birth does not demonstrate that gestation was singleton throughout. In an appropriate developmental context, persistent XX/XY blood chimerism, the coexistence of XX and XY blood-cell populations, is evidence that fetal cell exchange occurred. Detection of a Y-linked sequence establishes only that target DNA is present in the specimen. Neither finding alone demonstrates male-type reproductive-tract development or pathological freemartinism. Diagnosis therefore requires integration of gestational history, characterized chromosome-based or molecular findings, reproductive anatomy, functional findings and histopathology. Archival sections show ovarian follicles and testis-like tubular structures in the same gonad. Interpretation is limited by the unknown sex of the lost embryo, incomplete gonadal examination, lack of cell-level localization and cell-type identification, and unknown fertility. Twinning, multiple-embryo transfer and conceptus loss may increase opportunities for the condition to arise, but evidence demonstrates neither increased prevalence nor a quantitative contribution to reproductive failure. Prospective multicenter studies linking gestational records with molecular, anatomical and functional outcomes are required.

title: The corpus luteum transcriptome is dysregulated in dairy cows with mastitis.
abstract: Mastitis-induced inflammation in dairy cows can trigger premature luteolysis and subsequent pregnancy loss; however, the molecular mechanisms underlying these effects remain poorly understood. This study aimed to characterize changes in gene expression in the corpus luteum of cows with clinical or subclinical mastitis compared with healthy cows. Multiparous pregnant cows from a commercial pasture-based dairy herd were classified into three groups: subclinical mastitis (SCM; n = 6), clinical mastitis (CLM; n = 6), and healthy controls (CON; n = 5), based on California Mastitis Test scores and somatic cell counts. Corpus luteum biopsies were collected at pregnancy diagnosis, between 28 and 42 days post-insemination, using a transvaginal ultrasound-guided technique and subjected to RNA sequencing. Differential expression analysis identified 428 differentially expressed genes (DEG) between CLM and CON cows (263 upregulated and 165 downregulated), 186 between SCM and CON cows (76 upregulated and 110 downregulated), and 391 between CLM and SCM cows (236 upregulated and 155 downregulated; FDR < 0.05). Functional enrichment of DEG between CLM and CON showed dysregulation of pathways related to immune response, cortisol, GnRH, and oxytocin signaling. These transcriptional changes may reflect an adaptive luteoprotective response aimed at maintaining luteal function under systemic inflammatory stress. Overall, the results demonstrate that mastitis, particularly in its clinical form, markedly alters the luteal transcriptome during early pregnancy, potentially affecting corpus luteum function and contributing to an increased risk of pregnancy loss.

title: Development of the eye in grass carp (Ctenopharyngodon idella): Ocular histomorphology, corneal surface ultrastructure, and retinal calretinin and tyrosine hydroxylase immunoreactivity.
abstract: Eye posthatching development was examined in grass carp (Ctenopharyngodon idella) from 1 day posthatching (1 dph) to 365 dph. Eye histology and morphometry, retinal expression of calretinin (CR) and tyrosine hydroxylase (TH), and corneal ultrastructure were studied using light and scanning electron microscopy. Basic eye structure was detectable at 1 dph, though important features, including retina and iris pigmentation as well as photoreceptor differentiation, were delayed till 4 dph. Differentiated photoreceptors seemed to emerge at 4 dph with evident increases in their count and shape diversity at 20 dph. The corneal surface epithelium appeared smooth at 20 dph. However, it featured corrugations and micropits at 60 dph, excessive desquamations at 90 dph, and distinct intercellular boundaries at 365 dph. Iris differentiation was evident at 20 dph. The annular ligament was seen at the iridocorneal junction at 20 dph with noticeable intracellular coarse secretory granules in yearling fish. The choroidal rete appeared massively filled by blood at 90 dph. Morphometrically, eye diameter and corneal thickness increased markedly between 20 dph and 365 dph. While the iris and central parts of the retina showed a rapid increase in thickness between 4 dph and 20 dph. Immunohistochemically, CR- and TH-immunoreactive cells were detected in the retina from 1 dph onwards, with CR localized to the inner nuclear and ganglion cell layers and TH to the inner nuclear layer. Numbers of immunoreactive cells per mm 2 peaked at 90 dph for CR and 20 dph for TH, suggesting a differential timeline for their activities. CR immunoreactive cells were equally distributed between central and peripheral parts of the retina. While TH immunoreactive cells revealed a significantly higher count at the peripheral parts of the retina between 20 dph and 365 dph. This study characterizes early posthatching ocular development in C. idella and provides a reference for future studies of the cyprinid eye.

title: Msx1 orchestrates retinal progenitor cell homeostasis from mechanical locking to synthetic arrest through the PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway.
abstract: Despite the known association between the muscle segment homeobox 1 (Msx1) gene and neural diseases, its function in maintaining homeostasis in adult retinal progenitor cells (RPCs) unclear. We using an in vitro adult RPC model combined with short hairpin RNA-mediated knockdown, RNA sequencing, and tandem mass tag -based proteomics define Msx1 as a homeostatic rheostat that orchestrates cell structural dynamics and metabolic signaling pathways. We demonstrate that Msx1 loss triggers a mechanical locking state, defined by a paradoxical uncoupling of actomyosin dynamics: elevated Myh14 coexists with global attenuation of stability factors (Cnn1, Mad2l1b), causing aberrant punctate aggregation of Rho-GTPases and arresting cell movement, with subsequent metabolic paralysis through suppression PI3K/AKT signaling and induction of G2/M cell cycle arrest. Ultimately, these events converge toward synthetic arrest by the transcriptional translational decoupling of ribosomal protein large subunit hubs. These results indicate a severe blockade of de novo protein synthesis. Our findings indicate that Msx1 knockdown not only inhibit cell cycle progression but also disrupt the homeostatic rheostat, causing RPCs to undergo irreversible fate failure via a cascade of mechanical, metabolic, and synthetic failures. This regulatory model offers new insights into retinal regeneration, suggesting that therapeutic restoration of cytoskeletal and translational homeostasis may be required to re-establish the remodeling competence of retinal progenitor cells in degenerative retinal diseases.

title: Baseline MRI markers and clinical outcomes during anti-amyloid β therapy: A real-world study in a Japanese dementia center.
abstract: Importance Predictors of decline and of amyloid-related imaging abnormalities (ARIA) during anti-amyloid β therapy in routine care are undefined. Objective To identify baseline predictors of cognitive, functional, and safety outcomes. Design, setting, and participants Retrospective cohort of 161 consecutive patients initiating anti-amyloid β therapy at a Tokyo dementia center, 2024 to 2026 (lecanemab, 89; donanemab, 72). Exposures Lecanemab or donanemab. Main outcomes and measures Change in MMSE and CDR-Sum of Boxes (CDR-SB); baseline medial temporal atrophy (VSRAD Z score), amyloid PET burden, and microbleeds; ARIA. Results With lecanemab, MMSE and CDR-SB declined significantly at every assessment (CDR-SB +0.79, +1.10, +1.60 at 6, 12, 18 months); memory and orientation declined while language was preserved. Greater baseline medial temporal atrophy was associated with greater 12-month CDR-SB worsening (r = 0.39; P = .01; n = 40); patients in the most severe standard category (Z ≥ 3) worsened by 2.62 versus 0.64 points (adjusted β = +2.18; P < .001). Atrophy was associated with older age (r = 0.19; P = .03) and with baseline memory-related measures - ADAS-Cog score (r = 0.32; P < .001) and the MMSE subdomains of delayed recall (β = -0.25; P = .006) and time orientation (β = -0.30; P = .04) - but not MMSE total score. Amyloid PET burden showed no significant association at most time points. All ARIA events were asymptomatic; ARIA-H occurred in 6 of 25 with microbleeds versus 3 of 136 without (odds ratio, 14.0; P < .001). Donanemab follow-up was 6 months. Conclusions and relevance Baseline medial temporal atrophy was associated with functional decline and microbleeds with ARIA-H. Pretreatment MRI may provide prognostic and safety information during anti-amyloid β therapy.

title: A dual-tower multimodal framework with feature quality enhancement for predicting pathological complete response after neoadjuvant chemotherapy in breast cancer: a multicenter study.
abstract: Background Pathological complete response (pCR) is a key endpoint following neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NAC) in breast cancer, with potential to guide treatment adaptation and surgical de-escalation. However, limited generalizability across institutions remains a major challenge due to heterogeneous imaging protocols (scanner vendors, field strengths, and acquisition parameters) and diverse patient populations, which can cause significant domain shifts in model performance. This study develops and externally validates a multimodal framework for post-neoadjuvant, preoperative prediction of pCR using multiparametric MRI (mpMRI) and routinely available clinical data. Methods In a multicenter retrospective setting, 1291 patients from five institutions were enrolled and institutionally divided into a development cohort pooled from two centers (n=683) and three independent, single-center external validation cohorts (n=608). Model inputs comprised post-treatment mpMRI (dynamic contrast-enhanced and diffusion-weighted imaging) for deep feature extraction, clinicopathological variables, radiomics features from both pre- and post-treatment scans, and delta-radiomics features capturing longitudinal within-sequence changes (Δ = post - pre). A dual-tower attention network incorporating a Feature Quality Enhancer (FQE) module-which regularizes the latent space by promoting intra-class compactness, inter-class separability, and feature consistency-was designed to learn discriminative imaging representations. Deep, radiomic, and clinical features were then integrated through a hierarchical feature selection strategy, with robustness assessed via repeated experiments.. Predictive performance was evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) in both development and external validation cohorts. Results The proposed AIFPS achieved an AUC of 0.882 (95% CI: 0.855-0.905) in the development cohort. In external validation, AIFPS achieved the highest numerical AUCs (0.853, 0.888, and 0.895) and demonstrated statistically significant improvements over all single-modality models in all cohorts. While its superiority over certain dual-modality models did not reach statistical significance after correction for multiple comparisons, the full multimodal approach consistently yielded the numerically highest discrimination. Conclusion AIFPS integrates quality-enhanced deep imaging features with radiomics, including delta-radiomics, and clinicopathological variables to enable accurate and generalizable preoperative prediction of pathological complete response, particularly in HER2-positive disease, while further validation is required for triple-negative and luminal subtypes. Its application in luminal breast cancer requires further dedicated subtype-specific modeling. With prospective validation, this approach may support individualized treatment stratification following neoadjuvant chemotherapy.

title: Integrative single-cell and computational pathology analyses reveal a C11orf24-associated stem-like epithelial population linked to tumor microenvironment remodeling and immune evasion in bladder cancer.
abstract: Background Cancer stem-like cells drive tumor progression and therapeutic resistance, yet the epithelial stemness hierarchy in bladder cancer (BLCA) remains poorly defined. We aimed to characterize stemness-associated epithelial populations and their clinical significance. Methods We analyzed single-cell RNA sequencing data from 92,218 cells across 13 treatment-naïve BLCA samples to characterize epithelial stemness and tumor-microenvironment interactions. Spatial transcriptomics and independent bulk cohorts were used for orthogonal and clinical validation. An HStem-associated histopathology-based prognostic model was developed by integrating quantitative image features with deep-learning representations, followed by functional validation of the candidate gene C11orf24. Results We identified a highly stem-like epithelial population (HStem) at the apex of the differentiation hierarchy, exhibiting MYC activation, oxidative phosphorylation, and DNA repair enrichment, with preferential presence in advanced-stage tumors. HStem cells were inferred to serve as major communication hubs within the TME, interacting extensively with fibroblasts and endothelial cells via MIF-CD74/CXCR4 and MIF-CD74/CD44 axes. An 86-gene HStem signature enabled development of a robust image-based prognostic model. High-risk tumors showed immune exclusion, immunosuppressive enrichment, T-cell dysfunction, and predicted checkpoint blockade resistance. C11orf24 emerged as a candidate stemness-associated regulator; C11orf24-positive cells displayed enhanced stemness and stromal interactions. Functional experiments demonstrated that C11orf24 perturbation altered clonogenic growth, migration, and invasion in BLCA cells. Pharmacogenomic analyses identified predicted therapeutic vulnerabilities that warrant experimental validation. Conclusions We identify an HStem population associated with BLCA progression, microenvironmental remodeling, and immune evasion. Integrating single-cell and spatial transcriptomics with computational pathology, we establish a clinically relevant stemness framework and identify C11orf24 as a potential therapeutic target, offering opportunities for stemness-directed precision oncology.

title: Regional Expansion of Transplant Oncology: The First Case of Liver Transplantation for Unresectable Colorectal Liver Metastasis in the Gulf Region.
abstract: Introduction Liver transplantation for colorectal liver metastases (CRLM) has emerged as a potential curative option for highly selected patients with unresectable liver-only disease, with recent trials demonstrating 5-year overall survival rates of 55% to 83%. Surgical resection remains the only curative treatment for colorectal liver metastases (CRLM), but its applicability is limited, with only 25% of patients eligible. However, this approach remains investigational with limited global experience and has never been implemented in the Middle East region. Recently, liver transplantation (LT) has emerged as a potential curative option for select patients with unresectable liver-only metastases. This report highlights the potential for liver transplantation to serve as a curative modality in highly selected patients with CRLM and demonstrates its feasibility in a new geographic region. Case report We report the first case in the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) region of a 41-year-old male with unresectable CRLM who underwent LT following an aggressive multimodal pretransplant protocol. The patient was initially treated at an outside facility for synchronous left-sided colorectal cancer with liver metastases, achieving complete remission after FOLFOX chemotherapy. He subsequently developed 2 liver recurrences: the first in July 2023, with 17 metastases managed at the outside facility by surgical resection and chemotherapy; and the second in October 2023, with 40 metastases, treated with systemic chemotherapy and trans arterial radioembolization (TARE-Y90). He received additional treatment with ablative liver-directed therapies consistent with the "Cleveland Protocol." The patient subsequently underwent orthotopic liver transplantation. His postoperative course was complicated with moderate acute cellular rejection, which was successfully treated, and he was discharged on post-operative day 16. Conclusion This case demonstrates the successful implementation of liver transplantation for CRLM in the Gulf region, achieving disease-free survival at 4-month follow-up despite high-risk biological features typically associated with poor prognosis. It illustrates the feasibility and potential benefit of LT for unresectable CRLM in carefully selected patients, following an aggressive pretransplant locoregional therapy protocol modeled after the Cleveland Clinic approach. Key success factors included rigorous patient selection using established criteria (Oslo score 0, low Fong score, low PET-MTV), intensive pretransplant optimization with multimodal therapy, and experienced multidisciplinary management of post-transplant complications. With careful patient selection and integration of systemic and liver-directed therapies to achieve maximal disease control, this strategy may help expand transplant eligibility, possibly offering a curative approach. This case provides valuable regional data for the evolving role of transplant oncology in colorectal cancer management in a resource-limited setting.

title: Incidentally Diagnosed Pulmonary Embolism Two Months After Living Liver Donation in a Donor With Homozygous MTHFR A1298C Mutation: A Case Report.
abstract: Living donor liver transplantation (LDLT) is widely performed in countries with limited cadaveric organ donation. Although donor hepatectomy is generally safe, venous thromboembolic events such as pulmonary embolism (PE) remain rare but potentially life-threatening complications. Genetic thrombophilia, including methylenetetrahydrofolate reductase (MTHFR) mutations, may contribute to thrombotic risk. A 39-year-old female living liver donor underwent right donor hepatectomy for LDLT. The donor had no preoperative risk factors for venous thromboembolism, and a routine thrombophilia panel, including protein C, protein S, antithrombin III, factor V Leiden, and prothrombin gene mutations, was normal. Two months after surgery, an abdominal computed tomography (CT) scan performed due to fluid collection adjacent to the remnant liver in ultrasound (USG) during routine follow-up incidentally revealed partial PE. Pulmonary CT angiography confirmed the finding, while lower extremity Doppler USG showed no evidence of deep vein thrombosis. Laboratory tests revealed elevated D-dimer and homocysteine levels. Further genetic evaluation demonstrated a homozygous MTHFR A1298C mutation. The patient was treated with low molecular weight heparin followed by oral anticoagulant therapy for 6 months, resulting in complete radiological resolution of the embolism. PE after donor hepatectomy is rare but potentially fatal. This case suggests that MTHFR A1298C mutation may represent a previously underrecognized risk factor for venous thromboembolism in living liver donors. In populations with a high prevalence of MTHFR mutations, extended thrombophilia screening and appropriate thromboprophylaxis may help reduce the risk of postoperative thromboembolic complications.

title: Rapid Progression of Cardiac Allograft Vasculopathy With Sudden Cardiac Death Within the First Year of Heart Transplantation: A Case Report.
abstract: Cardiac allograft vasculopathy (CAV) is a major cause of mortality and morbidity within the first 3 years of heart transplantation (HT). CAV results in progressive coronary artery stenosis and may lead to arrhythmias and sudden cardiac death. In some cases, sudden cardiac death represents the initial presentation of CAV, as cardiac denervation blunts anginal symptoms that otherwise could have preceded sudden cardiac death (SCD). Here, we describe the case of a 56-year-old man with non-ischemic cardiomyopathy. He underwent left ventricular assist device implantation followed by orthotopic HT. Five months after transplantation, he presented with atypical mid-sternal chest discomfort initially thought to be musculoskeletal in origin. Routine coronary angiography at 12 months revealed severe, diffuse 3-vessel disease consistent with International Society of Heart and Lung Transplantation (ISHLT) CAV-3, and cardiac MRI revealed full thickness delayed enhancement in the inferior wall consistent with infarction. Despite overall preserved left ventricular ejection fraction, he developed polymorphic ventricular tachycardia (VT) with an appropriate shock from a wearable cardioverter-defibrillator (WCD) and was transferred with an intra-aortic balloon pump to a larger transplant center and underwent another heart transplantation. This case highlights rapid CAV progression leading to infarction and arrhythmia despite preserved LVEF, emphasizing the need for enhanced screening with biomarkers and imaging as well as earlier consideration for device-based strategies to prevent sudden cardiac death in high-risk transplant recipients.

title: Inadvertent Coronary Sinus Cannulation During Central Venous Catheter Placement in a Liver Transplant Recipient with Persistent Left Superior Vena Cava: A Case Report.
abstract: Persistent left superior vena cava (PLSVC) is the most common thoracic venous anomaly and is usually asymptomatic. Central venous catheterization through a PLSVC can be challenging, and inadvertent advancement of catheters into the coronary sinus may result in arrhythmias, perforation, thrombosis, or inaccurate hemodynamic measurements. We report a case of coronary sinus cannulation by a left internal jugular dialysis catheter in a liver transplant recipient with previously unrecognized PLSVC. Initial chest radiography suggested catheter termination within a duplicated left superior vena cava; however, intraoperative transesophageal echocardiography (TEE) demonstrated the catheter tip within the coronary sinus. The catheter was withdrawn under direct echocardiographic guidance, avoiding potential complications. This case highlights the utility of intraoperative TEE for definitive localization of central venous catheters in patients with anomalous thoracic venous anatomy.

title: Evaluation of nanofibrillated cellulose as a urethral bulking agent in female dogs with acquired urethral sphincter mechanism incompetence: a prospective clinical study.
abstract: Urethral bulking agent (UBA) implantation is a minimally invasive, effective and safe alternative treatment for refractory urethral sphincter mechanism incompetence (USMI). However, repeated implantations are frequently needed to maintain continence. Therefore, a prospective interventional clinical study with eight client-owned neutered female dogs was designed to evaluate the clinical efficacy and 12-month outcome of nanofibrillated cellulose (NFC), a novel biomaterial as a UBA. Concurrent causes of urinary incontinence were excluded with clinical and neurological assessment, blood and urine sampling, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), retrograde vaginourethrography, cystoscopy, and urodynamic testing. A continence score (CS) was assigned before and after treatment, and monthly thereafter. Furthermore, the dogs were followed with MRI, retrograde vaginouretrography, and urethroscopy at 1 and 12 months or at the time of euthanasia or recurrence. All dogs were continent (CS ≥ 8/10) at 1 month with a significant increase in mean CS (p < 0.0001, difference 5.4, 95% CI 4.1-6.6). Median duration of continence was 8 months (IQR 4 - not estimable). At 12 months, the treatment response was still significant (p = 0.0010) with (n = 4/7) or without (n = 3/7) medical intervention. The imaging and urethroscopy findings suggest that flattening of the deposits with or without mucosal ulceration may contribute to recurrence. Sporadic bacterial cystitis was diagnosed in two dogs and recurrent cystitis in one. In conclusion, NFC showed promising short-term effect and a low complication rate when used as a UBA. Urinary incontinence resolved after single NFC implantation in all dogs for a median of 8 months without adjunctive treatment.

title: Sheep pulmonary image recognition (SPIRO): An explainable deep learning framework for macroscopic assessment of ovine pulmonary lesions.
abstract: Accurate detection and classification of pulmonary diseases in sheep are critical for ensuring animal welfare, food safety, and effective disease surveillance in abattoir settings. In this study, we propose a two-stage, explainable, histopathology-informed deep learning framework for the automated classification of ovine lung lesions. The dataset comprises 1052 sheep lung images, annotated through a dual-level diagnostic process involving macroscopic inspection and histopathological confirmation, and classified as healthy, inflammatory, or neoplastic. Four convolutional neural network architectures-VGG16, VGG19, ResNet50, and EfficientNetB0-were benchmarked under identical conditions. EfficientNetB0 achieved the highest observed standalone performance and was integrated into a two-stage pipeline, in which YOLOv11 first localized lung regions and EfficientNetB0 subsequently classified the cropped images. Model interpretability was evaluated using Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM). The YOLOv11-EfficientNetB0 pipeline achieved an overall test accuracy of 90% and a weighted F1-score of 0.88. Neoplastic lesions were classified with the highest performance, reaching precision, recall, and F1-score values of 0.98, 0.99, and 0.99, respectively, while healthy and inflammatory lungs achieved F1-scores of 0.83 and 0.82, respectively. Grad-CAM visualizations indicated that predictions were mainly driven by diagnostically relevant pulmonary regions. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of explainable artificial intelligence for objective, scalable, and biologically grounded post-mortem assessment of sheep lungs, with potential applications in abattoir surveillance, veterinary pathology, and flock health monitoring.

title: Automated Segmentation of Intrinsic Foot Muscles in Ultrasound Using Deep Neural Networks: Development and Validation Study.
abstract: Objective To develop and validate the first automated deep-learning image-processing framework for pixel-level segmentation of the plantar intrinsic foot muscles (PIMs) in ultrasound (US) images. This approach supports objective and reproducible US-based muscle segmentation from conventional B-mode images. Methods US images of four PIMs (abductor hallucis, flexor digitorum brevis (FDB), quadratus plantae [QP] and abductor digiti minimi) were collected from 200 healthy participants (n = 1099 images). Manual segmentations were used as ground truth. Three deep neural network architectures (U-Net, Feature Pyramid Network [FPN] and DeepLabV3+) with a Mix Transformer backbone were trained and evaluated. Model performance was assessed using the Intersection over Union (IoU) and Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC), two complementary pixel-level segmentation metrics. Agreement with manual measurements was evaluated using intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC), mean difference and standard error of measurement. Results All models demonstrated excellent segmentation performance, with mean IoU values ≥0.90 and mean DSC values ≥0.95 across all muscles. The highest accuracy was observed for the FDB (IoU = 0.95; DSC = 0.97), while QP showed slightly lower performance (IoU = 0.90; DSC = 0.95). FPN and DeepLabV3+ exhibited greater stability (SD: ±0.02-0.03) compared to U-Net (up to ±0.08). Agreement with manual segmentation was high for cross-sectional area (ICC: 0.836-0.960) and moderate-to-high for border length (ICC: 0.705-0.944), with minimal systematic bias. Mean model inference time was under 0.01 s per image, reflecting forward-pass model inference only and excluding image loading, resizing and post-processing. Conclusion This study presents the first automated segmentation framework for the PIMs in US. Built on established segmentation architectures with a Mix Transformer backbone, it enables accurate and reliable pixel-level segmentation in under 0.01 s per image; its novelty lies in extending automated musculoskeletal US analysis to this previously unaddressed muscle group. By automating tissue boundary detection at the pixel level, this framework advances US imaging beyond conventional manual measurement, enabling objective and scalable musculoskeletal assessment with reduced operator dependence at the segmentation stage. These findings establish the feasibility of accurate and reproducible PIM segmentation in healthy adults and provide the necessary foundation for subsequent validation in clinical populations.

title: Deep Learning-Enabled Automated B-mode Segmentation for Regional Cerebral Perfusion Assessment in Neonates Using Ultrafast Power Doppler.
abstract: Cerebral perfusion disturbances contribute to neonatal brain injury, and ultrafast power Doppler can quantify regional cerebral blood volume but relies on manual segmentation that limits clinical use. We developed and validated a U-Net model for automated regional brain segmentation on B-mode images derived from neonatal transfontanellar ultrafast ultrasound to enable rapid arterial and venous cerebral blood volume quantification. Time-integrated, log-compressed ultrafast B-mode images from 80 neonates were manually segmented by an expert into the cortico-sub-cortical areas, the cingulate gyrus and the basal ganglia, and then used to train a U-Net with class-weighted loss (a 70/15/15 train/validation/test split). The trained model was then applied to segment B-mode images, with the resulting regions of interest used to quantify arterial and venous cerebral blood volume from the corresponding power Doppler data. Segmentation performance was quantified using the Dice similarity coefficient, with agreement between artificial intelligence- and manually derived cerebral blood volume assessed by Bland-Altman analysis. The median Dice similarity coefficients were 83%, 84% and 88% for the three regions. Mean Bland-Altman differences were ≤0.103 dB (arterial) and ≤0.096 dB (venous). title: Automated Quantification of 3-D Carotid Ultrasound Vessel Wall Texture Change Predicts Vascular Events.
abstract: Objective To reduce reliance on labor-intensive and operator-dependent explicit plaque segmentation, we evaluated whether a texture-change score (ΔTexture) derived from semi-automated 3-D ultrasound (3-DUS) vessel wall segmentation predicts vascular events better than baseline vessel wall texture (BL-Texture), vessel wall volume change (ΔVWV) and Framingham risk score. Methods 3-DUS images were acquired from 272 patients with carotid atherosclerosis at baseline and 1 y later. Vessel walls were delineated using a validated, minimally user-initialized segmentation workflow. Longitudinal texture change was summarized as vessel wall ΔTexture and compared with BL-Texture, ΔVWV and Framingham risk score. Patients were followed for up to 5 y (median, 3.16 y) for myocardial infarction, transient ischemic attack and stroke. Results ΔTexture and BL-Texture predicted vascular events (log-rank, p < 0.001 for both), whereas ΔVWV did not. No event occurred in the lowest-risk tertile of ΔTexture. The area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of ΔTexture was 0.89, compared with 0.82 for BL-Texture, 0.53 for ΔVWV and 0.53 for Framingham risk score. In Cox regression, ΔTexture (median hazard ratio, 4.05; p < 0.001) and BL-Texture (median hazard ratio, 3.63; p < 0.001) were significant predictors, whereas ΔVWV and Framingham risk score were not. Conclusion Vessel wall ΔTexture derived from minimally user-initialized 3-DUS vessel wall segmentation predicted vascular events better than ΔVWV and Framingham risk score. This approach provides a scalable imaging biomarker for vascular event risk assessment without requiring explicit plaque segmentation.

title: Doppler-based Radiomics Integrated With Frozen Section Analysis Enhances Borderline Ovarian Tumor Prediction: A Multicenter Study.
abstract: Objective To develop a Doppler-based radiomics model that utilizes tumor characteristics related to neovascularization, with or without integrating intraoperative frozen section analysis (FSA), to enhance borderline ovarian tumors (BOT) prediction. Methods In this retrospective multicenter study, patients diagnosed with BOT or epithelial ovarian cancer (EOC) between January 2010 and October 2022 across five centers were included. Data from Center I were randomly divided into training (80%) and validation (20%) sets, while Centers II-V provided the test set. Three ultrasound-radiomics models were developed: color Doppler features (CD), grayscale features (GS), and combining both (GSCD). An Integration Model was developed by incorporating clinical variables, FSA and the best-performing radiomics model. Color Doppler signals were acquired through three channels with RGB information. Model performance was evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). Results A total of 1244 patients with a median age of 49 years (IQR, 37-58 years) were included, consisting of 520 patients with BOT and 724 EOC. The GSCD exhibited the best predictive performance for BOT among the three ultrasound-radiomics models, showing an AUC of 0.975 (95%CI, 0.962-0.985) in the training set, with a sensitivity of 92.9% and a specificity of 88.9% in the validation set. The Integration Model further improved the performance, achieving an AUC of 0.997 (95%CI, 0.993-0.998) in the training set, with a sensitivity of 87.2% and a specificity of 98.7% in the validation set. Additionally, both the GSCD and Integration Model effectively distinguished BOT from Stage I EOC, with AUCs of 0.919 (95% CI: 0.849-0.963) and 0.936 (95% CI: 0.871-0.974) in the validation set. Conclusion We developed a Doppler-based radiomics model utilizing red-green-blue information. This model, irrespective of integration with FSA, demonstrated improved accuracy in predicting BOT and stratified the FIGO Stage EOC.

title: Deep Learning-Driven Multimodal Integration of Ultrasound and CT for Identifying Central Lymph Node Metastasis in Papillary Thyroid Carcinoma.
abstract: Objective To evaluate the utility of multimodal imaging biomarkers in papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC), this study developed a deep learning model using ultrasound (US) and computed tomography (CT) imaging to predict central lymph node metastasis (CLNM) in PTC by integrating radiomic features of perivascular adipose tissue (PVAT) at the cervical vertebra 6 (C6) level. Methods We retrospectively analyzed 477 PTC patients from two centers. Using ResNet101 with Hierarchical Attention Integration (ResHAI-101), we extracted deep learning features of the tumor area from US images. Separately, we extracted radiomic features of PVAT from CT images. Univariate and multivariate analyses were conducted based on clinical data, followed by feature selection and integration. Results Multimodal prediction model performance was quantified by the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). Predictive performance was validated using an external test cohort (ETC). The Multimodal Prediction Model 3, integrating deep learning features, PVAT radiomic features and clinical features, showed superior diagnostic performance for predicting CLNM compared to the Unimodal Model, achieving AUCs of 0.915 in the internal test cohort and 0.890 in the ETC. Binary logistic regression identified gender, age, tumor size and extrathyroidal extension as independent risk factors for CLNM. Conclusion This study establishes and validates the significant impact of PVAT on CLNM in PTC, providing a non-invasive tool for pre-operative risk assessment to aid in surgical decision-making.

title: Ultrasound Localization Microscopy Combined With Regional Division for Differentiating Benign and Metastatic Lymph Nodes.
abstract: Objective Ultrasound Localization Microscopy (ULM) enables high-resolution visualization of lymph node microvasculature. However, most previous studies rely on whole-node analysis, which may overlook spatial heterogeneity and be affected by confounding factors. This prospective single-center study aimed to investigate the diagnostic value of ULM combined with regional analysis for differentiating benign and metastatic lymph nodes. Methods A total of 104 lymph nodes from patients with sonographically suspicious lymph nodes were included. All lymph nodes underwent ultrasound-guided core needle biopsy, which served as the reference standard for classification (benign or metastatic). Each lymph node was divided into central, peripheral, and global regions, and ULM quantitative parameters were extracted. Regional ratio features were calculated. Feature selection was performed using univariate analysis, LASSO regression, and backward stepwise logistic regression. Model performance was evaluated using 10-fold stratified cross-validation, 2000 bootstrap resamples, decision curve analysis (DCA), and clinical impact curve (CIC). Results Three diagnostic models were constructed: a conventional ultrasound (US) model, a ULM model, and a combined US-ULM model. The combined model demonstrated the best discriminative performance with an AUC of 0.866 (95% CI: 0.7875-0.9320), followed by the ULM model (AUC = 0.833, 95% CI: 0.7464-0.9108) and the US model (AUC = 0.730, 95% CI: 0.6219-0.8285). In multivariable analysis, SD.Density_C_P (OR =0.0578, p = 0.012), FD_C_P (OR = 0.8847 per 0.01 increase, p = 0.003), and peripheral vascular pattern (OR = 10.9501, p < 0.001) were identified as significant predictors of lymph node metastasis. At optimal cut-off values, the combined model achieved a sensitivity of 0.733 and specificity of 0.915. Conclusion The proposed region-based ULM model combined with conventional ultrasound provides an improved quantitative approach for differentiating benign and metastatic lymph nodes in patients with sonographically suspicious lymphadenopathy.
